institutions: Applied Technology College of Soochow University
all.abstract: Introduction Digital and environmental transformation increasingly converge in agri-food cold-chain logistics, yet how digital capabilities relate to frontline loss-prevention practices remains unclear. Drawing on the Twin Transition perspective, this study examined the associations among digital maturity, green human resource analytics (GHRA), employee green loss-prevention behavior, and supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. It also examined whether the association between GHRA and employee behavior varied with perceived algorithmic pressure. Methods This cross-sectional study analyzed matched questionnaire data from 96 supervisors and 545 employees across 96 Chinese agri-food cold-chain firms or departments. The primary analysis used a pooled single-level structural equation model. Sensitivity analyses used composite-score mixed models and unit-level cluster bootstrapping to assess the influence of clustering. Results Digital maturity was positively associated with GHRA, which in turn was positively associated with employee green loss-prevention behavior. This behavior was positively associated with supervisor-rated sustainable logistics performance. The direct association between GHRA and performance was statistically nonsignificant. Positive indirect estimates were consistent with the proposed pathways linking GHRA to performance through employee behavior and linking digital maturity to performance through GHRA and employee behavior in sequence. The positive association between GHRA and employee behavior was weaker at higher levels of perceived algorithmic pressure. The sensitivity analyses supported the overall pattern of associations. Discussion The findings extend the Twin Transition perspective by specifying how digital capability, analytics applied to green employee management, and frontline loss-prevention practices are linked in cold-chain operations. They also highlight the importance of how employees experience algorithmic oversight when organizations use analytics to support loss prevention.

all.title: Models for Sustainable Human Resource Management: Combining Ethics, CSR and Data-Driven HR Analytics
all.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
all.abstract: This research presents a conceptual framework for sustainable human resource management (HRM) that integrates ethical decision-making, corporate social responsibility (CSR), and data-driven HR analytics. It underscores the importance of sustainable HR practices in fostering long-term employee development, enhancing organizational resilience, and promoting adaptability in the current digital landscape. Ethical principles are emphasized as vital for creating transparent, fair, and inclusive workplaces, while CSR initiatives significantly contribute to increasing employee engagement and nurturing a mission-driven organizational culture. The paper further examines the role of HR analytics as an effective instrument for optimizing workforce planning, improving employee retention, and enhancing productivity. Proposed strategies aim to align HRM with broader sustainability goals by utilizing the interrelatedness of these components. The study concludes by providing practical recommendations for implementing this integrated model to build strong and sustainable organizations.

all.title: Context-Aware Workforce Analytics for Enhancing Creativity and Innovation in Hybrid Teams: A Talent Management Perspective
all.abstract: The way organizations collaborate, their employee engagement strategies and talent management mechanisms exhibited a major transformation as hybrid work environments set in. Workforce analytics has been adopting to support strategic organisational decision-making. However, past literature focus on context-aware workforce analytics that can enhance creativity and innovation in hybrid teams. This research looks at how workforce analytics, communication effectiveness, collaboration quality, employee autonomy, and innovation outcomes are interrelated in hybrid work environments. Using purposive sampling, primary data has been collected from 85 employees working in hybrid teams belonging to IT and service organizations Bangalore. The tools which were used were correlation analysis, regression analysis, t-test analysis, and Cronbach's alpha reliability analysis. The results show a high relationship between employee creativity and workforce analytics. The effectiveness of communication and the quality of collaboration contribute significantly to innovation outcomes. The conclusion suggests a shift towards more human-centered workforce analytics frameworks that can strengthen collaborative and innovative hybrid work cultures in organizations.

all.title: People analytics in employee performance management: A bibliometric mapping and structured content review
all.venue: Ho Chi Minh City Open University Journal of Science- Economics and Business Administration
institutions: Ho Chi Minh City University of Economics and Finance
Ho Chi Minh City Open University
all.abstract: People analytics is increasingly being used to measure, track and improve performance. The research in this area, however, is highly fragmented across disciplines and the results are mixed. This paper maps the thematic and intellectual structure of the field and synthesizes the evidence on the impact of people analytics on performance management. It combines a bibliometric analysis of the Scopus indexed literature with a structured content review of the full text studies. There has been a significant increase in the volume of publications over recent years with HR analytics, AI and HRM forming the core of the keyword network. Bibliographic coupling reveals four tentative theoretical streams emerging over time: from incentive economics to organizational capability, then to a more behavioral focus on fairness and finally to the more recent generative AI work which largely reuses the existing frameworks. The content review suggests that people analytics can improve measurement, prediction and feedback, but the extent of this is contingent upon the quality of the data, the design of the metrics, the presence of complementary management practices, the level of managerial support and employee trust. A number of the studies point to trade-offs between the quality and quantity of output and between the technical accuracy of the analytics and employee acceptance. The paper presents an integrative multi-level framework with testable propositions and sets out a research agenda which includes causal designs, multi-dimensional performance measures, employee voice, data governance, emerging economy contexts and human-AI collaboration.

all.title: Transformación de la toma de decisiones en la gestión del talento humano mediante People Analytics e inteligencia artificial: un modelo estratégico para organizaciones Panameñas
all.venue: Revista Multidisciplinar Epistemología de las Ciencias
all.abstract: Digital transformation has redefined Human Talent Management by incorporating analytical tools capable of converting large volumes of data into strategic information for decision-making. In this context, People Analytics and Artificial Intelligence represent key innovations for optimizing recruitment, selection, performance evaluation, talent retention, and workforce planning.This study aimed to analyze how the integration of these technologies transforms decision-making in Human Talent Management within Panamanian organizations and to propose a strategic analytical maturity model adapted to the national context. A qualitative research approach with descriptive, explanatory, and propositional scope was employed, supported by a systematic review of scientific literature, documentary analysis, and the conceptual design of the Panamanian People Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Maturity Model (MPM-PAIA). The findings indicate that organizations with greater analytical capabilities improve strategic decision-making, strengthen the efficiency of human resource processes, and enhance competitiveness. Data quality, leadership, organizational culture, analytical competencies, and ethical governance were identified as critical success factors. The study concludes that the progressive integration of People Analytics and Artificial Intelligence represents a strategic opportunity for Panamanian organizations, provided that technological adoption is accompanied by workforce development and ethical governance.

all.title: A comparative fuzzy MCDM framework for employee evaluation: Fuzzy TOPSIS versus Fuzzy AHP–TOPSIS on the IBM HR analytics dataset
all.venue: Journal of Electrical Systems and Information Technology
all.abstract: This study compares equal-weight Fuzzy TOPSIS with hybrid Fuzzy AHP–TOPSIS for multidimensional employee evaluation. Both models use the synthetic IBM HR Analytics dataset (1,470 employees) and the same seven criteria; only the weighting rule changes. Expert-derived weights were highest for Job Involvement (0.241140), Years in Current Role (0.200279), and Training Times Last Year (0.169016). The rankings were strongly associated (Spearman 0.904389; Kendall’s tau-b 0.738746), yet individual positions moved substantially (mean absolute shift 139.169; maximum 601.5). Top-10, Top-20, and Top-50 overlaps were 60%, 55%, and 66%. Fourteen employees shifted by more than 500 positions. Sensitivity analysis of both models, covering 56 weight perturbations, kept within-model Spearman correlations above 0.990. An alternative coding that preserves the numerical detail of two criteria left the global weighting contrast intact (Spearman 0.905428) while changing Top-10 membership. A secondary vertex-distance Fuzzy VIKOR ranking that used the same expert weights agreed more closely with hybrid TOPSIS (Spearman 0.898969) than with equal-weight TOPSIS (Spearman 0.718161). Because the dataset is synthetic, the rankings are a reproducible decision-support benchmark, not evidence about a real workforce.

all.title: From Employee Data to Strategic Decisions: A Conceptual Framework for Predictive People Analytics in Employee Attrition Management
all.abstract: Voluntary employee attrition poses substantial operational and financial challenges for modern organizations, incurring direct talent-replacement expenditures alongside indirect losses in institutional memory and productivity. This conceptual research paper examines the strategic role of People Analytics in predicting and managing employee turnover, charting the transition from reactive Human Resource (HR) reporting to forward-looking, evidence-based decision-making. Using a qualitative thematic synthesis of secondary literature, the study evaluates supervised machine learning (ML) architectures (Random Forest, XGBoost, Extra Trees, and Stacking Ensembles), key attrition predictors, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) frameworks (SHAP and LIME). The reviewed literature indicates that ensemble algorithms often achieve higher predictive accuracy than classical linear models across evaluated datasets, although comparative performance depends on individual dataset characteristics, model configurations, and validation procedures. Meanwhile, XAI methods address algorithmic opacity by decomposing risk scores into interpretable root causes. To connect risk forecasting with managerial action, the paper proposes an integrated five-stage conceptual decision-support framework, illustrating how HR professionals can translate explained risk profiles into targeted retention interventions while adhering to ethical governance principles, including data minimization, algorithmic bias auditing, meaningful human oversight, and compliance with the qualified automated-decision safeguards of Article 22 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Ultimately, the synthesis suggests that People Analytics strengthens Strategic Human Resource Management (SHRM) when predictive precision is balanced with managerial empathy, data privacy, and organizational justice. Keywords: People Analytics; HR Analytics; Predictive Modeling; Employee Attrition; Explainable AI (XAI); Strategic Human Resource Management (SHRM); Machine Learning; Workforce Planning.

all.title: AI-enabled talent analytics and workforce agility in manufacturing SMEs: the mediating role of human-AI collaboration and the moderating role of technostress resilience
all.abstract: Introduction Small and medium-sized enterprises increasingly use AI-enabled talent analytics (AITA) to support workforce planning and adaptive performance, yet the mechanisms linking AITA to workforce agility (WA) remain underexplored. This study examines human-AI collaboration (HAIC) as a mediating mechanism and technostress resilience (TR) as a psychological resource and boundary condition. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 334 owners, HR managers, and operations/production heads from Pakistani manufacturing SMEs actively using AITA. Exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modeling, 5,000 bootstrap resamples, and moderation analyses were used to assess the measurement and structural models. Results AITA was positively associated with WA, and HAIC showed a significant indirect association between AITA and WA, consistent with partial statistical mediation. TR was positively associated with WA and significantly strengthened the AITA-WA association. The exploratory TR x HAIC interaction was not statistically significant. Discussion The findings position AITA as a socio-technical work-design resource whose association with agility depends on human interpretation, collaborative routines, and psychological capacity to manage technology-related demands. Because the data are cross-sectional and based on one knowledgeable respondent per firm, the results should be interpreted as manager-perceived associations rather than causal effects.

all.title: Predictive People Analytics Using Machine Learning-Based HR Metrics for Strategic Workforce Planning in Industry 5.0
all.abstract: As Industry 5.0 can be introduced the nature of the relationship between human capital and intelligent technological systems fundamentally changed as the workforce is now at the core of the organization strategy. In this paper, the author puts forward a Predictive People Analytics (PPA) model, which embraces the HR metrics on machine learning (ML) to provide a strategic workforce planning that is supported by evidence. The suggested architecture transforms a data convergence of private data, including HR resource planning documents, IoT sensor streams, HR Information Systems (HRIS) and workforce survey devices, into one analytical data stream. Four ML models are also trained and aggregate to predict meaningful workforce results: employee turnover, mobility within the organization, performance curves, and succession preparedness: Random Forest, XGBoost, Deep Neural Networks (DNN), and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN). Transparency in high stakes HR is promoted through explainability through SHAP-based posthoc attribution. Empirical test on the IBM HR Analytics dataset and an augmented synthetic workforce panel shows that the ensemble model has the accuracy of 94.7, AUC-ROC of 0.971 and F1-score of 0.938 that are better than all of the baseline models and previous benchmarks. The results affirm that industry 5.0 people analytics enhanced by ML can assist in creating proactive, people-concentrated workforce in a noteworthy way.

all.title: People Analytics and Employee Retention: A Descriptive Study of Data-Driven Approaches to Understanding and Reducing Employee Turnover
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Employee retention is a strategic concern because departures can disrupt operations, weaken institutional knowledge, increase recruitment and training costs, and affect team morale. Traditional practices such as exit interviews, engagement surveys and retrospective turnover reports remain useful but may not identify emerging risks in time. People analytics combines workforce data, statistical analysis and, where appropriate, machine-learning techniques to support better HR decisions. This paper examines the contribution of people analytics to employee retention through a descriptive and conceptual review of the academic literature. It discusses turnover theories, workforce data, analytical methods, HR applications and the ethical conditions required for responsible implementation. It proposes a framework in which data quality and analytical capability support the identification of retention drivers, insights inform fair and targeted interventions, and evaluation supports continuous improvement. The review argues that predictive signals must be interpreted alongside organisational context and employee voice: a model may estimate resignation risk, but it cannot independently establish why an employee may leave or which intervention is appropriate. The paper therefore recommends a human-centred approach that combines descriptive, diagnostic and predictive analysis with managerial judgement, transparency, privacy safeguards and evaluation.

all.title: Performance Appraisal Fairness, Perceived Organisational Support, Employee Engagement and Human Resource Analytics: A Human-Centred Decision-Support Framework
all.venue: Journal of Engineering Management and Systems Engineering
all.abstract: This study develops a human-centred human resource (HR) decision-support framework integrating performance appraisal fairness, perceived organisational support (POS), employee engagement and workforce analytics. Drawing on the Social Exchange Theory, the conceptual component proposes that appraisal fairness and POS are positively associated with employee engagement and that POS may strengthen the positive relationship between appraisal fairness and engagement. These relationships are proposed rather than empirically tested because the secondary dataset does not contain validated measures of appraisal fairness or POS. However, an “Engagement Score” is available; its measurement provenance is undocumented. Accordingly, the analytics case is used to examine the sufficiency and governance limitations of administrative HR records rather than to test the proposed conceptual relationships. The illustrative analytics component uses the publicly available HR Analytics Dataset. The raw file contained 3,150 records and 39 variables; removal of 150 exact duplicate records resulted in a final analytical dataset of 3,000 observations. A target-leakage audit identified ExitDate, EmployeeStatus, TerminationType, TerminationDescription and exit-dependent tenure measures as inappropriate prospective predictors. Following their exclusion, a leakage-controlled Random Forest (RF) model showed essentially chance-level discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.507 and an area under the precision–recall curve (PR-AUC) of 0.528. Logistic regression produced similarly weak performance (ROC-AUC = 0.475). These findings demonstrate the importance of data provenance, temporal validity, leakage control, fairness assessment and human oversight when developing HR analytics systems. The study therefore contributes a theoretically grounded and systems-oriented framework for responsible workforce decision support while identifying direct empirical testing of the proposed moderation relationship as an important direction for future research.

all.title: SCIENTIFIC AND METHODOLOGICAL TOOLKIT FOR MANAGING THE HUMAN RESOURCE POTENTIAL OF SMART SPECIALISATION DOMAINS
all.venue: Facta Universitatis Series Economics and Organization
institutions: V. N. Karazin Kharkiv National University
all.abstract: The digital transformation of human capital management has intensified the need for integrated analytical tools that can support personnel decision-making within regional smart specialisation strategies. While international frameworks (the OECD Skills Strategy, ESCO, Skills Forecast, ISO 30414/30401) and a growing body of research on HR Analytics, People Analytics and digital HR management provide valuable partial solutions, most existing approaches remain functionally fragmented and are not integrated into a single methodological system aligned with the SMART-HR S3 approach. This paper aims to develop a scientific-methodological toolkit for managing the human resource (HR) potential of smart specialisation domains that provides comprehensive information-analytical support for managerial decision-making throughout the implementation of the SMART-HR S3 approach. Drawing on a synthesis of the international HR-management and regional innovation-policy literature, the study proposes a five-level architecture (conceptual, analytical, model, digital, managerial) and six functional components (methodological, model, indicator, algorithmic, digital, analytical) that integrate strategic-analysis methods, competency and forecasting models, a system of indicators, decision algorithms and digital HR platforms into a single decision-support cycle. The proposed toolkit and its accompanying operating mechanism allow public authorities, regional administrations, universities and research institutions to move from fragmented, tool-by-tool HR analytics towards a closed-loop process of assessment, forecasting, decision-making and monitoring. Future research should operationalise the framework through econometric models of integral HR-potential assessment and a dedicated SMART-HR S3 digital platform.

all.title: ‘Datafied' Employees in the Traditional Workplace
all.abstract: This chapter turns to the modern conventional workplace and examines the rise of algorithmic management and ‘people analytics’, arguing that these systems do more than increase the quantity of surveillance because they connect the recording of conduct much more directly to managerial evaluation and intervention. Digital systems can allocate work while monitoring its pace, after which the resulting data may inform rankings or anomaly detection and increasingly shape future opportunities through predictive profiling; in this sense, ordinary digital monitoring and algorithmic management remain analytically distinct even though they are frequently combined in practice. The chapter then considers ‘people analytics’ as a wider managerial rationality through which workers are translated into scored profiles and assessed in terms of risk, bringing the workplace closer to a developed form of the ‘panoptic’ project in which labour becomes continuously traceable and comparable so that observation can be translated into action, although this project can never be completed because labour-power remains embodied and situated rather than fully reducible to data.

all.title: A Phased Model for Digitalizing Human Resource Management in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face a practical challenge when digitalizing human resource management(HRM). They must decide which processes to digitalize first, how to allocate limited resources, and when to invest in more advanced capabilities. This article develops a phased model based on a conceptual synthesis of selected literature on SME digital transformation, electronic HRM, and HR analytics. The model comprises four phases: HR process assessment and standardization, employee record digitization, workflow automation and integration, and the use of HR data in managerial decisions. Each phase specifies its expected outputs and the conditions for moving to the next phase. The model treats data quality, employee adoption, and process ownership as prerequisites for expanding the scope of digitalization. Its main contribution is to translate these prerequisites into practical criteria that SMEs can use when making investment and implementation decisions. The model requires empirical validation across firms of different sizes and sectors.

all.title: Explainable AI for Fair and Transparent Human Resource Decision- Making
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Human resource (HR) decisions are currently supported by algorithmic processes for hiring, promotions, and retaining employees, the lack of transparency in these models raises concerns about fairness, accountability, and trust of employees towards the process. In this paper, we develop a two-channel explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that combines the post hoc explanation methods such as SHAP and LIME with the inherently interpretable classifier for HR decisions. In our methodology, adversarial debiasing is used in the training process to prevent the influence of sensitive attributes on the model performance. For testing the effectiveness of the proposed XAI model, we conduct an experimental evaluation using IBM HR analytics dataset with three HR decision making tasks including promotion prediction, attrition prediction, and candidate selection task. As results, we show that our model achieves reductions in demographic parity disparity without compromising the explanation quality using local accuracy and stability measures. Comparing with baseline models in terms of fairness-utility trade-off consistently yields improvements.

all.title: The role of Artificial Intelligence in human resource and public relations decision-making and legal accountability in the UAE
all.venue: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
all.abstract: The growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Human Resource (HR) management has completely changed the way decisions are made in organizations, especially in areas of recruitment, performance appraisal, and workforce planning. Although AI-based HR systems are expected to enhance efficiency, precision, and objectivity, they also raise significant concerns regarding legal accountability, equality, and compliance with employment regulations. This paper explores the application of Artificial Intelligence in human resource decision-making and its legal responsibilities within organizations based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The research design is quantitative, and the primary data will be collected from 400 respondents, including HR managers, senior managers, legal advisors, and compliance officers from public and private organizations in the UAE. The conceptualization of Artificial Intelligence in HR is multidimensional, encompassing AI-based recruitment and selection, AI-based performance evaluation, predictive HR analytics, and the automation of HR decision-making. The dependent variable is the quality of HR decision-making, assessed by decision accuracy, decision speed, fairness and objectivity, and risk reduction. The data are analyzed using SmartPLS, employing descriptive statistics, reliability and correlation analyses, and regression to test the proposed relationships. The results will show that AI-based HR practices positively impact the quality of HR decision-making, and that these effects are contingent on effective legal accountability practices, such as transparency, regulatory compliance, and human oversight. This research paper contributes to the literature by integrating technological, managerial, and legal perspectives. It provides practical guidance to organizations and policymakers seeking to balance AI-based innovation with legal and ethical accountability in the UAE labor market.

all.title: Empowering Women In The Workplace: The Role Of Strategic Human Resource Management In Inclusive Organizational Growth
all.venue: International Conference on Health Science, Green Economics, Educational Review and Technology
authors: R. RATHI DEVI MBA, M. Phil, Ph.D.  MSW, M.SC (PSY)
all.abstract: Women’s workplace empowerment has become an indispensable dimension of organizational legitimacy, human-capital optimization, and sustainable growth. Yet persistent disparities in employment access, managerial progression, compensation, care responsibilities, and executive influence expose the limitations of conventional diversity interventions. This article examines how strategic human resource management (SHRM) can transform gender inclusion from an aspirational corporate value into an operationally measurable institutional capability. Adopting a critical, integrative review of academic scholarship and secondary evidence from the World Economic Forum, World Bank, International Labour Organization, and McKinsey–LeanIn.Org, it evaluates gender-responsive recruitment, equitable reward architectures, career sponsorship, flexible work, leadership accountability, and people analytics. Recent findings demonstrate that global gender parity remains incomplete and that organizational advancement pathways reproduce gendered exclusion. The article proposes an integrated framework connecting structural diagnosis, policy redesign, managerial accountability, and outcome evaluation. It concludes that sustained empowerment requires redistributing organizational opportunity, authority, recognition, and resources—not merely increasing numerical representation.

all.title: Green Human Resource Management: Sustainability and the Employment Relationship
all.abstract: This chapter examines the opportunities and tensions involved in embedding green human resource management (HRM) in diverse organizational contexts. It highlights how cultural and institutional conditions shape the possibilities and limits of green HRM practices. The chapter first considers the role of HR professionals in leading corporate sustainability, emphasizing their strategic and operational influence on workforce engagement with ecological goals. It then reviews core green HRM practices through the ability-motivation-opportunity (AMO) framework. Drawing on pluralist perspectives, it shows how green HRM bundles are shaped by power, trust, and employee voice across the employee life cycle. The chapter argues that green HRM is embedded in the contested employment relationship and that its effectiveness depends on fairness, employee involvement, and commitment to the common good. Environmental sustainability in the workplace thus becomes a negotiated terrain, where future research and practice should explore how HR can foster more just and sustainable organizational transformations.

all.title: The Role of Digitalization in the Transformation of Human Resource Management
all.venue: International Journal of Social Science Research and Review
all.abstract: Digitalization has revolutionized the way organizations manage human resources, shifting from traditional practices to automated, data-driven approaches. This study aims to examine the impact of digital technologies on recruitment, training, and performance evaluation, highlighting the advantages and challenges associated with this transformation. The methodology includes a theoretical analysis of existing literature and a review of practical cases from international contexts. The findings reveal that digitalization provides numerous benefits, including increased efficiency, improved employee experiences, and enhanced decision-making capabilities through data analytics. However, challenges such as high implementation costs, lack of technological skills, and data security concerns persist. The paper concludes by recommending that organizations implement training programs to develop the digital skills of their workforce, invest in technologies that adhere to privacy standards, and focus on integrating digital systems that support their long-term human resource management strategies. These measures are essential to fully leverage the potential of digitalization in an increasingly technology-dependent world.

all.title: Impact of Employment Laws on Human Resource Management Practices
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Employment laws shape human resource management (HRM) by defining employee rights, employer responsibilities and minimum workplace standards. They influence recruitment, wages, working hours, leave, workplace equality, safety, social security, discipline and termination. This review examines the relationship between employment legislation and HRM, with particular reference to India. Drawing on established literature and eight related management studies, it finds that legal compliance can promote fairness, transparency and organisational accountability. However, complex regulations, uneven implementation, limited resources and low employee awareness can create difficulties, especially for small businesses. The paper argues that HR departments should integrate legal compliance into everyday workforce planning and decision-making.

all.title: Human Resource Management: Core Functions, Trends & Topics
all.abstract: Discover the fundamentals of Human Resource Management (HRM), including recruitment, employee engagement, performance management, workplace diversity, training, and organisational development. This presentation explores essential HR concepts, modern workplace challenges, emerging industry trends, and important research areas for university students. HR Assignment Help provides valuable academic guidance for understanding complex HRM theories, exploring relevant case studies, and developing effective assignment-writing skills. Learn how human resource practices influence employee productivity, organisational performance, and workplace culture while gaining insights into contemporary HR strategies and management practices.

all.title: Views of Bank Employees on E-HRM Practices in Mysore District
all.abstract: The success of an organization depends on the effectiveness of its HR personnel. The ability, skills, knowledge, etc. of employees can be used repeatedly through human resource management of an organization. The study is based on the process of management that manages and develops human beings, which is an essential part of human resources. The use of Information Technology(IT) to manage personnel information and create human resources (HR) procedures, such as role analysis, hiring, selection, training, performance management, and compensation, is known as Electronic Human Resource Management (E-HRM). The process and transmission of digital human resource data, or e-HRM, makes it simple for employers and employees to communicate.

all.title: HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, EMPLOYEE WELFARE, AND INDUSTRIAL STABILITY IN NIGERIA: A QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS
all.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between HRM practices, employee welfare, and industrial stability in Nigeria, with a focus on how workplace policies shape employee wellbeing and labour relations. This is with the specific objectives to: explore how human resource management practices are perceived and experienced in relation to employee welfare within Nigerian organizations; examine the role of employee welfare in shaping workplace relations and industrial stability in the Nigerian work environment; and investigate the organizational and institutional factors influencing the implementation of employee welfare policies in Nigeria. The study adopted a qualitative research design and an exploratory–descriptive approach. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, and document analysis involving HR managers, employees, labour union representatives, and organizational administrators in selected organizations in Lagos State, Nigeria. Thematic analysis was used to identify and interpret recurring patterns relating to HRM practices, employee welfare provisions, and industrial relations outcomes. Findings indicate that effective HRM practices particularly in recruitment, training, compensation, performance management, and employee relations contribute positively to employee welfare and workplace harmony. Organizations with strong welfare systems tend to experience higher employee commitment, improved motivation, and reduced industrial conflict. Conversely, poor welfare implementation, delayed salaries, weak communication systems, and adverse economic conditions were found to contribute significantly to industrial unrest and declining employee morale. The study concludes that industrial stability in Nigeria is largely dependent on the effectiveness of HRM systems and the extent to which organizations prioritize employee welfare. Strengthening institutional frameworks, improving communication, and ensuring fair and consistent welfare practices are essential for promoting sustainable labour relations and organizational stability. It was then recommended that government should strengthen labour laws, enhance enforcement institutions, and ensure strict compliance with labour standards to promote worker welfare, fairness, and sustained industrial peace and productivity in the country.

all.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Human Resource Management in the Modern Scenario
all.abstract: In current scenario many of the organizations are investing huge money for the development of AI Tool so that better decisions can be made and also the performance of employee can be improvised. In the modern scenario, AI-driven tools are increasingly used for recruiting the new employee for the organization, training, performance evaluation, and involving many psychometric test for improvising the engagement level of the employee. Most of the AI Tools will always improvise the efficiency of the process and making the practices to be more effective. This paper infer the exploration of AI Tools in the field of HR either positive or negative, challenges, and the future implications of AI in HRM. The study highlights how AI contributes to strategic HR practices while also addressing ethical concerns and limitations.

all.title: Beyond Green Rhetoric: How Human Resource Management Bridges Strategy and Sustainability in Hotels
all.abstract: Drawing on the natural resource‐based view (NRBV) and social cognitive theory (SCT), this study examines the relationships among strategic green intentions, green human resource management (Green HRM) practices, sustainable business performance and employee outcomes in Ghana's hospitality industry. Two independent quantitative studies were conducted in star‐rated hotels. Study 1 surveyed 282 managers and supervisors to examine Green HRM practices as mediating mechanisms linking strategic green intentions to economic, social and environmental performance. Study 2 surveyed 302 frontline employees to investigate employee green commitment as a mediator of the relationships between Green HRM practices and employee green behaviour and turnover intention. Data were analysed using a disjoint two‐stage PLS‐SEM approach. Study 1 revealed that strategic green intentions were directly associated with social performance but not with economic or environmental performance. Green HRM practices exhibited significant positive indirect effects across all three performance dimensions, with indirect‐only mediation for economic and environmental performance and complementary mediation for social performance. Study 2 demonstrated that employee green commitment significantly mediated the positive relationship between Green HRM practices and employee green behaviour. However, neither Green HRM practices nor employee green commitment was significantly associated with turnover intention, and the corresponding indirect effect was nonsignificant. The findings refine NRBV and SCT‐informed explanations by demonstrating differentiated relationships between environmental strategic intentions and sustainability performance, while highlighting the outcome‐specific relevance of employee green commitment. Practically, the research underscores the importance of embedding environmental priorities in credible Green HRM practices while recognising that broader employment outcomes may require complementary employee‐support strategies.

all.title: Human Resource Management Practices and Employee Outcomes: Evidence from the Albanian Private Sector
institutions: Ministry of Health and Social Protection
all.abstract: Human resource management (HRM) practices can shape employees’ experiences and contribute to organizational effectiveness, particularly in transitional economies. This study examines the relationships between three HRM practices—recruitment and selection, training and development, and rewards and recognition—and employee-level outcomes in private-sector organizations in Albania. Drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the Ability–Motivation–Opportunity (AMO) framework, the study uses questionnaire data from 65 non-managerial employees working in private companies with more than 50 employees. Separate simple linear regression models were used to examine associations between individual HRM practice items and employee outcomes, including motivation, engagement, retention, and ability. The reported results indicate positive and statistically significant associations for several items across these outcomes. Rewards and recognition show particularly consistent associations, while recruitment and selection and training and development are also significantly associated with a number of outcomes. Because the study relies on a small, employee-level sample and does not directly measure organizational performance, the findings should be interpreted as evidence about perceived employee outcomes rather than as proof of effects on firm-level performance. The study adds context-specific evidence from the Albanian private sector and identifies areas for further research using larger samples and direct organizational performance measures.

all.title: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AGILE HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND SMES PERFORMANCE IN KATSINA
all.abstract: This study examined the relationship between Agile Human Resource Management and SMEs performance in Katsina State, Nigeria. Specifically, the study investigated the relationship between agile talent management, agile employee engagement, and SMEs performance. A correlational research design was adopted. The population comprised 337 registered manufacturing SMEs in Katsina State as identified by the 2025 SMEDAN and NBS survey. The sample size of 180 was determine using Cochran 1977 formula for finite population. Structured questionnaires were administered to owners and managers of the SMEs within the State, of which 172 valid responses were used for analysis. Data were analyzed using Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed a strong and statistically significant positive relationship between agile talent management and SMEs performance (r = 0.763, p < 0.01). The study also found a strong and statistically significant positive relationship between agile employee engagement and SMEs performance (r = 0.790, p < 0.01). The results indicate that SMEs that adopt flexible talent management practices and foster employee participation, continuous feedback, collaboration, and adaptability tend to achieve higher levels of organizational performance. The study concludes that agile human resource management is a critical strategic capability that enhances the performance and sustainability of SMEs operating in dynamic business environments. The study recommends among other things that SME managers should institutionalize agile talent management practices through continuous employee development, flexible recruitment, and adaptive performance management systems. The study contributes to knowledge by providing empirical evidence on the role of agile human resource management in enhancing SME performance within the context of Katsina State, Nigeria.

all.title: THE IMPACT OF AI BASED HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ON LEADERSHIP PERFORMANCE IN HEALTHCARE
all.abstract: This study investigates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based Human Resource Management (HRM) on leadership performance within the Saudi Arabian healthcare sector, specifically within the context of the National Transformation Program and Vision 2030. Grounded in Socio-Technical Systems (STS) Theory, the research addresses a critical gap concerning how algorithmic administrative tools affect the behavioral and operational outcomes of mid-to-senior level healthcare leaders. Employing a positivist, deductive quantitative approach, a cross-sectional survey was administered to clinical and administrative leaders at Qassim University. The findings reveal a strong positive relationship between the adoption of AI-based HRM tools and enhanced leadership effectiveness. The research demonstrates that AI functions—such as predictive staffing and automated analytics—significantly reduce administrative burdens on healthcare leaders. This reduction facilitates a shift toward "Augmented Leadership," allowing managers to delegate routine quantitative tasks to algorithms and redirect their cognitive resources toward qualitative, human-centric responsibilities like empathy and conflict resolution. Furthermore, while certain demographic factors did not alter perceptions of these tools, the study noted that cultural background plays a role in how technology is embraced within the hospital ecosystem. Ultimately, the study concludes that achieving sustainable operational excellence requires a synergy of digital literacy and high emotional intelligence, alongside strict "algorithmic transparency" to maintain staff trust and prevent digital resentment.

all.title: Indonesian Human Resource Management Challenges Amid Digital Transformation And Post-Pandemic Recovery
all.abstract: Digital transformation and post-pandemic recovery have made contemporary challenges in human resource management (HRM) concern not only technological adaptation but also the psychological meaning of organizational practices. This study explores contemporary HRM practices and the challenges of implementing them, as perceived by 243 human resources (HR) leaders across industries in Indonesia, using Perceived Organizational Support (POS) as an interpretive lens. A qualitative descriptive design was used; data were collected through an open-ended online questionnaire and analyzed with Braun and Clarke’s thematic analysis. Seven interrelated themes emerged: leadership and top management support, talent acquisition and internal placement, employee well-being, compensation and benefits, generational differences, organizational culture, and knowledge management and adaptive learning. These themes reflect the perceptions of HR leaders. Rather than identifying entirely new HRM challenges, the findings illustrate how HR leaders perceive established HRM concerns as increasingly interconnected within the context of digital transformation and post-pandemic organizational adjustment. By employing POS as an interpretive lens, the study highlights the potential psychological significance of these organizational challenges without assuming that employees' perceptions of organizational support were directly measured.

all.title: Reward Systems and Organizational Justice in Human Resource Management: Implications for Employee Performance
all.abstract: Reward systems are important human resource management practices for recognizing employee contributions and supporting organizational performance. However, their effectiveness may depend not only on the rewards provided but also on employees' perceptions of organizational justice. This article examines the relationship between reward systems, organizational justice, motivation, employee loyalty, and performance through a narrative literature review of eight journal articles published between 2022 and 2026. The reviewed literature was analyzed using expectancy theory, equity theory, organizational justice theory, and social exchange theory. The findings generally indicate positive associations between reward systems and employee motivation, loyalty, and performance. However, the evidence is not entirely consistent. In particular, a study involving 51 hospital nurses found that the association between rewards and performance was no longer statistically significant in multivariate analysis (p = 0.731). Qualitative findings further indicate that perceived unfairness and unclear reward criteria may generate jealousy, conflict, and reduced employee trust. The synthesis suggests that organizational justice may play an important role in shaping employees' responses to reward practices, while performance is also associated with other factors, including leadership, competencies, and the work environment. Accordingly, organizations should establish transparent and measurable reward criteria, provide complaint mechanisms, and integrate reward policies with competency development and supportive leadership. The proposed relationships provide a basis for further empirical investigation

all.title: Human Resource Management Practices and Academic Staff Retention in Rivers State Universities.
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This study examined the relationship between Human Resource Management Practices and Academic Staff Retention in Rivers State Universities. The specific objectives were to determine the relationship between compensation and rewards, training and development, career development, and performance appraisal on academic staff retention. A correlational research design was adopted for the study. The population consisted of 160 lecturers from the Departments of Educational Management and Business Education in Rivers State University and Ignatius Ajuru University of Education. The entire population was used as the sample size, while 133 copies of the questionnaire were retrieved and used for analysis, representing an 83.1% response rate. The instrument used for data collection was a structured questionnaire divided into two sections titled Human Resource Management Practices Questionnaire and Academic Staff Retention Questionnaire. The instruments were structured on a four-point Likert scale of Strongly Agree (SA), Agree (A), Disagree (D), and Strongly Disagree (SD), designed to capture respondents’ perceptions on the extent of relationship between the study variables. The instrument was validated by 3 experts and tested for reliability using Cronbach’s Alpha, which yielded a coefficient of 0.71 and 0.87. Data were analyzed using Pearson Product Moment Correlation Coefficient and hypotheses were tested using t-transformation at 0.05 level of significance. The findings revealed that compensation and rewards (r = .72; t = 12.64), training and development (r = .65; t = 10.87), career development (r = .70; t = 11.92), and performance appraisal (r = .60; t = 9.76) all had significant positive relationships with academic staff retention. The study concluded that effective human resource management practices significantly enhance academic staff retention in Rivers State universities. Based on the findings, it was recommended that university management should improve compensation packages, strengthen training and development programmes, provide clear career advancement opportunities, and ensure fair performance appraisal systems to enhance academic staff retention.

all.title: Human Resource Management and the Development of Islamic Work Ethic at Pesantren Business Center
all.venue: Journal of Economics Law and Humanities
institutions: Universitas Islam Negeri Kiai Ageng Muhammad Besari Ponorogo
all.abstract: Background/Introduction: University business units rooted in the Indonesian Islamic boarding school (pesantren) tradition manage operational staffing needs while upholding institutional values. Research Objectives: This study examines how workforce planning, recruitment and selection, and employee development support the formation of an Islamic work ethic at UNIDA Business Center Ponorogo. Methodology: The study used a qualitative case study design. Data from in-depth interviews, direct observation, and document review were analyzed inductively and compared through triangulation. Results: Unit heads and managers identified staffing needs based on operational requirements. Selection considered technical competence and character, and interviews explored how applicants would apply Islamic values in the workplace. Employee development combined job skills and professional conduct with Islamic study sessions, Qur’an recitation instruction, and congregational prayer. The study also identified difficulties with workplace discipline and the delivery of a program scheduled every two weeks. Unique Contribution: The study brings workforce planning, selection, and employee development into a single account of how a pesantren-based university business unit manages its workforce and communicates ethical expectations.. Conclusion: Recruitment and employee development were the clearest ways the business unit introduced and reinforced expectations for an Islamic work ethic. Recommendations: Future research should follow employees over time to examine how they apply these expectations and investigate the reported difficulties with discipline and program delivery.

all.title: Beyond Employee Engagement: The Role Of Strategic Human Resource Management In Building A Sustainable And High-Performance Workforce In Msmes, Tamil Nadu, India
all.abstract: The growing complexity of the business environment has transformed human resource management from a predominantly administrative function into a strategic organizational capability. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), particularly in developing economies such as India, face significant challenges relating to employee retention, skill development, workforce adaptability, employee well-being, and organizational performance. These challenges highlight the need to move beyond conventional employee engagement initiatives towards an integrated approach to Strategic Human Resource Management (SHRM). This study examines the role of strategic human resource management in building a sustainable and high-performance workforce in MSMEs in Tamil Nadu, India. Specifically, it investigates the relationships between strategic HRM practices, employee engagement, training and development, performance management, employee well-being, workforce sustainability, and organizational performance. Drawing on the Resource-Based View, Social Exchange Theory, Human Capital Theory, and the Ability-Motivation-Opportunity framework, the study proposes an integrated conceptual model explaining how HR practices can contribute to sustainable workforce outcomes. The empirical investigation adopts a quantitative research approach using structured questionnaires administered to employees working in selected MSMEs in Tamil Nadu. The proposed analytical framework includes descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation, multiple regression, and mediation analysis, subject to the suitability of the collected data. Employee engagement is examined as a potential mediating mechanism linking strategic HRM practices with workforce and organizational outcomes. The study seeks to contribute to strategic HRM literature by contextualizing sustainable workforce development within the operational realities of MSMEs. Its practical implications concern affordable talent management, employee participation, skill development, workplace well-being, and retention-oriented HR policies. The empirical findings and statistical conclusions will be incorporated after verification of the collected survey dataset.

all.title: The effects of HRM practices on organizational performance: The moderating role of workplace safety in Bangladesh’s garment industry
all.abstract: This study attempted to examine how Human Resource Management (HRM) practices affect the organizational performance of Bangladesh's garment industry. The moderating effects of workplace safety on the relationship between HRM practices and organizational performance were also investigated. To achieve better organizational performance, four factors have been selected in the Bangladeshi context and, more specifically, in the garment industry of Bangladesh. 400 human resource managers from several Bangladeshi garment industries took part in this study. PLS-SEM was employed in analyzing the data. It was found that recruitment and selection, training and development, performance evaluation, and rewards and benefits have a substantial influence on organizational performance in the Bangladesh Garment Industry. The results revealed that workplace safety has a significant moderating influence on the relationship between human resource management practices and organizational performance. It will help the garment factory owners and HR managers to follow the ideal and standard procedures for the recruitment and selection process, an appropriate environment and adequate arrangements for training and development, effective means and procedures to evaluate employee performance, and gratify employees and workers for their excellent performance in their respective jobs and trades. This study provides a framework and references for future HRM research on Bangladesh’s garment industry and organizational performance. It highlights workplace safety’s role in linking HRM practices, recruitment, training, appraisal, and rewards- to organizational performance, contributing valuable insights into HRM dynamics and practices that can guide future academic and industry research.

all.title: Responsible AI in human resource management: a sustainable framework for employee trust and organisational performance
all.venue: Journal of Organizational Effectiveness People and Performance
institutions: Asia Pacific University of Technology & Innovation
all.abstract: Purpose This paper examines how responsible artificial intelligence (AI) governance in human resource management (HRM) may support employee trust and sustainable organisational performance. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual model, developed through purposive theoretical synthesis, connects employee-visible governance with justice, focal trust, employee responses and organisational outcomes, while specifying contextual conditions and learning feedback. Findings The framework proposes that employee-visible responsible AI governance informs justice perceptions, which inform trust in organisationally governed AI-enabled HRM decision processes. Trust may support calibrated reliance and constructive responses; individual performance and collective emergence may then contribute to sustainable organisational performance. Socio-technical alignment, contextual conditions and organisational learning delimit this pathway. The six governance dimensions and twelve propositions are conceptual and have not been empirically validated. Practical implications The conceptually derived guidance links accountable decision ownership, meaningful human review, accessible explanation and appeal, and lifecycle learning to employee experience. Originality/value The framework specifies an employment-system unit of analysis and distinguishes technical trustworthiness from employee trust. Its bounded contribution connects employee-visible governance with justice-mediated trust, cross-level emergence and governance reconfiguration.

all.title: Green Human Resource Management and Environmentally Friendly Behavior of Employees in Iraq's Ministry of Environment
all.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), expressed through green recruitment, green training, green performance appraisal, and green rewards, relates to and influences the environmentally friendly behavior of employees at the Ministry of Environment in Baghdad, Iraq. Methodology: A descriptive analytical design was used. A questionnaire built on a five point Likert scale was distributed electronically to a convenience sample of 110 employees, and 98 questionnaires were returned. Validity was checked with Pearson item correlations, reliability with Cronbach's alpha, and the hypotheses were tested with Pearson correlation and simple linear regression in SPSS version 27. Results: All four GHRM dimensions were rated highly, with green performance appraisal ranked first. GHRM correlated strongly and positively with environmentally friendly behavior (r=0.673) and had a significant effect on it (B=0.752, F=77.079, R²=0.453). Green training and green rewards were the strongest individual dimensions. Conclusions: Green HR practices, particularly training and rewards, give the ministry a practical way to steer employees toward greener behavior at work. Limitations: The study relied on a single public organization, a small convenience sample, cross sectional self reported data, and bivariate analysis. Contributions: The study adds evidence from an Iraqi public sector setting, where GHRM research is still scarce, and offers managers concrete steps such as environmentally oriented job descriptions and incentives for employees who propose ways to reduce waste.

all.title: Human resource management practices for ethical AI governance and their links to perceived ethical AI implementation and employee well-being
all.abstract: The swift emergence and adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) at workplaces have created unparalleled opportunities for organizational agility and competitiveness. However, these opportunities have also been accompanied by numerous ethical issues that arise due to deploying AI at work, such as fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and employee well-being. This study focuses on exploring human resource management (HRM) practices influence on ethical AI governance and how ethical AI governance impacts Perceived Ethical AI Implementation, trust in AI, employee well-being, and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) workplace outcomes. The study introduces and tests a structural model grounded in socio-technical systems theory and social exchange theory. Using a cross-sectional study design, the data were collected from 457 employees working in information technology workplaces in Hyderabad, India. The Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) approach was used to analyze the study data with IBM AMOS 28 software. The study results revealed that HRM practices for ethical AI governance significantly predict Perceived Ethical AI Implementation and employees trust in AI. Employees Perceived Ethical AI Implementation and trust in AI positively predict employees well-being, and employee well-being is positively associated with SDG workplace outcomes. Employees trust in AI partially mediates the relationship between HRM practices for ethical AI governance and employee well-being. This study makes several contributions to the limited literature on ethical AI governance by theoretically integrating and empirically testing several vital concepts like HRM practices, employee well-being, trust in AI, Perceived Ethical AI Implementation, and sustainability outcomes within one framework. Practically, this study’s results can help managers and policymakers understand how to engage in responsible AI governance that facilitates desirable employee experiences at work.

all.title: The Challenges in Implementing Talent Management to Fill Bureaucratic Positions
all.abstract: Talent management has become a strategic approach for strengthening merit-based public administration by ensuring that bureaucratic appointments are based on competence, performance, and integrity rather than political considerations. However, its implementation in local governments continues to face institutional and political challenges. This study aims to examine the implementation of talent management in the Governments of West Java Province, Bandung City, and Bogor City, which have formally adopted merit systems and received excellent institutional assessments. The study uses the theories of Public Administration, Human Resource Management, the Merit System, and the Boston Consulting Group Talent Management Model, which emphasizes talent planning, identification, development, placement, and retention. A qualitative descriptive case study approach was employed using document analysis, media reports, institutional observations, and in-depth interviews with key stakeholders. The findings indicate that although digitalization, competency mapping, and employee development have been implemented, talent management has not functioned as a fully merit-based governance system because political intervention, patronage networks, and transactional appointment practices continue to influence strategic personnel decisions. The study demonstrates that strong administrative compliance with talent management does not necessarily translate into substantive merit-based governance, as patronage, political intervention, and transactional appointments remain persistent challenges. These findings underscore the need to strengthen transparency, independent oversight, and competency-based appointment mechanisms to safeguard the integrity of talent management. The study concludes that these governance reforms are essential for developing a professional, accountable, and politically neutral bureaucracy.

all.title: Coaching and Mentoring as Succession Planning Tools: An Integrative Review with Implications for Ghanaian Organizations
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This paper examines the role of coaching and mentoring as strategic tools for succession planning and leadership development through an integrative review of relevant theoretical perspectives and existing empirical literature. It explores how structured coaching and mentoring interventions contribute to leadership capacity development, knowledge transfer, talent identification, employee development, and the preparation of potential successors for critical organizational positions. The paper reviews the conceptual foundations of coaching, mentoring, and succession planning, highlighting their interconnected roles in building leadership pipelines, strengthening organizational capabilities, preserving institutional knowledge, and ensuring leadership continuity. It further examines the benefits, challenges, and organizational conditions that influence the successful integration of coaching and mentoring into succession planning frameworks. With particular attention to Ghanaian organizations, the paper considers the implications of coaching and mentoring for human resource management, talent management, leadership development, organizational sustainability, and institutional effectiveness. It discusses how organizations in Ghana can leverage structured coaching and mentoring programmes to identify, develop, and retain high-potential employees while preparing them to assume future leadership and managerial responsibilities. The paper contributes to management and human resource development literature by integrating insights on coaching, mentoring, and succession planning within an organizational development perspective. It offers practical considerations for organizational leaders, human resource professionals, management consultants, policymakers, and academics seeking to strengthen succession planning practices and develop sustainable leadership pipelines in Ghanaian organizations. It also highlights opportunities for further empirical research on the effectiveness of coaching and mentoring interventions in succession planning within the Ghanaian organizational context.

all.title: Talent Management Practices and Performance of the State Department for Roads in Kenya
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
institutions: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology
all.abstract: The State Department for Roads plays a critical role in Kenya's socio-economic development by overseeing the construction, maintenance and management of the national road network. However, the Department faces major performance challenges, including stalled projects and delays in project delivery. This study sought to establish the effect of talent management practices on the performance of the State Department for Roads in Kenya. Specifically, the study sought to determine the effect of talent development and of talent engagement on the performance of the Department. The study was guided by Human Capital Theory and Self-Determination Theory and adopted a descriptive research design. The target population comprised 620 management employees of the Department, from whom a sample of 243 was determined using the Yamane formula. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire, and 216 questionnaires were returned, a response rate of 88.9%. The data were analysed using SPSS version 26 through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. The respondents agreed that the Department implements talent development (M = 3.772) and talent engagement (M = 3.798) practices. The study concludes that talent development (Beta = 0.378, p < 0.001) and talent engagement (Beta = 0.385, p < 0.001) each have a positive and significant effect on the performance of the State Department for Roads in Kenya. The study recommends that the management of the Department should strengthen talent development through continuous training, mentorship and career development programmes aligned with employees' skills gaps and the Department's strategic objectives. The management should also enhance talent engagement by promoting employee participation in decision-making, effective communication and recognition of employee contributions. Keywords: Talent Management Practices, Talent Development, Talent Engagement, Organizational Performance, State Department for Roads

all.title: How remote work reshapes talent acquisition and innovation: evidence from U.S. listed firms
institutions: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade
all.abstract: This paper examines how work-from-home (WFH) policies shape firms’ talent acquisition and innovation performance. While prior research has treated remote work as an employee benefit affecting individual productivity and retention, we conceptualise WFH as a firm-level strategic capability for overcoming geographic labour market frictions. Drawing on human capital theory, we argue that acquiring skilled talent beyond local labour markets is a key channel through which remote work enhances innovation. Using difference-in-differences with propensity score matching on a panel of U.S. listed firms, we find that firms with higher WFH feasibility achieved significant gains in talent acquisition quality following the widespread shift to remote work. This relationship is strengthened by organisational flexibility and concentrated in industries where geographic constraints were previously binding. Talent acquisition, in turn, partially mediates the effect of WFH on innovation.

all.title: Workforce diversity and employee performance: Talent management and innovation as strategic catalysts
all.abstract: This systematic literature review (SLR) synthesizes contemporary research by examining the relationship between workforce diversity and employee performance. This review also aims to synthesize the current literature to examine how talent management and innovation act as strategic catalysts, transforming workforce diversity into measurable organizational excellence. This review integrates four complementary analytical approaches using a structured and rigorous design. First, a systematic search and screening process guided by the PRISMA framework identified relevant studies published between 2010 and 2025 from Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and major academic publishers. Second, descriptive and trend analyses were performed to examine publication growth, geographic distribution, journal quality, and dominant research context. Third, thematic analysis identified recurring themes, theoretical perspectives, and conceptual linkages between workforce diversity, talent management, workplace innovation, and employee performance. Finally, a content analysis synthesized the empirical findings to clarify the mediating and contextual mechanisms across the selected studies. Following the PRISMA process, 42 high-quality empirical and conceptual articles were included in the final review. The findings revealed a steady growth in diversity-performance research since 2010, with a significant shift after 2015 from direct effects models toward mechanism-based explanations. In general, workforce diversity rarely has a direct effect on employee performance; instead, its effect is largely indirect and dependent on supportive organizational practices. Inclusive and strategic talent management mediates this relationship by enabling the equitable recruitment, development, and retention of diverse human resources, whereas workplace innovation facilitates the effective utilization of heterogeneous knowledge through participatory, adaptive, and learning-oriented work practices. This review identifies the resource-based view, social exchange theory, and sociotechnical systems theory as dominant theoretical foundations explaining how workforce diversity becomes a performance-enhancing resource when supported by appropriate managerial capabilities, leadership behaviors, and organizational systems. Despite these advances, important gaps remain, including limited integration of diversity, talent management, and workplace innovation within a single framework, overreliance on cross-sectional designs, and insufficient evidence from developing economies and vocational or educational contexts. This review proposes an integrated conceptual perspective to guide future research and organizational practice.

all.title: Advanced Predictive Approaches to Talent Management Employee Retention Productivity and Career Growth
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Today’s workforce calls for a pro-active approach towards talent management beyond the existing reactive approach. This paper develops an integrated predictive model based on deep learning and graphical architectures that will model employee retention probability, productivity dynamics, and career trajectory in parallel. In contrast to the current practice of dealing with each of these aspects separately, the methodology introduced in the paper is based on sequential HRIS data and relational networks to derive insights for talent management. The model utilizes the LSTM-Attention mechanism to predict retention probability and GNN for personalized career planning, making it possible to predict retention, optimize productivity, and plan career development in parallel. Comparative analysis of the models’ performance shows that an integrated architecture outperforms separate machine learning models in terms of modeling interactions between retention, productivity, and growth outcomes.

all.title: Emotional Intelligence and HR Leadership Effectiveness: A Conceptual Review of Employee Engagement and Talent Management
all.abstract: Emotional intelligence is one of the most important predictors of leadership performance in the modern human resource management, especially enhancing employee engagement and talent retention. Although the research on emotional intelligence, leadership effectiveness, employee engagement and talent management has been discussed separately in previous studies, there is still a lack of an integrated conceptual knowledge, particularly on a comparative Indian and international basis. In filling this gap, the paper puts forward a conceptual review that is theoretically informed and synthesizes existing literature to explore the part played by emotional intelligence in improving the effectiveness of the HR leader. Based on Goleman mixed model of emotional intelligence, Social Exchange Theory and Transformational Leadership Theory the review presents employee engagement as a result of emotional intelligent leadership as well as a mediating process between the leadership effectiveness and the talent management results including development and retention. The research hypothesizes a conceptual model of integration that brings out the strategic role of emotional intelligence in HR leadership in the cross-cultural contexts. This review related to leadership and HRM literature by integrating fragmented knowledge and provides a basis on which empirical research can be undertaken in the future.

all.title: AI Driven Talent Management and the Performance of Agri Based Enterprises in Central Region Cameroon
all.venue: Journal of Economics Management Entrepreneurship and Business (JEMEB)
all.abstract: Purpose: This study examines the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) driven talent management practices and the performance of agri based enterprises in the Central Region of Cameroon, focusing on the mediating roles of workforce productivity and employee resilience. Research Methodology: A quantitative cross sectional survey design was employed, targeting 250 managers and human resource professionals. Data were collected with a structured questionnaire and analyzed with SPSS and AMOS through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and mediation analysis with 5.000 bootstrap resamples. Results: AI driven talent management was positively and significantly related to enterprise performance (r=0.523, p<0.01). Workforce productivity (β=0.18) and employee resilience (β=0.14) significantly mediated this relationship. Both the total indirect effect (β=0.32, p<0.01) and the direct effect (β=0.29, p<0.01) were significant, indicating partial mediation, with about 52 percent of the total effect transmitted through the two mediators. Conclusions: AI driven talent management enhances the performance of agri based enterprises both directly and indirectly through improved workforce productivity and stronger employee resilience. Enterprises should integrate AI strategically into talent management and support employees through change management. Limitations: The cross sectional design, self reported data, purposive sampling, and focus on a single region limit causal inference and generalizability. Contributions: The study provides empirical evidence from an underresearched African agricultural context and clarifies the mechanisms through which AI driven talent management translates into enterprise performance.

all.title: Workforce Sustainability Risk in A High-Retention it Infrastructure Services Firm: a Knowledge Management and Succession Planning Perspective
all.venue: Journal of Economics and Business UBS
all.abstract: High employee retention is generally regarded as an indicator of organizational health; however, in knowledge-intensive firms, it may conceal increasing workforce continuity risks. This study examined how high employee retention and limited workforce regeneration coexisted within the maintenance and services department of an Indonesian information technology (IT) infrastructure services firm, how this imbalance affected knowledge continuity, and what organizational measures could mitigate the associated risks. A qualitative single-case study design was employed, involving semi-structured interviews with 14 informants representing field engineers, IT specialists, and functional managers. The data were examined using framework-based thematic analysis.
