The findings identified four interrelated contributing conditions: structural recruitment constraints, an organizational culture emphasizing employee loyalty, reliance on internal mobility as a substitute for workforce regeneration, and the absence of a formal strategic workforce planning function. These conditions contributed to knowledge concentration, succession planning gaps, and operational vulnerability. The study also identified dependence on individual client relationships as an emerging risk factor, whereby client trust concentrated in specific employees constrained staffing decisions, complicated succession efforts through resistance to personnel replacements, and potentially transformed workforce continuity risks into revenue-related vulnerabilities. Although these risks were recognized across organizational levels, no dedicated function assumed clear accountability for managing them. The findings highlighted workforce governance as a critical mechanism for addressing these challenges. Accordingly, the study proposed a three-horizon workforce sustainability strategy informed by the Asian Productivity Organization (APO) Knowledge Management Framework, supported by a permanent strategic workforce planning function and clearly defined workforce continuity indicators.

all.title: Leader–Follower Dynamics in Leadership Succession Planning: A Study of Three Faith-Based Nonprofit Organizations in Georgia
all.abstract: Leadership succession planning (LSP) strategically identifies and prepares employees and followers for key roles through leader–follower dynamics: interaction, mutual influence, shared responsibility, and common goals. Beyond filling vacancies, LSP maintains continuity whenever experienced members resign, retire, or change roles; develops internal talent; supports employee growth and performance; and aligns leadership development with long-term goals. LSP supports adaptability, competitiveness, and mission stability as leadership changes. The study examined biblical integration and godly principles in LSP, drawing on the Bible’s many examples of leader-follower relationships. This qualitative phenomenological study, supported by methodological triangulation, investigates leadership succession planning (LSP) effectiveness in three Georgia faith-based nonprofits. Three executive participants represented a social services and homelessness organization, a denominational ministerial association, and a youth-focused community agency. Questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and archival documents provided the data.

all.title: Analysis of the Role of Talent Management in Improving Employee Competency Quality at Statistics Indonesia (BPS) of Nias Regency
all.abstract: This study examined the role of talent management in supporting employee competency development at the Statistics Indonesia (BPS) Office of Nias Regency. The study employed a qualitative descriptive approach involving five informants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews, non-participant observation, and documentation and were analyzed through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing. Data trustworthiness was strengthened through source and technique triangulation and member checking. The findings showed that talent management was implemented through employee potential identification, training, seminars, workshops, education and training programs, performance management, functional career development, recognition of high-performing employees, and leadership support. These practices were associated with the development of employees’ technical, managerial, and socio-cultural competencies, as well as their ability to adapt to technological change and engage in continuous learning. The findings also revealed that competency development depended not only on formal organizational programs but also on leadership support, learning opportunities, alignment between competencies and job requirements, organizational learning culture, employee willingness to learn, adaptability, and proactive mindset. However, facilities, technological infrastructure, motivation, and employee readiness for change still required improvement. The study concluded that talent management functioned as an organizational process that supported competency development through the interaction between organizational practices and employees’ active involvement in continuous learning and development.

all.title: Talent management, knowledge management, and transformational leadership: Associations with perceived retention conditions in an Indonesian regional government agency
all.venue: The Contrarian Finance Accounting and Business Research
all.abstract: Employee retention is a concern for public agencies whose work requires specialized technical competence, and the Regional Financial and Asset Agency (BKAD) of North Sulawesi Province, Indonesia, has experienced a decline in headcount retention that is concentrated among employees on government work agreements (PPPK). This study examines how perceived talent management, knowledge management, and transformational leadership are associated with perceived retention conditions among current employees. A cross-sectional survey was administered to all 116 eligible staff, comprising civil servants and PPPK employees, and the data were analyzed using multiple linear regression complemented by confidence intervals, robust standard errors, and dominance analysis. The results show that employees who rate each of the three practices more favorably also report more favorable retention conditions, and that the three practices jointly account for a substantial share of the variation in these conditions. However, the practices cannot be ranked with confidence, and the association for talent management is the least robust. Because only employees who stayed were surveyed, the outcome overlaps conceptually with two predictors, and all data come from a single source, the findings describe associations and do not explain why employees left. The study suggests that career development, knowledge sharing, and supervisory leadership should be monitored together, and that future research should complement perception data with exit records and intention-to-stay measures.

all.title: The Impact of Talent Management on Achieving Sustainable Employee Performance in Public Service Institutions: An Applied Study at the Amarah Municipality Directorate
all.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effect of talent management on sustainable employee performance in the employees of the Amarah Municipality Directorate. It used the descriptive-analytical approach with quantitative research design and the sample was 320 employees taken from a study population of 1,881 employees. The findings showed that the level of availability of talent management practices is high in four dimensions, namely critical position identification, competence training, development and reward management. They also indicated that the employees had a high level of sustainable employee performance. In addition, the statistical analysis revealed that a positive and statistically significant relationship exists between the dimensions of talent management and sustainable employee performance, where there were differences in the extent of contribution of the dimensions. Competence training was the dimension that contributed the most to explaining sustainable employee performance, followed by development, reward management and finally identification of critical positions. The study concludes that talent management is an important managerial strategy in improving employees' proficiency in achieving work objectives efficiently and consistently. This can be done by identifying critical positions, building competencies, improving professional skills and offering adequate reward and recognition systems, which can contribute to sustain performance and keep employees in a satisfactory condition of well-being, in public service institutions.

all.title: Brain Drain and National Talent Management in Indonesia: An Islamic Human Resource Economics Analysis Based on Maqasid al-Shariah
all.abstract: The phenomenon of brain drain, or the migration of highly skilled workers, represents a strategic challenge for Indonesia in optimizing its human resources and responding to global competition. The migration of academics, researchers, professionals, and highly educated individuals may reduce national innovation capacity when it is not balanced by talent development and knowledge transfer mechanisms. This study aims to analyze brain drain and national talent management strategies in Indonesia through the perspective of Islamic Human Resource Economics based on Maqāṣid Syariah. This research employs a qualitative approach using library research through the analysis of open-access journal articles, institutional reports, and relevant government regulations. The findings indicate that addressing brain drain requires improvements in working environments, equal opportunities, competency development, diaspora collaboration, and the integration of Maqāṣid Syariah principles to promote individual and societal welfare.

all.title: Pengaruh Talent Management dan Employee Engagement Terhadap Kompetensi Digital Karyawan di Era Transformasi Digital pada PT.ISS INDONESIA
all.venue: Journal of Business Economics and Management
all.abstract: Digital transformation requires organizations to strengthen their employees’ competencies to adapt to technological advancements and changing workplace demands. In this context, human resource management plays a strategic role in developing employees’ capabilities and ensuring organizational readiness for digital change. This study aims to analyze the effects of Talent Management and Employee Engagement on Employees’ Digital Competence at PT ISS Indonesia, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative approach with an associative research design will be employed. Primary data will be collected through questionnaires distributed to selected employees of PT ISS Indonesia based on predetermined sampling criteria. All variables will be measured using a five-point Likert scale, with Talent Management (X1) and Employee Engagement (X2) as the independent variables and Employees’ Digital Competence (Y) as the dependent variable. The data will be analyzed using validity and reliability tests, relevant classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, partial significance tests (t-tests), simultaneous significance tests (F-tests), and the coefficient of determination. This study is expected to provide empirical evidence regarding the contribution of talent management practices and employee engagement to employees’ digital competence. Furthermore, the findings are expected to provide practical insights for PT ISS Indonesia in designing talent development initiatives, strengthening employee engagement, and improving employees’ digital capabilities to support work effectiveness and sustainable organizational performance amid ongoing digital transformation.

all.title: The Effect of Talent Management on Human Resource Performance Moderated by Human Resource Audit at The Public Works and Spatial Planning Office of Central Kalimantan Province
all.abstract: Talent management in the public sector is a strategic factor influencing the effectiveness and efficiency of public service delivery. Government institutions face challenges related to talent mismatches, particularly gaps between employees' existing competencies and organizational requirements, which complicate the recruitment and retention of qualified personnel, especially when the private sector offers more competitive compensation and career development opportunities. Previous studies have reported inconsistent findings regarding the relationship between talent management and employee performance, while empirical evidence concerning the role of human resource (HR) audits remains inconclusive. These inconsistencies highlight the need to examine HR audits as a moderating variable. This study aimed to examine (1) the effect of talent management on HR performance and (2) the moderating role of HR audits in this relationship. Employing an explanatory research design, data were collected through structured, closed-ended questionnaires administered to 164 of the 167 targeted employees at the Public Works and Spatial Planning Office (Dinas Pekerjaan Umum dan Penataan Ruang, DPUPR) of Central Kalimantan Province, selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings revealed that talent management had a positive and statistically significant effect on HR performance (β = 0.498; t = 4.860; p < 0.001), with career management emerging as the most influential indicator. HR audits significantly strengthened the relationship between talent management and HR performance (interaction coefficient = 0.426; t = 4.059; p < 0.001) and demonstrated a positive and statistically significant direct effect on HR performance (β = 0.332; t = 2.684; p = 0.007). The model explained 57.3% of the variance in HR performance (R² = 0.573) and demonstrated predictive relevance (Q² = 0.473). These findings indicated that effective talent management was positively associated with HR performance and that HR audits strengthened this relationship. Accordingly, the institution was encouraged to improve career management practices and conduct regular HR audits to enhance employee performance. Future research should incorporate additional explanatory variables and extend the investigation to other government institutions to improve the generalizability of the findings.

all.title: The Rise of Multi-Agent AI in Strategic Human Resource Management: Exploring How Collaborative AI Agents Transform Talent Management, Workforce Coordination, and HR Decision Authority
all.venue: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
all.abstract: This study examined how professionals in Pakistan understood the role of collaborative artificial intelligence (AI) agents in talent management, workforce coordination and HR decision authority. Guided by Socio-Technical Systems Theory and Organizational Information Processing Theory, the study used reflexive thematic analysis to interpret 20 online interviews with HR, operations and technology professionals. Six themes captured participants’ accounts of recruitment, career development, workforce planning, decision authority, procedural fairness and organizational readiness. Participants located a critical point of recruiter oversight at initial screening, when historical hiring preferences could exclude qualified applicants before human review. In development and scheduling, they identified employee aspirations, skills and personal circumstances as information that could change an otherwise plausible recommendation. They assigned responsibility for pay adjustments to compensation committees and staffing reductions to executives. Across functions, participants connected fairness with understandable reasons and access to a reviewer empowered to correct an outcome. The findings show that, in participants’ judgments, the value of collaborative agents depends on whether decision owners can inspect underlying evidence, exercise judgment and intervene when recommendations affect employment opportunities. all.title: Understanding the Mediating Role of Talent Retention in SMEs' Sustainability Practices
all.abstract: Digital transformation and institutional regulation do not consistently translate into more sustainable practices in small‐ and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs). This study, which is grounded in the resource‐based view (RBV) and draws on institutional theory (IT) and talent management theory (TMT), emphasizes talent retention as a theoretically central mediating mechanism that links external institutional and digital drivers with embedded sustainability practices. Applying PLS‐SEM to survey data from 253 SMEs in La Rioja (Spain), our findings reveal no significant direct effects of digital management intensity or the social and regulatory framework on sustainability. However, both of these variables have an indirect effect on sustainability via talent retention. Our results suggest that regulatory and digital drivers are more likely to be effective when supported by a stable “Green Pillar” of human capital that can internalize these external stimuli. By positioning talent retention as the core conduit through which external digital and institutional pressures are converted into sustainable practices in SMEs, the study advances TMT, adds to the Digital Green Twin Transition debate, and offers practical implications for aligning talent management strategies in SMEs with digital and institutional policies.

all.title: Research on the Integrated Development of Talent Attraction and Cultivation in Higher Education Institutions from the Perspective of Simultaneous Attraction and Cultivation
all.venue: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
institutions: North China University of Science and Technology
all.abstract: Talent is the primary resource; the recruitment of talent by universities is a key measure for attracting high-end intellectual resources and supporting discipline development and scientific and technological innovation. In the new era, the recruitment of university talent not only carries the strategic mission of building a country strong in education and science and technology, but also faces practical challenges, including increasingly fierce competition, high costs, and inadequate coordination between recruitment and talent development. On the basis of elucidating the value and significance of university talent recruitment in the new era, this paper analyzes the primary issues currently present and proposes pathways for optimization by adhering to the Party's leadership over talent management, improving evaluation mechanisms, promoting both recruitment and talent development, and strengthening institutional frameworks and standards; the aim is to provide a reference for enhancing the quality and effectiveness of university talent recruitment.

all.title: An Intelligent Framework for Automated Recruitment Filtering and Skill Gap Analytics via Vector Space Model
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The rapid digitization of talent acquisition has resulted in a high volume of unstructured job applications, creating severe screening bottlenecks for human resource teams. Conventional Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) rely heavily on opaque Boolean keyword filters that lack transparency and offer no diagnostic feedback to job seekers. This study presents An Intelligent Framework for Automated Recruitment Filtering and Skill Gap Analytics via Vector Space Model, an interactive web-based architecture developed using Python and Streamlit. The proposed system standardizes multi-format document ingestion (PDF and DOCX), extracts technical competencies via boundary-safe regular expression lookarounds, and computes a quantitative compatibility score using Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) weighting and Cosine Similarity within a Vector Space Model (VSM). Furthermore, the framework executes set-theoretic skill gap analytics to partition required competencies into matched strengths and missing qualifications. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate that the framework processes document pairs in under 350 milliseconds, eliminates false negatives on symbolic technical terms (such as C++ and CI/CD ), and suppresses boilerplate score inflation through TF-IDF stop-word filtering. Ultimately, this transparent, low-latency architecture enhances initial candidate shortlisting efficiency for recruiters while providing actionable upskilling insights for applicants.

all.title: AI Powered Recruitment Portal Using Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning
all.venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
all.abstract: Recruitment teams routinely receive more applications than they can screen manually, and job seekers find it hard to locate roles that fit their skills.This paper combines a literature review with the design of an AI Powered Recruitment Portal.Four recent studies on artificial intelligence enabled talent sourcing, natural language processing based resume screening, resume to job matching and automated campus placement management are reviewed and compared.The review shows that existing work relies largely on keyword comparison, struggles with varied resume formats, offers limited skill gap analysis, explains its scores poorly and gives recruiters little control over automated outcomes.To address these gaps, the paper proposes a web platform for candidates, recruiters and administrators, organised into eight modules and built on a React frontend, a Java Spring Boot backend, a centralized MySQL database and an artificial intelligence and natural language processing engine that extracts resume features, matches them with job requirements, scores and ranks candidates and generates recommendations, while the recruiter takes the final decision.Random Forest and Logistic Regression are proposed for suitability scoring.The paper separates proposed components from components verified as implemented.It reports no accuracy figures because no experimental results were available at the time of writing, and it gives an evaluation plan instead.

all.title: A hybrid data-driven framework integrating machine learning and multi-criteria decision making for recruitment
all.venue: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
all.abstract: Context—Recruitment has become a multidimensional decision-making process in which organizations must evaluate both qualitative and quantitative candidate attributes simultaneously. While machine iearning (ML) methods are effective for predicting recruitment outcomes and Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) techniques provide structured ranking mechanisms, these approaches are commonly applied independently. As a result, the advantages of predictive analytics and expert-based evaluation are not fully utilized within a unified decision-support processObjective—This study proposes a hybrid decision-support framework that integrates ML and MCDM techniques to improve personnel selection. The framework is designed to combine data-driven prediction with systematic multi-criteria evaluation, while also examining the relative importance of recruitment criteria and the consistency of alternative ranking methods.Method—The proposed methodology consists of two sequential stages. First, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting Tree algorithms are developed using a publicly available recruitment dataset, and their predictive performances are comparatively evaluated to identify the most suitable model. The predicted hiring probabilities are then used to shortlist the most promising candidates. In the second stage, these candidates are evaluated using an integrated MCDM framework. Criterion weights are determined through the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), whereas candidate rankings are generated using TOPSIS, ELECTRE, and VIKOR. Finally, Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient is employed to examine the degree of agreement among the rankings obtained from the different MCDM methods.Results—Among the evaluated ML algorithms, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Tree demonstrated closely comparable predictive performance. Gradient Boosting Tree was retained for candidate screening because it achieved slightly higher recall, F1-score, and test ROC–AUC. The integration of predicted hiring probabilities into the MCDM stage enabled a more focused evaluation of shortlisted candidates. TOPSIS, ELECTRE, and VIKOR consistently identified the same highest-ranked candidate, although varying degrees of agreement were observed across the remaining candidate rankings. Furthermore, the AHP results identified Interview (0.5031) and Personality (0.2316) as the most influential criteria, followed by Education (0.1481), Skill (0.0755), and Experience (0.0417).Conclusion—The proposed hybrid framework effectively combines predictive modeling with multi-criteria evaluation in a unified decision-support environment. By linking ML predictions with transparent ranking techniques, the framework improves the reliability and interpretability of recruitment decisions. Owing to its flexible structure, the proposed approach can be adapted to various industrial engineering applications and other decision-making problems involving multiple evaluation criteria.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Green Recruitment Practices and Their Impact on Employee Engagement and Retention: An Empirical Study of Sustainable Human Resource Management
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Green Recruitment Practices and its impact on employee engagement and retention. Integrating AI with Green Human Resource Management enables organizations to digitize recruitment, reduce paper consumption, minimize unnecessary travel, improve candidate screening and matching, and communicate sustainability-oriented employment values. AI can support candidate sourcing, resume screening, virtual assessments, interview scheduling, candidate communication and recruitment analytics. However, organizations must also address concerns relating to fairness, transparency, privacy, algorithmic bias and excessive automation. Following the structure of the supplied model paper, the present study adopts a quantitative approach using a structured questionnaire and an illustrative sample of 300 respondents. Frequency analysis, Chi-square, ANOVA, correlation, and multiple regression are used to examine the relationships among AI-enabled green recruitment practices, employee engagement, and retention. The illustrative findings indicate significant associations between AI-enabled green recruitment and employee engagement and retention intention. Fairness and transparency, perceived environmental responsibility and employee engagement also emerge as important factors associated with retention. The study recommends human oversight, transparent AI governance, monitoring of algorithmic bias, responsible data management, digital, paperless recruitment, and alignment between recruitment promises and actual green organizational practices. The study concludes that AI can strengthen Green Recruitment Practices and contribute to employee engagement and retention when technological efficiency is combined with authentic sustainability and responsible HR management.

all.title: AI Literacy and Ethical Voice in Algorithmic Hiring: The Mediating Role of Psychological Safety and Moral Efficacy
all.abstract: Responsible human resource management (HRM) relies on human oversight, which works only when people are willing to question problematic algorithmic outputs. Based on social cognitive theory and psychological safety theory, this study investigates whether there is a direct link between AI literacy and the ethical voice in algorithms for hiring, as well as whether there is an indirect link through psychological safety and moral efficacy. Data of the survey in the form of information was collected from 390 employees who were engaged in recruitment and selection process in four multinational companies in Pakistan (purposive sampling; 470 questionnaires were distributed). The regression and bootstrap analyses revealed that the variables of psychological safety (B = 0.31) and moral efficacy (B = 0.37) had a positive relationship with AI literacy, while the direct path from ethical voice to AI literacy showed a stronger effect (total effect B = 0.44, p < .001). Psychological safety and moral efficacy both predicted ethical voice, and there was an indirect relationship between psychological safety and moral efficacy. Indirect effects made up approximately 42% of the overall effect, and there were significant indirect paths via psychological safety, via moral efficacy, and sequentially via both psychological safety and moral efficacy, in addition to a significant direct path (complementary partial mediation). AI-literacy training in combination with a safe reporting climate and high moral efficacy might therefore be most likely to help supervise ethical use. Data are cross-sectional in nature and self-reported, so the results are interpreted in terms of associations.

all.title: Responsible AI in Recruitment: Balancing Predictive Accuracy, Algorithmic Fairness and Human Oversight in Indian SMEs
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics are reshaping recruitment through faster applicant screening, candidate matching and data-driven hiring. However, their adoption raises a question: how can organizations balance predictive accuracy and operational efficiency with algorithmic fairness and meaningful human oversight? This conceptual paper examines this challenge among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in India, where resource constraints, digital infrastructure gaps and reliance on third-party recruitment software complicate responsible AI governance. Drawing on secondary literature in business analytics, strategic human resource management, socio-technical systems and organizational justice, the paper synthesizes three themes: the operational potential of AI-driven recruitment analytics; ethical risks such as historical and proxy-based algorithmic bias, limited transparency and data privacy; and governance mechanisms that preserve human accountability. It examines Explainable AI (XAI), including SHAP and LIME, alongside Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) oversight, fairness audits, data protection and vendor due diligence. The analysis indicates that predictive accuracy alone is insufficient to establish the legitimacy of AI-supported hiring. Algorithms may reproduce inequalities, while opaque recommendations can weaken procedural justice and encourage overreliance on automated outputs. Human judgment remains important, particularly when assessing soft skills and cultural fit. The paper proposes a Responsible AI Governance Framework tailored to Indian SMEs, structured around operational, tactical and strategic safeguards. It argues that vendor assessment, explain ability and active recruiter oversight can help SMEs improve recruitment efficiency while supporting fair, transparent and inclusive selection. As a conceptual study based on secondary sources, the framework offers propositions for future empirical testing rather than empirically validated causal findings.

all.title: Proposal Preprint_Validating the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Scale in the Philippine Workforce
all.abstract: Proposal Preprint_Validating the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Scale in the Philippine WorkforceResearch proposal; empirical data collection and analysis pending.AbstractThis research proposal outlines an initial psychometric validation of the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Scale (AISES) in the Philippine workforce context. Although AISES has been developed and evaluated in other populations, the applicability of its established measurement structure to workers with a substantive Philippine work nexus remains to be empirically examined. The proposed study will employ a quantitative, nonexperimental, cross-sectional design involving a minimum of 220 eligible workers recruited through nonprobability sampling. The original 22-item AISES, comprising four dimensions—Assistance, Anthropomorphic Interaction, Comfort with AI, and Technological Skills—will be evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis with robust maximum-likelihood estimation. Cronbach’s alpha will subsequently assess internal consistency for dimensions demonstrating adequate structural support. The study seeks to generate initial context-specific psychometric evidence that may inform the appropriate use of AISES in Philippine workforce research and organizational diagnostic applications. Findings will be interpreted within the study’s methodological and sampling limitations.Keywords: Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Scale, AISES, psychometric validation, confirmatory factor analysis, internal consistency, Philippine workforce

all.title: A Study on the Effectiveness of Digital Recruitment Tools in Improving Recruitment Efficiency and Candidate Management
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Recruitment is an essential Human Resource Management function through which organisations attract, identify and evaluate candidates for vacant positions. The increasing use of online job portals, professional networking platforms, applicant tracking systems, digital communication, virtual interviews and data-management tools has changed the way recruitment activities are performed. This study examines the effectiveness of digital recruitment tools in improving recruitment efficiency and candidate management, with practical context drawn from an HR internship at Peoplezone Consultants Pvt. Ltd., Jaipur. The study is descriptive and exploratory in nature and is based on secondary research, published literature and conceptual analysis. It does not use a survey, interview dataset or confidential organisational records. The discussion considers the potential contribution of digital tools to candidate sourcing, application screening, interview coordination, recruitment tracking, communication and record maintenance. It also evaluates limitations such as inconsistent data, technology dependence, privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, accessibility and the need for human judgement. The review indicates that digital tools can support speed, process visibility, record organisation and communication consistency, but technology alone cannot ensure quality hiring. Their usefulness depends on clear job criteria, reliable data, trained users, candidate-centred communication, privacy safeguards and human oversight. The study recommends a balanced approach in which digital tools support recruiters throughout the hiring workflow while final decisions remain accountable and contextual.

all.title: Data Science Job Profiles Classifiers Using Machine Learning
all.venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
all.abstract: This research examines the power of various professional competencies and industry characteristics within the Data Science job market to classify profiles in Barcelona and Madrid. We utilized human resource classification criteria and Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Decision Trees, XGBoost, and CatBoost as classification algorithms to identify key variables that drive model interpretability and performance. These variables include education, experience, personal attributes such as adaptability and continuous learning, English level, specific insights, teamwork, and external stakeholders' interactions. Our analysis reveals that soft skills, industry experience, and educational background—particularly English proficiency—are the primary determinants of job market classification, guiding stakeholders in talent development and optimizing recruitment strategy. This study focuses on the variables essential to the classification models, thereby contributing to a more sophisticated understanding of job market dynamics. Specifically, we highlight the synergy between professional skills and industry context as the primary driver of market identity in Barcelona and Madrid. This synergy is crucial for individuals and organizations striving for excellence in the competitive landscapes of Barcelona and Madrid. To situate the method for large‐scale analysis, we also examine the classifiers as parallel and distributed workloads, benchmarking their scaling with corpus size and their multi‐core speedup and efficiency.

all.title: Employer Perceptions of AI-Generated Cover Letters: Detection, Trust, and Hiring Decisions
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has fundamentally disrupted the labor market's traditional signaling mechanisms. Cover letters, long conceptualized as costly signals of candidate conscientiousness, motivation, and organizational fit, can now be synthesized in seconds. This paper provides experimental evidence on how corporate recruiters perceive, detect, and penalize AI-generated cover letters. Utilizing a pre-registered 2 × 4 factorial experiment with 360 verified corporate hiring managers and human resource professionals evaluating 2,160 application dossiers, we orthogonally manipulate actual authorship (human-authored, generic zero-shot LLM, and contextually grounded career-engine AI) and disclosure status (double-blind, disclosed AI assistance, disclosed human authorship, and commercial AI-detector flags).Keywords:Our empirical findings yield three core insights. First, we identify a profound "Detection Illusion": in blind evaluations, experienced recruiters distinguish AI-generated cover letters from human-written ones with only 52.8% accuracy—statistically indistinguishable from random chance (p = 0.312). Commercial AI detectors perform equally unreliably in professional job search domains, exhibiting a 24.6% false-positive rate on human documents. Second, blind ratings reveal quality parity: AI cover letters equal or surpass human baselines in structural coherence (+0.42 SD) and grammatical fluency (+0.58 SD). Third, when AI generation is disclosed or algorithmically flagged, candidates suffer a severe "AI Stigma Penalty": recruiter willingness to grant an interview plunges by 17.6 percentage points (p < 0.001), mediated predominantly by a 28.4% collapse in perceived applicant effort. Crucially, contextually grounded AI architectures—exemplified by Offerum's resume-anchored career engine (offerum.work)—mitigate this effort deflation by integrating verifiable achievements and role-specific nuances, recovering 70.5% of lost hiring intent. We discuss regulatory implications regarding mandatory AI disclosure policies and automated surveillance tools in recruitment.

all.title: The impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on employee green well-being: The mediating role of employee engagement in Vietnamese enterprises
all.venue: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
institutions: Industrial University of Ho Chi Minh City
all.abstract: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into workplaces is transforming not only how employees perform their tasks but also how they experience work. However, the implications of this transformation for sustainable development remain insufficiently understood, particularly regarding whether AI-enabled workplaces can support employees’ long-term well-being and resilience. Addressing this gap, this study examines how positive attitudes toward Generative AI (POS_ATT) and responsible AI signals (RAIS) contribute to multidimensional Green Well-being through employee engagement (ENG). Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model, Signaling Theory, and the Job Demands–Resources theory, Green Well-being is conceptualized as a sustainable state encompassing emotional (GEW), cognitive (GCW), and social well-being (GSW). A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 342 knowledge workers employed by Vietnamese organizations using Generative AI. Participants were recruited using convenience and snowball sampling. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. The results show that both POS_ATT (β = 0.312, p < 0.001) and RAIS (β = 0.287, p < 0.001) are positively associated with employee engagement. ENG, in turn, is positively associated with all three dimensions of Green Well-being, with the strongest relationship observed for emotional well-being (β = 0.441), followed by cognitive (β = 0.418) and social well-being (β = 0.397), all at p < 0.001. Moreover, ENG fully mediates the relationships between POS_ATT and RAIS and the three Green Well-being dimensions. These findings broaden understanding of sustainable development in AI-enabled workplaces by showing that the potential human benefits of Generative AI are not associated solely with technology adoption. Rather, favorable employee perceptions and responsible implementation need to be translated into meaningful work engagement before they are associated with sustainable well-being outcomes. The study therefore identifies responsible AI, employee engagement, and multidimensional well-being as interconnected elements of a human-centered approach to sustainable digital transformation. Practically, organizations should complement investments in AI capabilities with transparent, explainable, and fair AI governance and engagement-oriented work design to preserve and develop human resources during digital transformation. Because the cross-sectional design captures relationships at a single point in time, the findings establish associations rather than causal effects. Longitudinal and cross-national research is therefore needed to examine whether these relationships persist over time and contribute to long-term employee and organizational resilience. Keywords: Generative artificial intelligence; responsible AI; employee engagement; Green Well-being; sustainable development; sustainable digital transformation.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence in Human Resource Management: A Global Comprehensive Overview of Applications, Human–AI Collaboration, Organizational Outcomes, and Ethical Challenges
all.venue: International Journal of Education, Research, and Innovation Perspectives
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping human resource management (HRM) by extending data-driven systems across recruitment and selection, onboarding, learning and development, performance management, employee engagement, workforce planning, and employee services. These applications may improve processing speed, information access, consistency, and analytical capacity. Their organizational value, however, is conditional. AI-enabled HRM can reproduce historical discrimination, weaken employee autonomy, increase surveillance, obscure accountability, and encourage excessive reliance on automated recommendations. This article develops a global integrative overview of AI in HRM using selected peer-reviewed literature published from 2021 through 2026. It is a conceptual and narrative synthesis, not a completed systematic review; accordingly, it does not report PRISMA counts, exhaustive database coverage, or newly calculated effect estimates. The literature is organized around HR functional applications, human–AI collaboration, organizational and employee outcomes, responsible-AI governance, and implementation capabilities. Research on recruitment experiments, algorithmic performance systems, AI capability, and responsible AI indicates that outcomes depend on system design, organizational communication, governance, and the quality of human review. The article proposes a socio-technical framework in which organizational readiness and responsible governance shape the relationship between AI-enabled HR practices and outcomes through decision quality, employee experience, and workforce capability. It concludes that AI should be treated as an augmentation and accountability challenge rather than a technology-acquisition exercise.

all.title: Generative AI adoption in organizations: A conceptual model of job crafting, employee productivity, creativity and work engagement
all.venue: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)
all.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly reshaping organizational work, yet its behavioural consequences for employees remain unevenly understood. Existing research on productivity, creativity and engagement is fragmented and rarely examined within a single theoretical framework. Drawing on Job Demands Resources theory, Conservation of Resources theory and Self Determination Theory, this conceptual paper develops an integrative model of how organizational GenAI adoption affects employee productivity, creativity and work engagement. Job crafting is proposed as the central behavioural mechanism. The model treats GenAI as both a job resource and a job demand. It therefore recognizes a double edged pathway in which technology insecurity and passive over reliance can offset the benefits of adoption. AI literacy, ethical use clarity and organizational readiness are identified as boundary conditions that determine which pathway prevails. Four hypotheses are developed, covering the mediating role of job crafting for productivity and engagement, its moderating role for creativity, and the conditioning effect of AI literacy and ethical guidance. A time lagged, multi source survey design, supplemented by supervisor ratings and an optional field experiment, is proposed for future empirical testing. The paper offers a resource based account of human and AI collaboration. It also provides managerial guidance for organizations that want GenAI adoption to deliver sustainable gains in performance and well being rather than short lived efficiency gains that erode over time.

all.title: Productivity Without Prosperity? Who Captures the Economic Gains from Workplace Artificial Intelligence?
all.abstract: Experiments show that generative AI raises productivity on specific tasks by 14 to 40 percent, but who benefits when it spreads through the economy is far less clear. This study builds a capture accounting from task to economy. It links published field and survey evidence on productivity gains, adoption and wage pass-through to an exact decomposition of productivity gains in the U.S. nonfarm business sector, using the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) release of 5 November 2026 and the Census Bureau’s Business Trends and Outlook Survey. Between the first quarter of 2024 and the third quarter of 2026, output per hour rose by 6.35 log points; 3.28 points (51.7 percent; rounding interval 50.3 to 53.1) reached workers as higher compensation relative to output prices, and 3.07 points went to nonlabor income as the labor share fell to 53.0 percent, the lowest since 1947. Labor’s capture fell from 84 percent in 2024 to 70 percent in 2025 and turned negative (-16 percent) in the four quarters to 2026 Q3, while nonfinancial corporate unit profits rose 16.1 percent. At the worker level, Danish administrative data show only 3 to 7 percent of productivity gains reaching earnings. A consistency bound combining these pass-through rates with plausible shares of AI in productivity growth implies that AI explains a minority of the rise in nonlabor capture (median 23 percent; 5th to 95th percentile 8 to 38 percent) and cannot be the whole story. The evidence is descriptive and aggregate, and the AI shares are bounds, not estimates. Purpose - This study asks who captures the economic gains from workplace AI, and how much of the recent shift in the distribution of productivity gains could plausibly be attributed to it. Design/methodology/approach - The paper combines published task-level, worker-level and firm-level evidence with an exact capture decomposition of BLS quarterly data, rounding-error Monte Carlo intervals, and a consistency analysis that bounds the AI contribution using pass-through rates and adoption arithmetic. Findings - Roughly half of the recent productivity gain went to workers and half to nonlabor income, with workers’ share falling over time and turning negative in the latest quarters. AI use is concentrated in large firms and in information and finance. Pass-through of AI-specific gains to workers is small, but AI can account for only a minority of the shift. Research limitations/implications - Aggregate indexes are rounded and revised, AI shares of productivity growth are not observed, and field studies are not representative of the economy. The analysis cannot identify causal effects. Practical implications - Bargaining institutions, training and transparency over how time savings are used are likely to determine capture, and policy should track labor’s share of gains alongside productivity. Social implications - Productivity growth need not translate into prosperity for workers, and young entrants in exposed occupations face distinct employment risk. Originality/value - The paper provides a transparent accounting that connects micro and macro evidence on AI’s distributional effects and quantifies what current data can and cannot say.

all.title: Who Gets the Credit? Generative AI Contribution Disclosure and Performance Appraisal Fairness among Faculty Members in Indian Higher Education Institutions
all.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by knowledge workers to prepare reports, teaching materials, research summaries, presentations and administrative documents. Although such tools may improve speed and output quality, they create a human resource management question that is not resolved by measuring productivity alone: how should an employee receive performance credit when a work product is created through a combination of human judgement and AI assistance? This conceptual paper develops a research framework to examine the relationship between GenAI contribution disclosure, perceived ownership of work, procedural fairness in performance appraisal and employees’ trust in institutional HR practices among faculty members in Indian higher education institutions. It proposes that transparent disclosure of the type and extent of AI assistance may improve appraisal fairness when institutions use clear contribution criteria and retain human review. However, disclosure may also create a perceived competence penalty if AI-assisted work is interpreted as evidence of lower individual capability. The paper proposes a quantitative, multi-source research design involving faculty members and their academic supervisors. It does not report empirical findings; the hypotheses and framework are intended for subsequent field testing. The study seeks to extend HRM research by connecting human–AI contribution attribution with faculty performance management in the Indian higher education context.

all.title: CULTURAL DIVERSITY AND EMPLOYEE RETENTION IN TIER 1 COMMERCIAL BANKS IN NAIROBI COUNTY, KENYA
all.venue: EPRA International Journal of Economic and Business Review
all.abstract: Kenya’s banking sector contributes largely to economic development through employment creation and provision of financial services. However, with globalisation and cultural shifts, retaining skilled and experienced employees has become a challenge. Recent evidence indicates that annual employee turnover reported to range between 10% and 15%. Therefore, the general objective of the study was to examine the influence of cultural diversity on employee retention in Tier 1 Commercial Banks in Nairobi County, Kenya. The study was anchored on the Social Identity/Categorization Theory. A correlational research design was adopted. The target population was 162 employees drawn from the human resource, finance, operations, customer service, marketing, and ICT departments across the nine Tier 1 Commercial Banks in Nairobi County. Stratified random sampling design was used to sample 115 respondents proportionately distributed across the six departments. Primary data was collected using a structured questionnaire administered through Google Forms. A pilot study was conducted at the Kenya Commercial Bank, Mombasa Branch. The study employed both descriptive and inferential statistics, analysed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS version 21), and data was presented in the form of tables. From the findings, the study concluded that cultural diversity has a statistically significant positive influence on employee retention in Tier 1 Commercial Banks in Nairobi County, Kenya (β = 0.282, p = 0.000; r = 0.825, p = 0.000). Based on the findings and the conclusions of the study, the researcher recommends that Tier 1 Commercial Banks embrace employees' distinct cultural identities, establish dedicated conflict-resolution mechanisms to manage cultural value clashes, and develop comprehensive cross-cultural training programmes to strengthen workforce cohesion.

all.title: The Predictive Influence of Management Leadership Styles on Employee Retention: A Quantitative Study in the Aerospace and Defense Industry
all.abstract: The Aerospace and Defense (A&D) industry in Northern Virginia faces a critical talent shortage exacerbated by high employee turnover and a retiring workforce. Replacing professionals holding specialized security clearances is commonly estimated at 150 to 250 percent of their annual salary. This quantitative, non-experimental applied research examined the predictive relationship between management leadership style and employee turnover intent within this sector. Grounded in Fiedler's Contingency Theory and Leader-Member Exchange Theory, the study surveyed 773 professionals across seven major organizations to measure turnover intent, management leadership style, job satisfaction, and leader support. Hierarchical multiple regression isolated leadership style's association with turnover intent from four demographic controls: age, gender, role, and years of service. The results showed that demographic variables accounted for 7.5 percent of the variance in turnover intent, and a composite leadership-style score explained an additional, independent 14.8 percent. Higher composite scores (reflecting more participative and delegative, less authoritative, supervisory behavior) were associated with significantly lower turnover intent, suggesting relationship-oriented leadership meaningfully predicts retention. Leadership style, job satisfaction, and leader support were strongly interrelated, consistent with the study's theoretical framework, though job satisfaction and leader support showed a substantially stronger direct association with turnover intent than leadership style alone. The findings suggest that shifting from technical, authoritative management toward more human-centric, participative leadership may help organizations mitigate talent drain. The study concludes with practical recommendations for industry leaders and integrates a biblical perspective on the moral imperative of stewarding human capital.

all.title: Transformational Leadership Effect on Public Sector Employee Retention: A Systematic Literature Review
all.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
all.abstract: Transformational leadership is considered an important leadership approach that can affect the employees’ experience at work and organizational commitment. However, there is a need for an overall analysis of the leadership dimensions and indicators discussed in current research to understand its relationship with employee retention in the public sector. In this research, a systematic literature review (SLR) has been conducted on 50 articles, based on the PRISMA methodology, about the relationship between transformational leadership and employee retention in the public sector. The objective of this paper is to highlight the major themes and indicators used to investigate the relationship between transformational leadership and employee retention. The review finds six main themes, which are idealized influence, individualized consideration, intellectual stimulation, inspirational motivation, empowerment and vision building with eleven indicators. Individualized consideration was the most common theme, followed by intellectual stimulation. Career development was the most frequently reported indicator. The findings offer a systematic overview of dominant areas of scholarly attention and highlight comparatively less scrutinized dimensions such as vision building and empowerment. This review provides a foundation to comprehend the conceptualization of transformational leadership in public sector retention research and provides direction for future empirical study.

all.title: Employee Retention Strategies and Performance of Microfinance Institutions in Nairobi City County, Kenya
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
institutions: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology
all.abstract: In the current fast moving and competitive business environment, organizations recognize that employees are not merely resources but valuable assets whose knowledge, skills and commitment greatly influence organizational success. As a result, attracting, retaining and developing a skilled workforce has become a strategic concern. Several employee retention strategies have been examined in empirical studies, including compensation, career advancement, work–life balance and recognition. However, the effect of these strategies on organizational performance remains inadequately examined, particularly within the Kenyan microfinance sector. The present study therefore assessed the effect of employee retention strategies on the performance of Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Specifically, the study sought to establish the effect of compensation and of career advancement on the performance of MFIs in Nairobi City County. The study was guided by Equity Theory and Human Capital Theory and adopted a descriptive research design. The target population comprised 4,920 employees of 14 microfinance institutions in Nairobi City County. The Yamane formula yielded a sample size of 369 employees, who were selected by stratified random sampling with the four departments in the organizations forming the strata. Quantitative primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire, and 295 questionnaires were returned. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. The study concludes that compensation and career advancement each have a positive and significant influence on the performance of microfinance institutions in Nairobi City County, Kenya. The study recommends that microfinance institutions should regularly review salaries, incentives, bonuses and other benefits to ensure that they remain attractive and aligned with employee performance. The study further recommends that the institutions should provide transparent promotion pathways, regular career development discussions and opportunities for employees to acquire the skills required for advancement. Keywords: Employee Retention Strategies, Compensation, Career Advancement Opportunities, Performance of Microfinance Institutions

all.title: The Influence of Work-Life Imbalance and Training & Development on Employee Turnover Among Employees of Multinational Companies in Solo Raya
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
all.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effects of work-life imbalance and training and development on Employee Turnover among employees of multinational companies in the Greater Solo area. The imbalance between work and personal life, as well as opportunities for employee development, are critical factors in retaining the workforce amid the demands of a dynamic work environment. This study employs a quantitative approach, involving 103 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale, while data analysis employed the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method using SmartPLS 3 software. Model evaluation included validity and reliability testing, structural model assessment, and hypothesis testing based on path coefficients and significance levels. The results indicate that work-life imbalance has a positive and significant effect on Employee Turnover, whereas training and development do not show a significant effect. These findings underscore the importance of managing work-life balance in employee retention strategies. Companies also need to ensure that training and development programs align with job requirements and employees’ career aspirations to make efforts to retain the workforce more effective.

all.title: The Intrinsic Drivers of Employee Retention: Reassessment of Organizational Justice Theory in a Resource Constrained Context
all.abstract: This study challenges the assumption that distributive justice remains a dominant driver of employee retention in resource‑constrained contexts. Drawing on Organizational Justice Theory, Self‑Determination Theory, and Two‑Factor Theory, the research examines how job satisfaction, work–life balance, distributive justice, and perceived job quality influence employees’ intention to stay within a private sector healthcare environment. The study investigates whether distributive fairness still remains a dominant driver of retention in an economically constrained environment. Using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‑SEM) on survey data from 177 employees across multiple settings, results indicate that job satisfaction and work–life balance significantly predict intention to stay, whereas distributive justice and perceived job quality do not. The findings suggest that intrinsic motivational factors tend to supersede distributive fairness considerations in a limited resourced context, thereby offering boundary conditions for justice‑based retention frameworks. Its implications for contextualized HRM theory and retention strategy are further discussed.

all.title: Beyond Formal HRM: Relational Practices and Employee Retention in SMEs – A Systematic Literature Review
all.abstract: This article develops a conceptual framework and reports a reproducible bibliographic inventory and provisional abstract-level map concerning formal human resource management (HRM), relational practices, and employee retention in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Two Scopus exports dated 19 October 2026 contained 219 records, with 11 duplicates removed and 208 unique records retained. A rule-based preliminary triage of all unique abstracts flagged three direct retention candidates, ten further retention candidates requiring SME confirmation, 24 supporting mechanism studies, six records requiring design checks, one record missing an abstract, and 164 records likely outside scope pending manual confirmation. These categories are not final inclusion or exclusion decisions. Three direct candidates and five illustrative supporting studies are discussed at the construct level. The proposed framework separates organizational practices, employee perceptions, attachment mechanisms, and retention outcomes. Complementarity, compensation, and undermining remain conceptual configurations rather than tested common effects. Enterprise-size verification, family-employee status, full-text statistical estimates, independent screening, and methodological appraisal are outstanding. No final eligible-study count or effect estimate is inferred from preliminary triage.

all.title: The Influence of Compensation and Democratic Leadership Style on Employee Turnover at the Central Mail Processing Office (SPP) in Yogyakarta
all.abstract: Employee turnover can disrupt workforce stability and operational continuity in logistics services. Interviews at the Central Postal Processing Office (SPP) in Yogyakarta identified 24 employees who had left or been replaced, representing a reported 15.69% of the workforce. This study examined how compensation and democratic leadership style were associated with employee turnover at the office. Using a quantitative causal-associative design, the study surveyed 156 employees through total population sampling. Responses to Likert-scale questionnaires were analyzed using multiple linear regression in SPSS. Compensation was negatively associated with turnover (coefficient = −0.199, p = .036). The association between democratic leadership style and turnover was statistically nonsignificant (coefficient = −0.012, p = .937). The model accounted for 2.4% of the variance in turnover (adjusted R² = .024), indicating limited explanatory power. The findings suggest that management could review compensation policies, particularly employee benefits, while maintaining supportive leadership practices as part of its retention efforts.

all.title: Working With Robots: How Robot Proportion in Human-Robot Teams and Robot Anthropomorphism Shape Employee Turnover Intention
all.abstract: Although robots are increasingly reshaping organizational workflows, how the robot proportion in human-robot teams affects employees’ turnover intention remains underexplored. Drawing on conservation of resources theory, we examine whether, why, and when robot proportion exerts divergent effects on turnover intention through two pathways: resource gain and resource loss. Evidence from a scenario-based experiment (Study 1, N = 290) and a three-wave field study (Study 2, N = 306) reveals that these two pathways operate in opposing directions. Specifically, work goal progress and work loneliness mediate the relationship between robot proportion in human-robot teams and turnover intention. Robot anthropomorphism further moderates these pathways: higher anthropomorphism strengthens the beneficial effect on work goal progress, whereas lower anthropomorphism amplifies the detrimental effect on work loneliness. This study offers initial evidence on how the structural composition of human-robot teams shapes employees’ turnover intention, and it provides practical implications for organizations deploying robotic coworkers.

all.title: INFLUENCE OF MENTORSHIP PRACTICES ON EMPLOYEE RETENTION IN STATE-OWNED HEALTH INSTITUTIONS IN NAIROBI CITY COUNTY, KENYA
all.venue: Academic Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences Research
all.abstract: Purpose of Study: The study sought to determine the influence of mentorship practices on employee retention in state-owned health institutions in Nairobi City County, Kenya. Specifically, it examined how mentorship contributes to employee commitment, career development, and intention to remain in public health institutions, guided by Social Exchange Theory and organisational support principles. Methodology: The study adopted a descriptive cross-sectional research design integrating quantitative and qualitative approaches. The target population comprised 7,358 employees, with 379 selected through stratified random sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and interviews. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and regression analysis, alongside qualitative thematic analysis. Findings: The findings revealed mixed perceptions of mentorship practices, with mean scores ranging from 2.85 to 3.15. Lack of formal mentorship structures (30.8%), inadequate senior staff (25.4%), and time constraints (21.7%) were major challenges. Although 59.5%–63.6% of respondents expressed organisational commitment and intention to remain, 47.6%–49.3% reported considering departure. Pearson correlation indicated a strong positive relationship between mentorship and retention (r = 0.671, p < 0.01). Regression analysis further established a positive, statistically significant influence of mentorship practices on employee retention (β = 0.231, p < 0.001), highlighting their contribution to workforce stability in public healthcare institutions. Conclusion: The study concluded that mentorship practices significantly influence employee retention, although their explanatory contribution remains modest. It recommends institutionalising structured mentorship programmes, ensuring equitable access, allocating dedicated mentoring time and strengthening career development opportunities. Integrating mentorship with recognition, transparent promotion procedures and supportive working conditions could enhance sustainable employee retention.

all.title: Work–Life Balance and Employee Retention: The Mediating Effect of Job Satisfaction and the Moderating Effect of Organizational Support
all.abstract: Employee retention (ER) is crucial for hospital sustainability and healthcare quality. Given inconsistent findings on the effect of work-life balance (WLB) on ER, this study examines job satisfaction (JS) as a mediator of the relationship between WLB and ER and perceived organizational support (POS) as a moderator of the relationship between WLB and JS. This study examines the direct and indirect effects of WLB on ER, with JS as a mediator and POS as a moderator of the relationship between WLB and JS. This quantitative causal study collected questionnaire data from 150 employees, using convenience sampling. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results show that WLB has a positive effect on JS and ER. JS mediates the relationship between WLB and ER, and POS moderates the effect of WLB on JS. The implications of this study indicate that WLB is important for employees in promoting higher JS and ER. Therefore, organizations need to implement policies that support WLB, such as flexible work schedules, balanced workload distribution, and adequate leave policies. These efforts can enhance employees’ JS, which in turn strengthens their commitment and intention to remain in the organization.

all.title: Compensation, Promotion Opportunities and Employee Retention among National Police Service Officers in Nairobi City County, Kenya
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
institutions: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology
all.abstract: Increasing cases of police officers exiting the service before retirement have raised concerns about workforce sustainability and the adequacy of reward management practices within the National Police Service (NPS) in Kenya. This study examined the effect of compensation and promotion opportunities on the retention of police officers in Nairobi City County, Kenya. The study was anchored on Social Exchange Theory and Expectancy Theory and adopted a convergent mixed-methods design. The target population comprised 9,530 police officers from the Kenya Police Service, Administration Police Service and Directorate of Criminal Investigations. A sample of 384 officers was selected using stratified random sampling, while key informants from the NPS and the National Police Service Commission were selected purposively. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and interview guides, and 329 questionnaires were returned, a response rate of 85.7%. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. Officers held generally unfavourable perceptions of compensation (M = 2.57) and promotion opportunities (M = 1.80). Compensation (r = 0.290) and promotion opportunities (r = 0.216) were positively and significantly correlated with retention. Jointly, the two practices explained 9.7% of the variation in employee retention. Compensation (Beta = 0.243, p < 0.001) and promotion opportunities (Beta = 0.121, p = 0.035) each had a positive and significant effect on retention. The study concludes that compensation and promotion opportunities contribute to the retention of police officers, although other factors account for most of the variation in retention. The study recommends that the NPS and NPSC review salaries and allowances to improve their fairness, adequacy and competitiveness, and strengthen the transparency, fairness and timeliness of promotion processes. Keywords: Compensation, Promotion Opportunities, Employee Retention, National Police Service, Reward Management

all.title: Employee Experience and Employee Engagement as Determinants of Employee Retention: Evidence from PT Air Tech Inti Karawaci Indonesia
all.abstract: Perceived retention-supporting conditions represent an important aspect of human resource management in promoting workforce stability. This study aimed to examine the individual and simultaneous associations of employee experience and employee engagement with perceived retention-supporting conditions at PT Air Tech Inti Karawaci Indonesia, West Jakarta. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, involving all 35 employees through saturated sampling. Data were collected using structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaires and analyzed through multiple linear regression using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. The results indicated that employee experience had a positive and statistically significant association with perceived retention-supporting conditions (β = 0.787, t = 7.687, p < 0.001), whereas employee engagement showed a positive but non-significant association (β = 0.150, t = 1.466, p = 0.153). The overall regression model was statistically significant (F(2, 32) = 56.254, p < 0.001), explaining 77.9% of the in-sample variance in the measured outcome (R² = 0.779). Employee experience emerged as the stronger independent predictor of perceived retention-supporting conditions. However, the findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the small sample size, cross-sectional design, potential construct overlap, and reliance on self-reported measures. Future research should incorporate validated intention-to-stay measures and actual employee retention records to establish a clearer understanding of workforce stability.

all.title: Work-Based Reward Schemes and Employee Retention among National Police Service Officers in Nairobi City County, Kenya
all.venue: East African Journal of Business and Economics
institutions: Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology
all.abstract: Employee retention is essential for maintaining workforce stability, institutional experience, and effective service delivery in law enforcement agencies. However, concerns regarding the adequacy of welfare provisions may undermine police officers’ willingness to remain in service. This study examined the relationship between work-based reward schemes and employee retention among National Police Service (NPS) officers in Nairobi City County, Kenya. The study adopted a convergent mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected from 329 police officers using structured questionnaires, while qualitative data were obtained through interviews with three key informants from the NPS and National Police Service Commission. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and simple linear regression, while qualitative data were analysed thematically. The findings revealed that respondents had generally unfavourable perceptions of the adequacy of work-based reward schemes (M = 2.71, SD = 1.26), particularly regarding housing allowances, medical insurance and pension arrangements. Employee retention was moderate (M = 3.28, SD = 1.25), with respondents reporting relatively favourable levels of loyalty to the Service and commitment to their responsibilities, although these findings suggest that retention-related attitudes were not uniformly strong. Qualitative findings corroborated the quantitative results, indicating that despite the availability of various welfare provisions, inadequacies in working and housing conditions could weaken officers’ intentions to remain in the Service. Pearson correlation analysis established a positive and statistically significant relationship between work-based reward schemes and employee retention (r = 0.565, p < 0.001). Simple linear regression further established that work-based reward schemes had a statistically significant positive predictive relationship with employee retention (B = .687, β = 0.565, t = 12.388, p < 0.001), explaining 31.9% of the variation in employee retention (R² = 0.319). The study concludes that work-based reward schemes are an important predictor of employee retention among NPS officers. It recommends strengthening the adequacy and implementation of medical insurance, housing support, pension arrangements, psychosocial services and other welfare provisions to support officers’ retention.

all.title: Influence of Strategic Human Resource Management Practices on Employee Retention in Rwanda: A Case of Rwanda Medical Supply Limited (RMS Ltd)
all.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
all.abstract: This study examined the influence of Strategic Human Resource Management (SHRM) practices on employee retention at Rwanda Medical Supply Limited (RMS Ltd). Specifically, it assessed the effects of compensation, career management, and work-life balance on employee retention. The study was anchored on Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs Theory, Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, Human Capital Theory, and Universal Theory of Strategic Human Resource Management.A descriptive research design and quantitative approach were adopted.From a target population of 288 permanent employees, a sample of 167 respondents was determined using Yamane's formula and selected through stratified random sampling.Data were collected using structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaires and documentary review, then analyzed using SPSS version 25 through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression analysis.Results showed significant positive correlations between employee retention and compensation (r = .695,p < .01),career management (r = .583,p < .01),and work-life balance (r = .549,p < .01).Regression results indicated that compensation (β = .532,p < .001)and worklife balance (β = .429,p < .001)significantly influenced retention, while career management had a positive but non-significant effect (β = .045,p = .484).The model explained 61.5% of the variance in employee retention (R² = .615,p < .001).The study recommends competitive compensation, flexible-work and wellness initiatives, and strengthened career development.

all.title: ANALISIS FAKTOR-FAKTOR YANG MEMPENGARUHI EMPLOYEE RETENTION, DIMEDIASI OLEH EMPLOYEE SATISFACTION PADA HOTEL BINTANG EMPAT DI JAKARTA
all.venue: Publik Jurnal Manajemen Sumber Daya Manusia Administrasi dan Pelayanan Publik
all.abstract: This study examines the effects of Internal Communication, Psychological Well-being, and Green Transformational Leadership on Employee Retention, with Employee Satisfaction serving as a mediating variable among employees of four-star hotels in Jakarta. A quantitative approach was employed using a survey of 207 employees selected through purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with AMOS. The results indicate that Psychological Well-being has a positive and significant effect on both Employee Retention and Employee Satisfaction, while Green Transformational Leadership has a positive and significant effect only on Employee Satisfaction. In contrast, Internal Communication has no significant effect on either Employee Satisfaction or Employee Retention. Furthermore, Employee Satisfaction has a positive and significant effect on Employee Retention, partially mediates the relationship between Psychological Well-being and Employee Retention, fully mediates the relationship between Green Transformational Leadership and Employee Retention, and does not mediate the relationship between Internal Communication and Employee Retention.
