The findings highlight the critical role of Employee Satisfaction as a key mechanism through which Psychological Well-being and Green Transformational Leadership enhance Employee Retention in four-star hotels in Jakarta.

all.title: DMADV Methodology in Talent Retention Management: A Systematic Literature Review and Analysis of Techniques (2016–2026)
all.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
institutions: Tecnológico Nacional de México, Campus Pachuca
all.abstract: Employee turnover represents one of the most costly and persistent challenges in contemporary organizations, particularly in manufacturing and industrial settings in Mexico and Latin America, where annual rates frequently exceed 30%. This study presents a systematic literature review, conducted following the PRISMA methodology, of the applications of the DMADV cycle and Lean Six Sigma to the reduction of employee turnover during the period 2016–2026. After screening approximately 230 records, 20 empirical studies and documented cases were included. The analysis shows that the disciplined application of DMADV produces measurable reductions in voluntary turnover, commonly ranging from 10% to 35%, together with significant shortenings of induction or onboarding cycle times (up to 50% in several cases) and improvements in work-climate indicators. The most recurrent root causes are deficient induction, weak leadership, unfavorable work climate, limited career development, and excessive workload. The most effective interventions combine structured induction programs, leadership training, mentoring systems, and continuous control mechanisms based on KPIs and NPS. These findings are consistent with the results obtained in the DMADV project implemented at Bruluagsa S.A. de C.V. (Atlacomulco pharmaceutical plant), where the induction cycle time was reduced from 569 to 281 days. The review confirms that Lean Six Sigma provides a structured, data-driven approach capable of transforming talent retention into a controllable process, while also highlighting the need for longer follow-up periods and greater methodological rigor in future research

all.title: Penerapan Data mining untuk Prediksi Turnover Karyawan Rumah Sakit dalam Manajemen Sumber Daya Manusia Metode Hybrid Naïve Bayes dan C4.5
all.venue: CEMERLANG Jurnal Manajemen dan Ekonomi Bisnis
all.abstract: The high rate of employee turnover in hospitals, reaching 20-30% per year, has become a serious challenge for human resource management (HRM) because it affects productivity, operational costs, and the quality of health services. This research is grounded in data mining theory through the Knowledge Discovery in Database (KDD) framework and the Naïve Bayes and C4.5 (Decision tree) classification algorithms, which respectively offer probabilistic advantages and interpretable decision-tree capability in predicting employee turnover. This study employed a descriptive qualitative method with a Human Resource Analytics approach, utilizing secondary data from the Human Resource Analytics (HRIS) consisting of 153 employee records at a private hospital in Menteng, Central Jakarta. The research stages followed the KDD process, comprising data selection, preprocessing, transformation, data mining, and evaluation, with model testing carried out through a K-Fold Cross Validation scheme using RapidMiner. The results showed that the Naïve Bayes algorithm achieved an accuracy of 91.30% with an AUC of 0.971, while C4.5 produced a higher accuracy of 97.83% with an AUC of 0.993, so that C4.5 is recommended as the primary predictive model. In conclusion, the application of data mining with a hybrid Naïve Bayes and C4.5 approach proved effective and feasible as the basis for a data-driven decision support system in formulating hospital employee retention strategies

all.title: Organizational Climate, Leadership, and Employee Outcomes
all.abstract: This study examines the correlation between job satisfaction, employee turnover, organizational climate, organizational culture, and transformational leadership. Quantitative methodology was used; the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was used to perform the analysis on the data obtained, which comprised 250 employees working in various organizational settings. They measured using standardized instruments that were designed to guarantee the precision and dependability of the measurements, such as the Job Descriptive Index (JDI), the Organizational Climate Assessment Instrument (OCAI), and the Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ-5X). These findings affirmed that transformational leadership is closely and significantly related with job satisfaction (r = 0.7420, p < 0.0010), organizational climate (r = 0.6920, p < 0.00100) and organizational culture (r = 0.5860, p < 0.0010). The hierarchical regression analysis showed that the combination of transformational leadership, organizational climate, and organizational culture described 59% of job satisfaction (R² = 0.5901, F = 118.1741, p < 0.0011). In addition, job satisfaction was also identified as a mediating factor between these organizational aspects and employee turnover. In general, the results confirm the theoretical lens that a conducive organizational climate and culture promote the practice of transformational leadership, which increases the level of job satisfaction in employees and eventually decreases turnover intentions. This research contributes to the body of leadership and organizational behavior literature by hypothesizing and empirically justifying a model that is integrated and multi-level by analyzing transformational leadership, organizational climate, organizational culture, job satisfaction, and real rates of attrition in one multi-level framework. This is in contrast with other models that have experimented with the constructs individually or in the form of direct associations because our model illustrates how climate and culture work simultaneously as contextual enablers of leadership, as well as indirectly as a way in which turnover is determined by job satisfaction. The study explains employee retention dynamics in a more detailed way, since it explains 59% of the difference in job satisfaction and verifies many mediation effects. Therefore, it goes beyond the piecemeal empirical evidence and offers a theoretically based, context-sensitive framework for creating a correlation between leadership behavior and quantifiable organizational results. Practical implications would be that organizations should be oriented to developing transformational leadership capacities and, simultaneously, develop favorable organizational climates and cultures to enhance employee retention and satisfaction.

all.title: The Effect of Toxic Leadership and Workload on Turnover Intention: The Mediating Role of Job Stress
all.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
all.abstract: Background and Purpose: Digital transformation is evolving the practices and services of banks at a rapid pace. Along with mobile digital and electronic banking services and fintech, there are great pressures for banks to evolve based on available technology and the needs of the consumer. In this environment, strategic human resources are critical to maintaining service and the competitive edge of the bank. Fast changing technology and competitive pressures increase the demands of the job, the workload, and job stress. These factors will likely increase the employee turnover rate. This study examines how toxic leadership and workload contribute to banking employee turnover, with job stress as a mediating factor. Methodology: This study adopts a quantitative methodology. The primary data for this study were obtained from surveys with a five-point Likert scale that were distributed to a total sample of 215 banking employees in Pontianak, Indonesia, through purposive sampling. The collected data were analyzed with the help of Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using SmartPLS 4. Findings: The results suggest that job stress is positively correlated with both toxic leadership and workload, and that job stress increases the intention to leave. Furthermore, toxic leadership and workload have an influence on the intention to leave. Stress plays a mediating role in the nexus of toxic leadership, workload, and the intention to leave. Contributions: This study examines how toxic leadership and workload drive employees to quit their jobs in the banking sector in Pontianak, Indonesia. Job stress mediates the impact of these variables on the intention to quit. The results highlight the importance of eliminating toxic leadership and managing workload to reduce job stress and the intention to quit. This also aims to improve employee retention and create a stable, productive, and competitive banking environment.

all.title: Selected Factors Affecting Turnover Intention of Finance Sector Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Employees in Colombo District: Mediating Role of Organizational Commitment & Moderating Role of Alternative Job Opportunities
all.abstract: Employee Turnover Intention problem has become an emerging problem in most Sri Lankan contexts, and it can be majorly seen in the Finance Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) sector. Employee Turnover Intention is the employee’s tendency to leave the organizations due to distinct factors such as the imbalance between work and individual life. There were less studies concerned the Finance BPO service sector employees and therefore the main purpose of this study is to identify the factors affecting Employee Turnover Intention in Finance – BPO sector employees in Sri Lanka with the mediating effect of organizational commitment & the moderating variable of alternative job opportunities. Accordingly, the population of this study consists of all the employees who are working in Finance BPO sector in Sri Lankan context and the sample of this study consists of the employees of Finance BPO sector in top 10 commercialized BPO organizations in Sri Lanka. Guided by Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, this study investigates four primary factors: rewards, career development opportunities, working environment & job satisfaction significantly influence employees’ turnover intention while the organizational commitment mediating the relationship between the factors affecting to the employee turnover intention and the employee turnover intention & alternative job opportunities moderating the relationship between the organizational commitment and the employee turnover intention The researcher has used the main data collection method of survey by distributing the questionnaire via online (Google Form) to the selected sample and succeeded in collecting 200 respondents. The researcher has used the SPSS Statistical Software to identify significant relationships. The results revealed that all the variables have significant negative impact on employees’ turnover intention. Furthermore, the organizational commitment mediates significantly the factors affecting the employees’ turnover intention & the alternative job opportunities moderates significantly in the relationship between the organizational commitment and the employees’ turnover intention. Overall, the findings confirm that the selected factors are significantly influencing the employees’ turnover intention, with career growth opportunities emerging as the most influential variable & working environment emerging as the least influential variable. The results offer valuable insights for BPO managers and HR practitioners in developing targeted retention strategies that enhance employee satisfaction and organizational stability.

all.title: The Influence of Compensation and Workload on Turnover Intention with Job Satisfaction as a Mediating Variable
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
all.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of compensation and workload on turnover intention with job satisfaction as a mediating variable among employees at PT Korindo Abadi in Papua. Motivated by high employee turnover rates in remote geographical regions, this research employs a causal quantitative approach. A sample of 74 respondents was selected from a total population of 290 employees using proportional stratified random sampling based on Slovin's formula. Data were collected through a 5-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4.0. The analysis results indicate that compensation has a significant positive effect on job satisfaction (f² = 2.227, p = 0.000), whereas workload has a significant negative effect on job satisfaction (f² = 1.025, p = 0.000). Compensation does not have a direct significant effect on turnover intention (p = 0.373), but workload exerts a significant direct positive effect on turnover intention (f² = 0.217, p = 0.035). Furthermore, job satisfaction does not significantly affect turnover intention (p = 0.264) and fails to mediate the effect of either compensation or workload on turnover intention. The findings suggest that in extreme geographical contexts, external factors override internal psychological satisfaction in determining employee retention.

all.title: Determinasi Retensi Karyawan Ditinjau dari Employee Engagement, Pengembangan Karir, dan Lingkungan Kerja
all.venue: Jurnal Akuntansi Ekonomi dan Manajemen Bisnis
all.abstract: This study examines the effect of employee engagement, career development, and work environment on employee retention, with organizational commitment as an intervening variable. The research was conducted at PT Parsaoran Global Datatrans, an internet service provider operating across six regional areas in Indonesia. A quantitative approach was employed using survey data collected from 96 employees, selected through proportional stratified random sampling from a population of 2,207 employees. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The results indicate that employee engagement and career development have a positive and significant effect on employee retention, while the work environment does not show a significant effect. Furthermore, organizational commitment does not have a significant effect on employee retention and does not mediate the relationship between employee engagement, career development, work environment, and employee retention. These findings suggest that strengthening employee engagement and providing clear career development opportunities are more critical for improving employee retention than relying on organizational commitment as an intervening mechanism. The study contributes to the human resource management literature by providing empirical evidence on employee retention determinants in the internet service industry.

all.title: Examining turnover intention in the public hospitals: An integrated model of job stress and organizational justice
all.abstract: While job stress is acknowledged as a significant factor, the relation with turnover intention is unambiguously clear. Although job stress recognized as an important variable, it does not entirely comprehend the notion of organizational justice, which is extremely significant for individual well-being and decision making. Not only job stress influence employee turnover intention but organizational justice also plays a significant role in employee retention. Nevertheless, a review of the extant literature shows a lack of scholarly research particularly addressing the organizational justice along with stress on job on the relationship of turnover intention. This research gap calls for more investigation. Hence, this study aims to pose following research questions: Does stress on job has a significant impact on turnover intention? In addition, to what degree does organizational justice dimensions have significant impact on turnover intention? This research uses a quantitative method with a survey design. The aim is to investigate a certain employees of public hospitals of Sindh province rather than to generalize the study results. The sample was selected through a random sampling method at the study location. Data were collected using adopted scales and examined through SPSS and PLS. The findings of this research suggest that the first hypothesis, which states that job stress has a significant impact on turnover intention, is accepted. In addition, the second and third hypotheses are also accepted, indicating that distributive and procedural justice have significant effect on turnover intention, while last hypothesis of study is rejected based on results. Results are aligning with most of the past studies on domain.

all.title: PENGARUH KOMITMEN ORGANISASI DAN KEPUASAN KERJA TERHADAP KEUNGGULAN KOMPETITIF MELALUI RETENSI KARYAWAN PADA TOKO TANETE DI KOTA TIMIKA
all.abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of organizational commitment, job satisfaction, and competitive advantage on employee retention at Tanete Store. The method used in this study is the associative method. The data collection techniques employed by the researcher were observation and questionnaires. This study is a quantitative study. The population for this study consisted of 54 Tanete Store employees, who were selected as the research sample using the census method. SPSS was used for data analysis. Overall, the results of this study confirm that job satisfaction has a positive and significant effect on employee retention; organizational commitment has a positive and significant effect on competitive advantage; and employee retention has a positive and significant effect on competitive advantage. Path analysis results show that organizational commitment has a positive indirect effect on competitive advantage through employee retention. Conversely, although job satisfaction has a fairly large indirect effect through retention, its total effect on competitive advantage is actually very small and tends to be negative.

all.title: Overt Incivility and Employee Withdrawal Behaviour in Public Owned Hospitals in South-South Region of Nigeria
all.abstract: This study investigated the relationship between overt incivility and employee withdrawal behaviour in public hospitals in the South-south region of Nigeria, and determining the moderating ability of personality traits. A number of factors have been suspected to cause employee withdrawal behaviour, they include organisational climate, financial benefits, organisational structure and management’s attitude towards employees (Okache, 2020) which makes employee withdrawal behaviour even more glaring because it affects organisational performance negatively. The cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, as quantitative data was gathered through the use of a structured questionnaire. The accessible population of this study is 9610 senior staff (including doctors, nurses, laboratory scientists, pharmacists and administrators) from 12 selected public owned hospitals and a sample size of 369 employees derived through the Krejcie and Morgan table were used for the study. However, the Bowley’s (1964) formula was used in allocating the number of copies of the questionnaire to each healthcare facility. Overt incivility was measured using the Workplace Incivility Scale (WIS) and employee withdrawal behaviour was measured with the Employee Withdrawal Behaviour Scale (EWBS). The data collected was analysed by Spearman Rank Order Correlation Coefficient which was also used to indicate the strength and direction of these relationships. Findings revealed that there is a significant correlation between overt incivility and measures of employee withdrawal behaviour, with overt incivility and employee turnover behaviour exhibiting the strongest positive correlation coefficient of 0.762. Overt incivility and tardiness revealed the weakest positive correlation at 0.285. Personality trait was observed to be a potent moderator between the variables. The study concludes that employee withdrawal behaviour is ignited by overt incivility and recommends that the workplace culture and climate be made more conducive for better employee retention through management flexibility and readiness to prevent situations that encourage employee withdrawal behaviour.

all.title: Algorithmic Management as a Double-Edged Form of Digital Work Design: Job Demands, Autonomy and Employee Outcomes across 35 European Countries
all.abstract: Computer-based managerial systems are part of the digital infrastructure of work, with potential implications for employee demands and discretion. Drawing on Job Demands-Resources theory, this study examines task allocation, work scheduling and performance monitoring as distinct functions and their parallel indirect associations with engagement and intention to quit through work intensity and autonomy. Weighted least squares mean- and variance-adjusted structural equation models were estimated for 26,504 employees in 35 European countries using the 2024 European Working Conditions Survey. The measures capture reported computer involvement rather than verified artificial intelligence capabilities. Engagement and autonomy were modelled as latent factors, and quit intention as an ordinal outcome. All three practices were positively associated with work intensity. Task allocation was positively associated with autonomy, whereas monitoring was negatively associated with autonomy; scheduling’s negative autonomy association was less robust to contextual fixed effects. Task allocation showed opposing indirect engagement associations through intensity and autonomy, whereas monitoring showed negative associations through both pathways. Intensity-related indirect associations with quit intention were consistently positive, while autonomy-related indirect associations were not statistically significant in the primary or fixed-effects models. Sensitivity analyses supported the main directional patterns, while exploratory country diagnostics indicated incomplete measurement invariance and heterogeneous slopes. The findings inform the evaluation of digital management by distinguishing functions associated with greater demands and greater autonomy from those associated with greater demands and reduced autonomy. The cross-sectional design does not establish causal mediation or uniform cross-country relationships.

all.title: An Analysis of Turnover Intention Based on Workload and Work Environment at PT Amarta Honda Motor’s Gorontalo City Branch
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
all.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of workload and work environment on employee turnover intention at PT. Amarta Sayap Merah (Honda Motor), Gorontalo City Branch. The study was motivated by the high rate of employee turnover over the past three years as well as relatively high sales targets. This study employs a quantitative approach, with primary data collected via a questionnaire from 63 respondents, supplemented by observations, interviews, and documentation. The test results indicate that, when analyzed individually, workload does not significantly affect turnover intention (t-calculated = -0.769; sig. 0.445 > 0.05), whereas the work environment does significantly affect turnover intention (t calculated = 2.410; sig. 0.019 < 0.05). Simultaneously, workload and work environment do not have a significant effect on turnover intention (F_calculated = 2.908; sig. 0.062 > 0.05). The coefficient of determination indicates that these two variables explain 8.8% of the variation in turnover intention, while 91.2% is explained by other variables outside the scope of this study.

all.title: Generational differences in quiet quitting: Exploring presenteeism and job burnout among hotel employees
all.venue: Journal of Tourism Leisure and Hospitality
all.abstract: This study examines the relationships between quiet quitting, presenteeism, and burnout among hotel employees, based on Generation Theory and Conservation of Resources (COR) theory. It also aims to determine whether quiet quitting levels differ across generations. Data were collected from employees of 5-star hotels operating in Türkiye using a survey, a quantitative data collection method. The findings show a positive relationship between quiet quitting and presenteeism, and between presenteeism and job burnout. Furthermore, hotel employees across Generations X, Y, and Z differ significantly in their perceptions of quiet quitting. The present study offers recommendations for HR managers and practitioners to reduce employee turnover in the hospitality industry.

all.title: HOW JOB CHARACTERISTICS INFLUENCE THE MOTIVATION OF MILLENNIAL HOSPITALITY WORKERS IN BRAZIL
all.abstract: This article investigates how job characteristics influence the motivation of Millennial hospitality workers in Brazil, where turnover is high and work schedules are demanding. The authors collected 137 responses from Millennials (18+) through an online questionnaire shared on LinkedIn and WhatsApp, then tested a structural model with PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. Motivation was modeled as the outcome of five predictors: organizational culture, feedback, skill variety, organizational support, and task importance. The measurement model retained 26 indicators with acceptable reliability and discriminant validity, and the structural model explained substantial variance in motivation (R2 ≈ 0.76). Hypothesis tests showed that only feedback had a strong, statistically significant positive effect on motivation, while culture (negative), support, task importance, and skill variety were not significant. The findings suggest that frequent, clear, developmental feedback is the most actionable lever for motivating and retaining Millennial hospitality employees in this sample. It also highlights limits of culture-focused interventions alone. The study articulates job characteristics and Millennial motivation in Brazilian hospitality, a context still underexplored empirically. By testing multiple predictors via PLS-SEM, it shows that feedback surpasses culture, support, and skill variety as the main motivational factor, offering novel evidence and specific practical implications for employee retention. The study articulates job characteristics and Millennial motivation in Brazilian hospitality, a context still underexplored empirically. By testing multiple predictors via PLS-SEM, it shows that feedback surpasses culture, support, and skill variety as the main motivational factor, offering novel evidence and specific practical implications for employee retention.

all.title: Where turnover contagion tips: Coworker network structure, job embeddedness, and retention targeting in an agent-based model
all.abstract: Employee turnover spreads among coworkers, but the organizational consequences of that contagion are poorly understood. We build an agent-based model in which employees embedded in a coworker network start searching for a new job when shocks and the share of searching or vacant coworkers exceed an embeddedness-dependent threshold. Across about 63,000 simulation runs, contagion strength produced a sharp tipping point between modest amplification of turnover and a self-sustaining regime. Clustered networks tipped earlier than random ones, whereas hubs alone did not lower the tipping point. Higher mean job embeddedness delayed tipping strongly. Under a fixed budget, retention practices that reached hubs or brokers and were attached to positions rather than individuals raised the tipping point most. The model is stylized and uncalibrated, so the findings are hypotheses for empirical testing.

all.title: Recognition, Rewards, and Employee Engagement: Reducing Turnover in the Tourism Industry
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: AbstractThis study investigates the role of recognition, rewards, and employee engagement in reducing turnover among hotel employees in Ilorin metropolis. Guided by Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory and Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, the study employed a descriptive survey design using a stratified random sample of hotels with at least five employees. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Findings reveal that recognition significantly lowers turnover intention, rewards enhance employee retention, and engagement strongly influences the decision to remain in the organization. The study concludes that sustainable retention strategies in hospitality must go beyond financial rewards to integrate recognition and engagement practices that address higher-level employee needs

all.title: The Influence of Employee Engagement and Employee Well-being on Service Quality at PT. Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
all.abstract: The present research intends to evaluate the impacts of employee engagement and employee well-being on service quality within PT. Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk. Prior literature has explored the connections among employee engagement, employee well-being, and diverse service-oriented results. Nevertheless, the current investigation concentrates on assessing these two factors simultaneously within the setting of a telecommunications corporation. A quantitative methodology utilizing an associative research framework was applied. Information was gathered via surveys handed out to 100 employees chosen through purposive sampling techniques. The collected data were assessed utilizing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) through the SmartPLS application. The findings demonstrate that employee engagement exerts a favorable and substantial impact on service quality, presenting a path coefficient of 0.526, a t-statistic of 7.216, alongside a p-value under 0.001. Employee well-being similarly displays a favorable and substantial impact on service quality, exhibiting a path coefficient of 0.459, a t-statistic of 6.116, alongside a p-value under 0.001. An R-squared figure of 0.687 reveals that these two constructs account for 68.7% of the variation within service quality. This investigation offers empirical proof regarding the significance of employee engagement and employee well-being in explicating service quality inside a telecommunications enterprise, while supplying perspectives for human resource management strategies directed toward enhancing service quality.

all.title: BEYOND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT: PSYCHOLOGICAL DETACHMENT, WORKPLACE WITHDRAWAL, AND THE PARADOX OF EMPLOYEE WELL-BEING IN MODERN ORGANIZATIONS
all.abstract: Employee engagement is widely treated as an indicator of healthy organizational functioning, yet the language of disengagement can conceal fundamentally different psychological processes. This conceptual review examines the distinction between psychological detachment during nonwork time and workplace withdrawal during work, and considers their relationships with emotional exhaustion and employee well-being. Using a theory-informed qualitative content-analysis framework, the manuscript critically integrates recent peer-reviewed studies and reviews concerning work recovery, job demands, exhaustion, and withdrawal. The synthesis suggests that temporal location, regulatory purpose, degree of volition, and organizational context are essential for differentiating restorative detachment from potentially harmful withdrawal. Evidence on recovery suggests that detachment is associated with reduced strain, although its link to job performance is less consistent, challenging assumptions that all forms of disengagement are detrimental. Conversely, workplace withdrawal cannot be classified as uniformly dysfunctional without considering whether it reflects avoidance, resource conservation, or resistance to unreasonable demands. An integrative framework is proposed to guide future empirical testing and organizational interventions. Because a reproducible database search and full article-level coding have not yet been completed, the framework and themes are presented as provisional conceptual synthesis rather than finalized systematic-review findings.

all.title: The Effect of Work–Life Balance and Employee Engagement on Job Performance: The Mediating Role of Employee Well-Being at PT PLN (Persero) UID North Sumatra
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Management and Accounting (IJEMA)
all.abstract: This study examines the effect of work-life balance and employee engagement on job performance, both directly and through employee well-being as an intervening variable, among employees of PT PLN (Persero) Main Distribution Unit (UID) North Sumatra. A quantitative approach was applied using a five-point Likert questionnaire completed by 294 employees. Data were analysed with Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS, using 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Work-life balance has a positive and significant effect on job performance (β = 0.315; p < 0.001) and on employee well-being (β = 0.425; p < 0.001). Employee engagement has a positive and significant effect on employee well-being (β = 0.500; p < 0.001) but no significant direct effect on job performance (β = 0.113; p = 0.065). Employee well-being has a positive and significant effect on job performance (β = 0.468; p < 0.001). Employee well-being partially mediates the work-life balance–job performance link (β = 0.199; p < 0.001) and fully mediates the employee engagement–job performance link (β = 0.234; p < 0.001). The model explains 77.8% of the variance in employee well-being and 72.4% in job performance.

all.title: SERVANT LEADERSHIP AND JOB SATISFACTION: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT IN ADAMAWA STATE UNIVERSITY, MUBI, NIGERIA
all.venue: International Journal of Entrepreneurship and Forensic Management Research
all.abstract: This study examined how servant-leadership relates to job-satisfaction, employee-engagement as an intervening variable. The study was prompted by concerns regarding satisfaction and engagement in higher-education institutions and the need to examine the influence of leadership practice on employee outcome. A cross-sectional survey design was used, and information was obtained from 279 teaching and non-teaching staff through a structured questionnaire. The result indicated significant positive relationships between servant leadership, and employee engagement. The mediation test further indicated that employee engagement explains part of the relationship between servant-leadership and job-satisfaction. The findings offer useful evidence on the relationship between servant-leadership and employee outcomes. The results suggest that servant leadership is associated with job satisfaction through both a direct pathway and indirect pathway involving employee engagement. Job satisfaction is influenced by leadership practices as well as other conditions within the organisation. The findings indicate the university administrators should strengthen leadership practices that support participation and well-being. Future studies should therefore examine other organisational influences and extend the investigation o other universities.

all.title: Impact of Techno-Invasion on Employee Well-Being
all.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
all.abstract: The rapid development and widespread adoption of information and communication technologies have transformed the way organizations operate and employees perform their work. Digital communication platforms, smartphones, email, messaging applications and online work systems enable employees to remain connected with their workplaces across different times and locations. Although these technologies improve communication, flexibility and efficiency, they may also intrude into employees? personal lives by creating expectations of continuous availability. This phenomenon is commonly described as techno-invasion, an important dimension of technostress. Techno-invasion refers to the experience of being constantly connected to work through technology, resulting in the blurring of boundaries between work and personal life. Employees may receive work-related calls, messages and emails outside regular working hours, including during evenings, weekends and holidays. Such interruptions may limit opportunities for rest, family interaction and personal activities, and may influence employees? psychological and overall well-being. The present study proposes to examine the impact of techno-invasion on employee well-being. A quantitative research design is proposed, using primary data collected through a structured questionnaire administered to employees working in different organizations. Secondary information will be obtained from research journals, books, reports and other relevant sources. The study may employ descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, regression analysis and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM)/PLS-SEM, depending on the final measurement model and sample characteristics. The study is expected to provide insights into the relationship between continuous work-related digital connectivity and employee well-being. The findings may help organizations understand the implications of technology-related work intrusion and develop appropriate digital communication practices, boundary-management measures and employee-support initiatives.

all.title: Financial Literacy as a Cross-Cultural Resource for Employee Well-Being
institutions: Sunan Kalijaga State Islamic University Yogyakarta
all.abstract: This chapter explores financial literacy as a cross-cultural resource that supports employee well-being in contemporary workplaces. Drawing on recent literature from financial literacy, employee well-being, and cross-cultural organizational psychology, it argues that financial literacy extends beyond financial knowledge to include psychological and cultural dimensions. Financial literacy enhances perceived control, resilience, and financial confidence while reducing financial stress and job insecurity. The discussion further highlights the influence of cultural values, organizational practices, and HR systems in shaping employee well-being. The chapter concludes that integrating financial literacy into well-being strategies can strengthen workforce resilience and organizational sustainability.

all.title: The power of perception: the impact of inclusivity policies and diversity climate on employee well-being
all.venue: Equality Diversity and Inclusion An International Journal
all.abstract: Purpose The purpose of the current study is to assess the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being (i.e. life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance). Moreover, we also examine diversity climate as a potential mediator of this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the model of inclusive organizations and the signaling theory, we hypothesized that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies would relate to better employee well-being through a more favorable perception of diversity climate. The sample consisted of 361 faculty and staff from a large Southeastern university. A single-level path-analytic mediation model was used to test hypothesized relationships due to the negligible between-college variance. Findings The results revealed that positive perceptions of inclusivity policies were associated with a more positive diversity climate which, in turn, enhanced certain well-being outcomes – life satisfaction, job satisfaction, turnover intentions and work–life balance. Further, diversity climate mediated the relationship between employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies and employee well-being. Our results highlight the importance of not only implementing inclusive policies but, also ensuring that employees perceive them as fair and effective. Originality/value The current study extends prior research by emphasizing employees' perceptions of inclusivity policies rather than just policy presence. Further, demonstrating the role of diversity climate as a mechanism linking inclusivity policies to well-being outcomes, offers a better understanding of how organizational inclusion initiatives can translate into employee attitudes and health.

all.title: Employee Well-Being in A Philippine Local Government Unit: A Descriptive correlational Assessment
all.venue: Journal of Social Science and Human Research Studies
all.abstract: Objectives: This study assessed the well-being of employees of the Local Government Unit (LGU) of Tanauan, Leyte, Philippines, across six dimensions—psychological, social, workplace, subjective, work–life, and self-efficacy—and tested whether well-being differed by sex and related to age, marital status, and length of service. Methodology: A quantitative, descriptive-correlational design was used. Employing Slovin’s formula at a 10% margin of error, 77 employees were surveyed through a convenience sample from a population of 343 using a questionnaire adapted from the Employee Well-being Scale (Pradhan & Hati, 2019). Data were analyzed with frequencies, means, independent-samples t tests, and Pearson correlations. Key findings: Respondents were predominantly female (55.8%), aged 32– 40 years (29.9%), married (49.4%), and short-tenured (84.5% had served 1–9 years). All six well-being dimensions registered high levels, with workplace well-being highest (M = 4.18) and work–life well-being lowest (M = 3.53). No significant sex differences emerged (all p > .05); age, marital status, and length of service showed only very weak, nonsignificant correlations (all r ≤ .151). Significance: Wellbeing was uniformly high across demographic groups, and the work–life boundary is the most promising target for municipal wellness intervention; the study offers one of the first multidimensional baselines for employee well-being in Philippine local government.

all.title: ภาวะผู้นำกับการสร้าง Employee Engagement
all.venue: Journal of Organizational Innovation and Management
all.abstract: This academic article aims to examine and analyze the systematic relationship between leadership and the creation of Employee Engagement, which is considered a strategic variable directly affecting organizational performance and sustainability within the context of today’s socio-economic environment. Through content analysis of instructional documents and contemporary research studies, the literature review reveals that Employee Engagement is a significant variable reflecting employees’ psychological characteristics, including commitment, dedication, and willingness to perform at their full potential. These characteristics demonstrate a statistically significant positive relationship with organizational performance. Furthermore, the study found that leadership, particularly Transformational Leadership and Servant Leadership, plays a causal role in enhancing engagement levels through several mechanisms, including the creation of intrinsic motivation, emotional and psychological support, effective organizational communication, and the cultivation of meaningfulness in work. In addition, contextual factors such as organizational culture and human resource management policies serve as supporting variables that strengthen and sustain engagement levels over time. Organizations that maintain a positive working environment are more capable of managing engagement effectively. This article also proposes the Leadership–Engagement Integration Model as a new body of knowledge that can be applied in digital-era organizations. The model emphasizes the development of leaders through Agile Leadership alongside the application of technology and data analytics to measure and analyze engagement levels concretely. In conclusion, leadership is regarded as a strategic factor with significant implications for the development of Employee Engagement and serves as a fundamental foundation for long-term organizational success.

all.title: The implications of digital leadership for productivity, innovation, and employee well-being: a systematic literature review
all.abstract: Purpose This systematic literature review examines digital leadership as a socio-technical capability that sustains digital transformation. Grounded in the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model, it examines which employee- and organizational-level outcomes are associated with digital leadership, which mechanisms mediate these relationships, and which contextual factors moderate these effects. Design/methodology/approach Following PRISMA 2020 principles, 47 sources published between 2020 and early 2026 were identified and synthesized, comprising 46 empirical studies and one conceptual-analytical contribution. These 46 empirical studies were appraised for methodological quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Outcomes were classified along the JD-R model’s motivational and health impairment pathways, and methodological appraisal was adopted to interpret the synthesized evidence. Findings Digital leadership correlates with more innovative work behavior, engagement, empowerment, and well-being; lower technostress; and organizational success in digital transformation, agility, and innovation performance. Because the evidence base is predominantly cross-sectional, these relationships are interpreted as correlational. Reported relationships frequently involve psychological empowerment, knowledge sharing, and digital self-efficacy as mediating dynamics, moderated by person–job fit, emotional intelligence, and strategic agility. Research limitations/implications a) 35 of the 46 empirical studies use cross-sectional, self-reported survey designs, which preclude causal inference and thus raise the issue of common method bias. The synthesized conclusions should be interpreted as tendencies of association, not as effects. b) The evidence is unevenly distributed geographically, with China, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Turkey accounting for just over half the sample and Western and high-income contexts represented by only eight studies of heterogeneous design, which limits external validity. c) The conceptual framework is an evidence-informed synthesis, with few studies using longitudinal, dyadic, or qualitative designs, and the proposed mechanisms (both sequential and cross-level) are largely inferential. d) Concepts emerging in AI (AI-savvy leadership and AI use) appear in only three studies and are therefore too early to be included in the framework as confirmed pathways. e) The review examines only English-language studies and overlooks the gray literature. This restriction to English-language publications is acknowledged as a potential source of language bias. f) The original search covered five databases and did not include a systematic backward citation search. g) While the authors present a structured search log to support transparency, they acknowledge that they did not record the exact day in December 2025 when they conducted the search, which restricts full reproducibility. Practical implications 1. Organizations should treat digital leadership as a core socio-technical capability rather than as an auxiliary managerial skill. 2. There is a central role for mediating mechanisms in translating digital leadership into employee and organizational outcomes. 3. There is an importance of organizational support systems in enabling digital leadership to produce positive outcomes. 4. Policymakers and institutional leaders should consider how to balance technological advancement with employee well-being and organizational sustainability. 5. Digital leadership is a driver of psychological, behavioral, and relational conditions that enable employees to engage productively with digital transformation. Originality/value This review is among the first systematic syntheses of the post-2020 digital leadership literature to apply a single integrated theoretical framework (JD-R) across question formulation and interpretation, use MMAT criterion-level appraisal to interpret the synthesized evidence, organize mediators and moderators into an explicit hierarchy and contingency structure, and incorporate emerging artificial intelligence-related leadership constructs. It identifies outcomes associated with digital leadership and the contextual factors under which these associations vary.

all.title: Employee Engagement in Contemporary Organizations
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The present study focuses on the issue of employee engagement. The main objective is to clarify the nature of engagement and determine whether differences exist depending on gender, age, total length of employment, and length of employment in the current organization. The empirical study was conducted among 112 employees using standardized instruments to measure work engagement and organizational commitment. The results indicate a high level of work engagement and a moderate level of organizational commitment. Statistically significant differences were found in certain aspects of engagement depending on age and length of employment in the current organization, whereas no such differences were found with regard to gender and total length of employment. The findings provide partial support for the research thesis and highlight the importance of demographic and employment characteristics in the study and management of employee engagement.

all.title: Job Satisfaction among Dentists by Specialty
all.abstract: Objectives: The aim of the present study was to assess the level of job satisfaction among specialist dentists according to their specialty. Materials and Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 541 specialist dentists completed a validated job satisfaction questionnaire in a dentistry conference held in Tehran in the spring of 2023. The questionnaire consisted of 45 questions in 8 domains (37 questions on job satisfaction and 8 questions about occupational stress), indicating the level of satisfaction based on a 5-point Likert scale. The satisfaction level was determined by adding the weighted scores of each area. The mean job satisfaction score (out of 100) was reported based on demographic factors and specialty. Statistical analysis was conducted using t-test and ANOVA (alpha=0.05). Results: The mean score of job satisfaction was 70±8 (out of 100). Male specialists, those working in the private sector, and those with lower stress scores had higher job satisfaction scores (P<0.05). Job satisfaction had a significant association with age (P=0.039) and work experience (P=0.048). Periodontists and orthodontists had the highest level of job satisfaction while endodontists and pediatric dentists had the lowest job satisfaction level (P<0.05). Conclusion: The level of job satisfaction of dental specialists appeared to be related to individual and demographic determinants (gender, work experience, age, and workplace) and differed based on the type of specialty.

all.title: EFFECT OF HYBRID WORK MODELS ON EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE AND JOB SATISFACTION
all.venue: International Journal of Financial Research and Business Development
all.abstract: The increasing adoption of hybrid work models has transformed contemporary workplace practices by combining remote and on-site work arrangements to enhance organizational flexibility, employee well-being, and business continuity. While hybrid work has become a prominent feature of the post-pandemic work environment, its influence on employee performance and job satisfaction remains a subject of ongoing scholarly debate. This study examines the effect of hybrid work models on employee performance and job satisfaction through a qualitative research approach using content analysis. The findings indicate that hybrid work models positively influence employee performance by increasing work flexibility, improving autonomy, reducing commuting time, and enhancing work-life balance. The analysis further reveals that employees working under effective hybrid work arrangements generally report higher levels of job satisfaction, organizational commitment, and psychological well-being when supported by inclusive leadership, effective communication, digital infrastructure, and equitable human resource policies. However, the study also identifies several challenges associated with hybrid work, including communication barriers, social isolation, technology-related constraints, difficulties in performance monitoring, and concerns regarding career progression and organizational culture. It recommends that organizations develop comprehensive hybrid work policies, strengthen digital competencies, promote inclusive leadership, and invest in employee well-being initiatives to maximize the benefits of hybrid work while mitigating its associated challenges.

all.title: Employee Engagement and Productivity: A Case Study of Mecon Limited, Ranchi
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Employee engagement is vital for organisational productivity in today’s competitive environment. This study examines the relationship between employee engagement and productivity at MECON limited, Ranchi, a public sector engineering consequently. It analyses how leadership, recognition, communication, motivation, and work culture influence employee performance and organisational growth. Most prior studies focused on private manufacturing and retail sectors, while limited research exists for PSUs like MECON limited. Earlier work also studied single engagement factors with narrow practical implications. The study aims to assess the engagement productivity link, evaluate the role of recognition, and understand leadership’s impact on engagement. A descriptive and quantitative design was used. Primary data was collected from 106 employees through structured questionnaire, and secondary data from Journals, company reports and previous studies. Hypothesis testing was done using SPSS and regression analysis. The significance value was p = 0.05, which is ≤ 0.05, making results statistically significant. Hence, the null hypothesis (H₀) was rejected and the alternative (H₀) hypothesis accepted. Findings reveal that higher employee engagement significantly improves productivity, job satisfaction, teamwork, and organisational performance. Supportive leadership, timely recognition, training, transparent communication, and digital HR initiatives boost motivation and commitment. Conversely, high workload, limited growth opportunities and communication gaps lower engagement levels. The study concludes that effective leadership, consist recognition, skill training, and a supportive work culture are essential to enhance productivity and satisfaction at MECON Limited future research can explore digital HRM practises, hybrid work, and cross sector comparisons.

all.title: “The System Says So”: Making Sense of AI-Driven HRM, Conditional Trust and Employee Well-Being in Saudi Arabian Organisations
all.abstract: Purpose This study explores how employees in Saudi Arabian organisations perceive artificial intelligence (AI)-driven human resource management (HRM) and how their interpretations of the technology shape trust in HR systems and employee well-being. Design/methodology/approach: This qualitative study draws on 35 semi-structured interviews analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings: Employees’ perceptions of AI-driven HRM were shaped by transparency, human involvement, and contextual sensitivity. Employees expressed conditional trust in AI used for administrative tasks, but were more reluctant to trust it with consequential decisions such as performance appraisals. Concerns about dignity, autonomy, and mental well-being were closely linked to perceptions of AI-driven HRM as context-blind and overly reductive. Originality/value: By placing employee sensemaking at the centre of the analysis, this study clarifies how AI-driven HRM is interpreted in organisational settings and how such interpretations shape trust and well-being. Practical implications: The study highlights the need for a hybrid HRM model that combines technological efficiency with transparency, contextual awareness, and meaningful human oversight.

all.title: Job Satisfaction in Inclusive Schools - A Systematic Literature Review
all.venue: Herausforderung Lehrer*innenbildung - Zeitschrift zur Konzeption, Gestaltung und Diskussion
all.abstract: Teacher job satisfaction plays a crucial role in enhancing the learning conditions of students. While a rich body of evidence exists from systematic reviews of teacher job satisfaction in general, little is known about teacher job satisfaction in inclusive schools. Given the different working conditions in inclusive schools, they must be examined separately, and such considerations have been minimal. This systematic literature review fills this gap by reviewing extant empirical studies on teacher job satisfaction in inclusive schools. A total of 19 studies were identified in line with the a priori defined inclusion criteria. This review presents aspects of teacher job satisfaction specific to inclusive schools and analyzes the results using qualitative content analysis. Results showed the importance of cooperation as well as school development processes for teacher job satisfaction in inclusive schools. The review further showed a need for further research aimed at distinguishing the relationships between teaching-related factors, non-teaching-related factors, and job satisfaction, as well as the effects of organizational structural requirements. Also, effects of teacher job satisfaction at the student level have yet to be investigated in inclusive schools.

all.title: Learning Agility and Performance: The Mediating Effect of Employee Engagement at TVRI
all.abstract: Amid digital transformation and increasing demands for public-service quality, learning agility and employee engagement have become increasingly important for improving employee performance in public broadcasting institutions. This study examines the mediating role of employee engagement in the relationship between learning agility and employee performance among 650 employees of Televisi Republik Indonesia (TVRI), collected via an online survey across five central directorates and 32 regional stations. Using PLS-SEM with a two-stage higher-order construct approach and 5,000-subsample bootstrapping, the study retained all 52 first-order items, forming 12 dimensions as second-order indicators. All three direct-path hypotheses were supported: learning agility positively affects employee engagement and employee performance, while employee engagement positively affects employee performance and emerged as the strongest path. Employee engagement partially mediated the learning agility-performance relationship. The model explained 10.6% of the variance in employee engagement and 33.1% in employee performance. PLS-Predict and CV-PATS confirmed the model’s out-of-sample predictive relevance and its significant superiority over the indicator-average benchmark. These findings indicate that strengthening employee engagement is a proportionally more dominant pathway to improved performance than the direct influence of learning agility, offering practical implications for HR management in public broadcasting institutions.

all.title: Employee Performance Determinants Using Job Satisfaction Intervening Variables.
all.abstract: The purpose of this study is to conduct an analysis to address the research gap between previous researchers and also the phenomenon where job satisfaction in this study has been modeled as an intervening variable inconsistently as an employee consideration to produce work performance as the problem of this study. This study is a quantitative descriptive study using the Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis method with the LISREL 8.70 application. The research objects used are employees in the Food & Beverage Manufacturing Industry listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The results of the study are that all exogenous variables can significantly explain their influence on endogenous variables. These results are expected to help company practitioners in organizing and also maximizing the availability of their human resources.

all.title: Work from Home: Employee Empowerment a Stimulus of Job Satisfaction
all.venue: American Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Innovation
all.abstract: This study examines the relationship between employee empowerment and job satisfaction among middle managers in various industries in Cebu City. Here’s a breakdown of the study: Determine the level of employee empowerment among middle managers. Assess the degree of job satisfaction among middle managers. Investigate the relationship between employee empowerment and job satisfaction. Descriptive-correlational research design: Used to determine the level of employee empowerment and job satisfaction. Purposive sampling technique: 55 respondents (account managers, channel officers, and team leaders) were selected. Modified survey questionnaire: Used to collect data, with three parts: respondent profile, level of employee empowerment, and degree of job satisfaction. Respondent profile: Majority were over 28 years old, female, single, and had 1-3 years of work experience. Employee empowerment: Respondents were moderately empowered in making bigger decisions and highly empowered in involving people, communicating expectations, and providing training/coaching. Job satisfaction: Respondents were highly satisfied with their salary, commission, job security, working conditions, and status. Relationship between variables: Significant relationships were found between: Age and level of empowerment in making bigger decisions, providing training/coaching, and creating new systems. Gender and level of empowerment in resources management. Age and degree of satisfaction with salary. Level of employee empowerment and job satisfaction (commission, job security, working conditions, and status. The study suggests that employee empowerment fosters job satisfaction among middle managers. The findings highlight the importance of providing autonomy, authority, and resources to middle managers to enhance their job satisfaction and overall performance

all.title: Job Satisfaction Among Secondary School Teachers in the West District of the Schools Division of Cauayan City: Basis for a Proposed Teachers’ Job Satisfaction Enhancement Plan
all.venue: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies
all.abstract: This study assessed job satisfaction among secondary school teachers in the West District of the Schools Division of Cauayan City in terms of work and workplace, benefits and rewards, and recognition. It also examined differences by gender, years of service, and school. The study involved 83 teachers from four secondary schools selected through simple random sampling. An adapted questionnaire provided data analyzed using weighted means and reported tests of group differences. Work and workplace received an overall weighted mean of 3.61 (Strongly Agree), while recognition received 3.28 (Agree). Comparatively lower ratings were observed for institutional benefits, salary fairness, and useful performance feedback. The reported analyses identified no statistically significant differences in work and workplace or benefits and rewards across the respondent groups. However, two administrative recognition indicators differed significantly by years of service (p = 0.008 for each). The findings indicate generally favorable job satisfaction alongside concerns requiring school-level attention. Recommended measures include maintaining professional development opportunities, strengthening instructional resources, providing constructive feedback, reviewing benefits, and applying consistent recognition practices. The study was limited to 83 teachers from four secondary schools in one district; its findings should be interpreted within that setting. Aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education), the study provides a localized basis for decisions intended to support teacher well-being, educational quality, and institutional sustainability.

all.title: Job Satisfaction and Perceived Organisational Performance in Nigerian Commercial Banks
all.venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
all.abstract: Job satisfaction is a well-established work attitude, but its relationship with organisational performance depends on how performance is defined, measured and attributed. This conceptual paper examines the expected association between job satisfaction and perceived organisational performance among employees in Nigerian commercial banks. Drawing on Locke’s value-based account of job satisfaction, social exchange theory and research on the satisfaction–performance relationship, the paper develops a perception-aware, capacity-contingent explanation. It argues that job satisfaction may be associated with cooperative behaviour, persistence and constructive service interactions, but that these behaviours cannot be translated into organisational outcomes without adequate staffing, reliable technology, role clarity and managerial support. The paper distinguishes perceived organisational performance from individual job performance and objective financial or operational indicators, and considers reverse directionality, shared antecedents and common-source measurement as rival explanations. A focused conceptual synthesis is used; it is not presented as a systematic review, and no new empirical data are reported. The principal contribution is a set of bounded propositions that specify when the association may be more or less visible and identify the measurement and research designs needed to test it. The propositions remain theoretical expectations, not empirically established findings.

all.title: LEADERSHIP DYNAMICS AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT: NAVIGATING CONTEXTUAL TURBULENCE IN MYANMAR'S BANKING INDUSTRY
all.abstract: Amidst Myanmar's profound political and economic turbulence, the banking sector faces critical challenges regarding workforce stability and service delivery. This empirical study examines the complex structural relationships among leadership styles, employee perceptions, and employee engagement, as well as the moderating effects of contextual constraints. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, we collected robust data from 400 personnel across domestic and foreign banks in Myanmar through proportional stratified random sampling. Structural equation modeling (SEM) revealed that leadership behaviors significantly shape both employee perceptions and engagement. Crucially, employee perceptions play a robust mediating role, effectively translating leadership practices into cognitive, emotional, and physical engagement. Furthermore, cultural norms and severe political-economic instability significantly moderate this dynamic, emphasizing that leadership effectiveness remains highly context-dependent in volatile environments. Consequently, heightened engagement positively predicts overall job satisfaction. These findings provide a comprehensive contextual framework for human resource management in emerging economies, offering actionable insights for banking administrators to recalibrate leadership strategies, foster supportive perceptual climates, and sustain organizational resilience amidst unprecedented macro-environmental uncertainty.

all.title: Impact of Generative AI Adoption on Employee Productivity and Job Satisfaction
all.venue: Journal of Advanced Research in HR & Organizational Management
all.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools can produce text, summaries, code, ideas and other work outputs, creating new opportunities to change how employees complete tasks. However, the effect of adoption may depend on task type, employee experience, training, trust in AI outputs, and organisational support. This study proposes to examine the relationship between generative AI adoption, employee productivity and job satisfaction among employees in selected organisations in Andhra Pradesh, India. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design is proposed, using a structured questionnaire and five-point Likert scales. GenAI adoption is treated as the main independent variable, employee productivity and job satisfaction as outcome variables, and AI literacy, perceived usefulness, and organisational support as potential explanatory factors. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation and regression are proposed for analysis; mediation or moderation tests may be used if justified by the final model and sample size. This document provides a research framework and data-collection plan. No empirical findings are claimed because respondent data have not yet been supplied.

all.title: Empowering Academic Workforce for Sustainable Development: Employee Well-Being, Empowerment, and Organizational Support as Drivers of Faculty Retention in Indian Higher Education Institutions
all.abstract: Faculty retention in institutions of higher education in India is a high-stakes, under-theorized, instrument to achieving the Sustainable Development Goal 4, which focuses on quality, inclusive, and equitable education, as well as on providing sufficiently qualified teachers in developing countries. This study forms and empirically tests a combination of models that employee well-being has its impact on faculty retention through the psychological and structural empowerment, which is mediated by a perceived organizational support. Using the survey data collected among the faculty of the institutions of higher learning in India and the partial least squares structural equation modelling, the research establishes that the psychological safety and the perceived institutional support play an important role in supporting the affective commitment which turns out to be the strongest predictor of intention to remain. Only the affective commitment provides complete mediation between institutional conditions and retention intentions wherein faculty are willing to stay mainly because they feel trusted, heard and cared about, and not necessarily because of work-load factors or professional relevance. These results theorise retention as a relationship and emotional process and suggest that low-cost solutions based on participatory governance, error management that is non-punitive and regular support may make a significant, longstanding retention impact in resource-constrained institutions.

all.title: Factors Influencing Employee Productivity and Job Satisfaction in the Technology Industry
all.abstract: The information technology (IT) sector continues to experience declining employee productivity and job satisfaction, a trend linked to inconsistent human resource (HR) policy execution, limited leadership adaptability, and insufficient professional development. This qualitative single-case study explored the factors shaping these outcomes within a California-based technology company through semi-structured interviews with 15 IT professionals, triangulated with a Likert-scale survey and organizational document review. Thematic analysis revealed seven interrelated themes: variability in job satisfaction, inconsistent HR policy execution, leadership visibility and responsiveness, change management practices, recognition and reward gaps, career growth and mentorship deficits, and the dual effect of workplace flexibility on culture and technostress. Findings indicated that the core problem was not an absence of policy but a syndrome of execution failures compounded by a deficit in adaptive leadership. The study proposes a four-pillar framework (standardizing HR policy delivery, cultivating adaptive leadership, formalizing recognition and career pathways, and deliberately managing workplace flexibility) to help chief information officers and human resource directors reverse these trends. Biblical principles of servant leadership, purposeful work, equitable stewardship, and rest reinforce the practical recommendations, illustrating the convergence of scriptural wisdom and organizational science. The study contributes context-specific, actionable insight for technology leaders seeking to strengthen retention, well-being, and organizational performance.

all.title: Organizational Identification as a Mediator between Perceived Job Performance, Pro-Environmental Behaviors and Employee Well-being: Evidence from Vietnam’s Textile Industry
all.venue: Advances in economics, business and management research/Advances in Economics, Business and Management Research
all.abstract: This study investigates the relationships among organizational identification, perceived job performance, pro-environmental behaviors, and employee well-being in the textile industry in HCMC, VN. In light of the increasing emphasis on sustainable human resource development and environmental responsibility, the research explores how these factors interact, with particular attention to the mediating role of organizational identification. A mixed-method approach was employed. The qualitative phase included a literature review and in-depth interviews to refine measurement scales and validate the conceptual framework. The quantitative phase utilized a structured survey administered to 718 employees from textile enterprises in HCMC. Data were collected via both online and paper-based questionnaires and analyzed using SPSS 26.0 and Smart-PLS software. Analytical methods included Cronbach’s Alpha, PLS-SEM for assessing reliability and validity, Bootstrapping for hypothesis testing, and Independent-Samples T Tests for group comparisons. The results demonstrate significant positive relationships among the four core variables. Notably, organizational identification was found to mediate the relationship between perceived job performance and pro-environmental behaviors. These results highlight the combined influence of perceived job performance, organizational identification, and pro-environmental behaviors on employee well-being. Organizational identification emerges as a powerful bridge linking performance with environ-mental engagement. For textile industry leaders, this reveals a strategic path: foster identification, and both green behavior and well-being follow. By integrating sustainability into human resources practices, organizations can unlock dual gains—people and planet. This study opens new avenues for sustainable work-force development in one of Vietnam’s most dynamic yet challenging industries.

all.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on employee engagement and performance in Chinese trading firms
all.abstract: With the increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into business operations, its impact on employees and workplace outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how AI Training and Development and STARA Awareness influence Employee Engagement and Employee Performance in Chinese trading firms, with Employee Engagement serving as a mediating mechanism. Using a quantitative cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 265 employees working in Chinese trading firms and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that both AI Training and Development and STARA Awareness have positive and significant effects on Employee Engagement. Employee Engagement also has a positive and significant effect on Employee Performance. Furthermore, the mediation analysis shows that Employee Engagement significantly mediates the relationships between AI Training and Development and Employee Performance, as well as between STARA Awareness and Employee Performance. These findings suggest that organizational initiatives related to AI can contribute to stronger employee performance by enhancing employees' technological readiness, awareness, and engagement. The study provides practical implications for Chinese trading firms by emphasizing the importance of AI-related training and employee awareness while maintaining employee engagement during technological transformation. The study also contributes to the literature by highlighting Employee Engagement as an important mechanism linking AI-related organizational factors with employee performance outcomes.

all.title: No exit, still loyal? Kinship employee engagement in the face of psychological entrapment
all.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how toxic leadership and interpersonal conflict are associated with knowledge hiding through psychological entrapment among creative industry MSME employees and investigates financial vulnerability as an intensifier of entrapment and kinship employee engagement (KEE) as a culturally embedded factor that may weaken knowledge hiding. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 317 employees of creative MSMEs in Lampung, Indonesia, using purposive sampling. Hypotheses were tested with covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). Findings Toxic leadership and interpersonal conflict are positively associated with psychological entrapment, which in turn is positively associated with knowledge hiding. Mediation occurs for toxic leadership but not for interpersonal conflict. Financial vulnerability strengthens the positive associations of both predictors with entrapment, while KEE weakens the positive association between entrapment and knowledge hiding. Research limitations/implications Several limitations should be considered when interpreting these findings. First, the cross-sectional design limits firm conclusions about causality. Future studies using longitudinal or diary methods could better reveal how psychological entrapment forms and changes over time within MSMEs. Second, the use of self-reported data may introduce perceptual bias. However, the presence of interaction effects, which are generally less sensitive to such bias, reduces this concern to some extent. Practical implications MSME owners and managers should reduce dominating leadership practices, manage interpersonal tensions and enhance employee security. Strengthening kinship-based engagement is a culturally aligned strategy to maintain cooperative knowledge exchange. Social implications By showing how economic vulnerability and relational climate shape defensive behaviors, this study supports the development of healthier work communities where solidarity and mutual care discourage knowledge withholding Originality/value This study examines psychological entrapment as a potential mechanism linking relational adversity to knowledge hiding in MSMEs, while integrating financial vulnerability and KEE as contextual moderators.

all.title: ADAPTIVE ORGANIZATIONAL CULTURE AND EMPLOYEES' ENGAGEMENT IN IMO STATE PRIVATE FIRMS
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The study investigated adaptive organizational culture and employees’ engagement in Imo State private firms. It specifically examined open communication, employee empowerment, and leadership engagement and their correlation with employee engagement. The study employed a correlational research design. Due to infinite nature of the population of the study, 385 employees were sampled with the aid of Cochran’s formula of sample size determination.
