The sample size was taken with the use of convenient sampling technique. The instrument used for data collection was a structured questionnaire. The instrument was validated by professionals in the field of management sciences, and their comments were considered in the final draft of the instrument. The reliability of the instrument was determined with test re-test which yielded a coefficient of 0.88. Data was collected through physical contact with the respondents. Data collected was analysed with Mean (x̄), Standard Deviation (SD), and Pearson Product Moment Correlation Co-efficient (r). Analysis of the data collected revealed that open communication, employee empowerment, and leadership engagement to a very large extent positively relate to employee engagement. Based on the findings, it was recommended that: rigid top-down communication should be replaced with practical tools like routine town hall meetings, suggestion boxes, and open-door policies to build trust; employees should be given a stronger sense of ownership by involving them in goal-setting and granting them the freedom to manage their tasks; and managers should be trained to move away from passive oversight and instead work alongside their teams, provide active support, and openly recognize contributions. Keywords: Adaptive Organizational Culture, Employee Engagement, Open Communication, Employee Empowerment, and Leadership Engagement. Title: ADAPTIVE ORGANIZATIONAL CULTURE AND EMPLOYEES’ ENGAGEMENT IN IMO STATE PRIVATE FIRMS Author: Joseph Odia, Isioma Chris Ugocha, Uzoeshi Dorcas Oghale International Journal of Novel Research in Marketing Management and Economics ISSN 2394-7322 Vol. 13, Issue 3, September 2026 - December 2026 Page No: 62-70 Novelty Journals Website: www.noveltyjournals.com Published Date: 18-November-2026 DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24338763 Paper Download Link (Source) https://www.noveltyjournals.com/upload/paper/ADAPTIVE%20ORGANIZATIONAL%20CULTURE-18112026-2.pdf

all.title: ‘Datafied' Employees in Remote Work
all.abstract: This chapter examines remote work as a reorganisation of the labour process that extends workplace surveillance into the home, challenging accounts of telework that emphasise autonomy and flexibility on the grounds that direct supervision has receded while overlooking the extent to which domestic space is itself reorganised by the demands of digitally mediated labour. Bossware and activity logging operate alongside videoconferencing and expectations of permanent responsiveness, so these technologies do not simply observe work at a distance but make visibility and self-presentation conditions of participation in work itself, reshaping working time as well as the worker’s use of domestic space. The chapter also stresses that these burdens are unevenly distributed, since care responsibilities and housing conditions affect workers’ capacity to meet the visual and temporal demands of telework, while racialised norms of professionalism and, for some workers, exposure to domestic violence further complicate the apparently neutral extension of managerial visibility into the home.

all.title: TRABALHO REMOTO E HÍBRIDO: IMPACTOS NA GESTÃO DE PESSOAS
all.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
all.abstract: This article addresses the impacts of remote and hybrid work on human resource management and team performance in organizations. Driven by technological advances and the COVID-19 pandemic, work flexibilization required companies to adapt to new management models. The study analyzes strategies that enable remote and hybrid work without compromising productivity and collective performance. Results show both positive impacts and challenges for employees and organizations, emphasizing the need for strategic adaptation.

all.title: The Social Structure of Remote Work: Trust and Autonomy
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Abstract: The rapid expansion of remote work is transforming the social structure of organizations by reshaping relationships between workers and their employers. Although remote work offers greater flexibility and productivity, digital surveillance raises concerns about employee autonomy, privacy, and workplace trust. Drawing upon Transaction Cost Economics, Principal-Agent Theory, and the Human Capital Perspective, this paper assesses the balance between workplace flexibility and organizational control. It argues that digital monitoring of employees’ activities may undermine trust, motivation, and creativity, whereas outcome-based evaluation of employees greatly motivates them. Furthermore, it argues that trust, as productive social capital, strengthens organizational commitment, collaboration, and human capital development. Finally, the paper proposes a hybrid work model that balances employee autonomy with accountability. Productive remote work requires a shift from intrusive surveillance to trust-based management and performance evaluation, fostering an efficient and human-centered workplace. Keywords: Remote Work, Social Structure, Trust, Autonomy, Digital Surveillance, Human Capital. Title: The Social Structure of Remote Work: Trust and Autonomy Author: Hannah Wang International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research ISSN 2348-3156 (Print), ISSN 2348-3164 (online) Vol. 14, Issue 4, October 2026 - December 2026 Page No: 541-544 Research Publish Journals Website: www.researchpublish.com Published Date: 11-November-2026 DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24137294 Paper Download Link (Source) https://www.researchpublish.com/papers/the-social-structure-of-remote-work-trust-and-autonomy

all.title: Self-Leadership in the Context of Remote Work: Systematic Literature Review
all.abstract: The transition toward remote and hybrid work arrangements has increased employee autonomy while reducing direct supervision, making self-leadership increasingly important for maintaining productivity and employee well-being. Although research on self-leadership has expanded, existing findings remain fragmented across different research perspectives, and comprehensive syntheses focusing specifically on remote work remain limited. This study aimed to examine how self-leadership has been conceptualized in remote work settings, identify existing research gaps, and propose directions for future research. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 reporting guidelines. Relevant articles were retrieved from the Scopus database using combinations of self-leadership-related terms (self-leadership, self-management, self-direction, and self-regulation) and remote work-related terms (remote work, work from home, telework, and hybrid work). The search was restricted to English-language, open-access articles published between 2022 and 2026. Of the 1,423 records initially identified, 13 articles met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed through descriptive and narrative synthesis. The findings revealed that self-leadership in remote work settings was conceptualized through several interrelated dimensions, including self-regulation, self-management, self-directed goal setting, self-monitoring, self-reward strategies, and self-care. These dimensions reflected individuals' abilities to regulate their behavior, manage work responsibilities independently, and maintain psychological well-being in highly autonomous work environments. However, conceptual inconsistencies persisted, particularly because related constructs were frequently used interchangeably across studies. Key research gaps included the limited use of longitudinal research designs, the geographical concentration of studies in European contexts, and insufficient differentiation between self-leadership and related psychological and behavioral constructs. Future research should establish clearer conceptual and operational boundaries for self-leadership, incorporate more diverse geographical and cultural contexts, and adopt longitudinal approaches to examine the development and effectiveness of self-leadership strategies in increasingly flexible work environments.

all.title: REMOTE WORK AUTONOMY AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT: EVIDENCE FROM KNOWLEDGE-BASED ORGANIZATIONS
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Whether autonomy in remote and/or hybrid work arrangements is a positive attribute of employee engagement is still under-explained. This study investigates the relationship between autonomy in the telework and involvement of teleworkers and tests the psychological empowerment as an explanatory mechanism. A three-wave time-lagged quantitative design is suggested to gather data from the knowledge workers from different organisations. The first Wave is about the autonomy of remote work, to the second Wave about psychological empowerment, and to the third Wave about employee engagement. Partial least squares (PLS) structural equation modeling in Smart PLS is used to evaluate the measurement and structural models, such as assessing reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, path coefficients, bootstrapped indirect effects, and explained variance, etc. Common-method bias is minimised and more time is allowed between the predictor and outcome variables. The study adds to the remote-work research by uncovering how flexibility in where, when, and how (WWH) work is completed can impact employees' sense of competence, impact, meaning, and self-determination, and consequently their engagement with the work. Keywords: Remote work autonomy; employee engagement; knowledge workers; psychological empowerment; time-lagged design; PLS-SEM; Smart PLS

all.title: Remote Work Barriers and Their Impact on IT Industry of Pakistan
all.abstract: This study aims at investigating the role of technological, organizational, environmental and psychosocial barriers on the engagement and sustainability of remote work among IT professionals in Pakistan, and at the same time explore the mediation role of remote work engagement and the moderation role of digital self-efficacy. The quantitative research design with cross-sectional type was applied and data were collected using a structured questionnaire with 302 respondents. Reliability tests, correlation, regression, mediation and moderation were used in analyzing the data. The results showed that when all four categories of barriers were taken into account, there were significant and negative relationships between organizational/social barriers and remote work engagement. Positive prediction for performance sustainability was achieved from remote work engagement, and organizational barriers showed significant negative association with performance sustainability. The mediation analyses revealed partial mediation for all four barrier categories between the variables and performance sustainability. Moreover, digital self-efficacy positively moderated the relationship between remote work engagement and performance sustainability as well. The study emphasizes the need to address organizational and psychosocial factors, to enhance employee commitment, and to build up digital skills to ensure high sustainable performance in remote and hybrid jobs.

all.title: Improving Employee Performance Based On Work From Home and Work Flexibility With Job Satisfaction as A Mediation Variable
all.venue: International Journal of Science and Environment (IJSE)
all.abstract: This study aims to analyze the improvement of employee performance based on Work From Home (WFH) and work flexibility with job satisfaction as a mediating variable in the manufacturing industry in Jakarta. The study used a quantitative approach involving 155 respondents. Data analysis was conducted using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method through the SmartPLS 4 application. The results showed that WFH had a positive and significant effect on employee performance (β = 0.214; p = 0.002). Work flexibility also had a positive and significant effect on employee performance (β = 0.248; p = 0.001). In addition, WFH had a positive and significant effect on job satisfaction (β = 0.384; p < 0.001), as did work flexibility (β = 0.381; p < 0.001). Job satisfaction was proven to have a positive and significant effect on employee performance (β = 0.438; p < 0.001). Mediation testing showed that job satisfaction mediated the effect of WFH on employee performance (β = 0.168; p < 0.001) and the effect of work flexibility on employee performance (β = 0.167; p < 0.001). These findings confirm that flexible work arrangements and job satisfaction are important aspects in supporting improved employee performance in the manufacturing industry.

all.title: Remote Work, Psychological Capital, and Employee Motivation: The Moderating Effect of Job Mobility
all.venue: The Journal of Economic Research & Business Administration
all.abstract: With the development of merging working model, especially remote work, there are more managers start to thinking about how to maintain sufficient motivational level in the new circumstance. Although prior studies have revealed both positive and negative effects that brought by remote work, mechanisms of influence that employee motivation brought by remote work is still worth to be focused. Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study works on examining how remote work influence employee motivation through psychological capital by developing a moderated mediation model. It also tests the moderating role of job mobility at the same time. Considering that remote work is a relatively abstract work arrangement, which is difficult to quantify directly, this study tend to use the remote work engagement to operationalizes remote work, so that to better quantify remote work. As long as employee remote work engagement shows employees’ behavioral responses in terms of effort, focus, and task involvement under remote working conditions. Based on survey data from 406 respondents across multiple industries in China, the study figures out that remote work (as reflected by remote work engagement) has a significant positive effect on employee motivation. Psychological capital mediates the relationship between remote work and employee motivation partially. The study shows that employees develop stronger psychological resources if they are more engaged in remote work, so that to enhance their motivation. Furthermore, job mobility positively moderates the relationship between remote work and psychological capital. The effect brought by remote work becomes stronger when perceived job mobility is higher. This study contributes to the literature by clarifying the behavioral mechanism between remote work and employee motivation, explaining role of psychological capital and job mobility in this process at the same time. The study also provides useful insight for organizations to optimism employee motivation under the circumstance of remote work. Keywords: remote work; remote work engagement; employee motivation; psychological capital; job mobility; self-determination theory

all.title: Residential relocation and commuting distance under hybrid work in Paris and London
all.venue: Transportation Research Part D Transport and Environment
all.abstract: This article examines the relationship between telework, residential relocation, and commuting distance within large metropolitan areas, using 2023 survey data from Paris and London (N = 583). Focusing on workers who relocated between March 2020 and 2023, it applies structural equation modelling to jointly account for pre-pandemic residential location, workplace location, telework frequency, and commuting outcomes. The results show that telework is associated with residential decentralisation in London and with longer commuting distances in Paris once initial spatial configurations are controlled for. Residential relocation and commuting patterns are strongly path-dependent and primarily structured by prior residential and workplace locations. In Paris, teleworkers’ longer commuting distances partly reflect selection into telework among workers already facing long commutes, and partly relocations that increase the distance to the workplace without increasing distance to the centre. Overall, the findings qualify rebound-effect interpretations of telework and suggest that hybrid work primarily affects transport demand through reduced trip frequency, which longer commutes only partly offset.

all.title: Beyond location: how workplace resources and empowerment drive organisational outcomes in hybrid work
all.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a holistic model to explain how workplace satisfaction, work activities and time allocation between home and office shape individual and organisational outcomes in hybrid work settings. The model integrates insights from social exchange theory, person–environment fit theory and the job demands–resources model to explain how workplace resources and workplace experiences shape organisational outcomes in hybrid work settings. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 10,923 hybrid knowledge workers from ten public organisations in the Netherlands was analysed using path analysis to examine relationships among personal characteristics, workplace satisfaction, work activities, work location allocation and outcomes including creativity, collaboration, performance, commitment and sense of community. Findings Time spent at home or in the office was only weakly associated with outcomes, although greater office presence predicted higher individual performance. Psychosocial workplace satisfaction was the strongest driver of creativity, collaboration, performance and commitment. Psychological empowerment was a key overall predictor, while physical workplace satisfaction supported outcomes indirectly by enhancing psychosocial conditions. Routine, focused and collaborative work activities were linked to outcomes too, highlighting the importance of aligning resources with tasks rather than location. Organisational outcomes were positively interrelated. Originality/value This study demonstrates that psychosocial resources and empowerment are more critical than physical presence in hybrid work. Findings inform strategies that balance flexibility with opportunities for in-person collaboration to optimise employee performance, engagement and organisational outcomes.

all.title: Hybrid Work Arrangements and Employee Engagement in Insurance Companies in Rivers State, Nigeria
all.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
all.abstract: The study examined the relationship between hybrid work arrangements and employee engagement in public universities in Rivers State, Nigeria. Specifically, the study sought to examine the relationship between hybrid work arrangements and the measures of employee engagement in public universities in Rivers State, Nigeria. This study employed a cross-sectional research design. There is a total of number of one hundred and eighteen (118) insurance firms in Rivers State as obtained from the Yellow Pages Directory of Rivers State Ministry of Commerce and Industry (See Appendix III). The population of this study consisted of 810 staff of fifteen (15) insurance firms in Rivers State. The sample size of the study was 267 obtained from taro yamen formula at 5% error tolerance and 95% level of confidence. Instrument used for data collection was primarily questionnaire. Mean, standard deviation and frequencies were employed in demographic and univariate analysis. Pearson Product Moment Correlation was used for the bivariate analysis to the establish the relationship between predictor and the criterion variables of the study. The study found that hybrid work arrangements positively influence the various facets of employee engagement. Specifically, hybrid work arrangements were found to be strong drivers of higher levels of dedication, vigour and absorption among employees in these insurance companies. The study concludes that employees working under hybrid arrangements demonstrate strong dedication, vigour and absorption in insurance firms in Rivers State Nigeria. Based on this, the study recommended that Management in insurance firms in Rivers State, Nigeria should provide the right digital tools and skill development that enable seamless work regardless of location. By doing this, employees can maintain performance quality and team cohesion regardless of where they work.

all.title: Realizing the value of people analytics: How and when it improves performance
Competency Assessment of Nursing Staff Using Talent Analytics in Healthcare
all.venue: Jharkhand Journal of Development and Management Studies
all.abstract: This study aims to explore the competencies of nursing staff by employing talent analytics in a NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers) – accredited private multispecialty hospital in Ranchi and to identify priority areas for skill development. A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among 191 nurses at one hospital using digital competency assessment tools that covered technical skills, infection control, communication, digital literacy, and emergency response. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation. The major findings of the study were that overall competency was satisfactory, but notable differences were observed across departments. Technical skills and communication emerged as strengths, while digital literacy was the weakest domain across units. The number of years of experience showed a weak positive, but statistically insignificant relationship with overall competency, though patterns varied by department. The study shows how talent analytics can provide actionable insights for competency monitoring, targeted training and evidence-based workforce planning in the healthcare sector.

all.title: Navigating the maze: HR analytics on firm performance and the mediating role of business process performance
all.venue: Evidence-based HRM a Global Forum for Empirical Scholarship
all.abstract: Purpose The study aimed to examine the direct and indirect influence of human resource analytics (HR analytics), comprising high-quality data (HQD), analytical competencies (AC) and strategic ability to act (SAA), on firm performance (FP) through business process performance (BPP). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through a structured questionnaire from a sample of 300 HR professionals of varied industries in India. A two-stage approach was utilized for assessing scale reliability and validity through confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling to test the proposed hypotheses. Findings The results indicate that AC and SAA positively influence BPP and firm performance. BPP mediates the relationship between HQD and AC on FP. However, the mediating influence of BPP on the SAA-to-FP relationship was not significant. The results lend support for the use of HR analytics for enhancing BPP and FP. Practical implications The hypothesized finding recommends that the integration of HR analytics by HR practitioners and HR managers in organizations will promote business process effectiveness and enhance FP. Originality/value The study contributes to the sparse evidence of the value creation of HR analytics capabilities (HQD, AC and SAA) on BPP and FP, extending the theoretical logic of the resource-based view, dynamic capability and knowledge-based view. Further, it advances the literature by examining the mediational mechanism of BPP on FP. The results extend valuable insights for HR managers and practitioners to formulate strategies for effective utilization of HR analytics for organizational outcomes.

all.title: A Bibliometric Analysis of People Analytics and its Impact on Human Resource Development
all.abstract: This paper reviews the evolution and the current state of research in Human Resource Analytics. It focuses on the development of ideas and theories in this field over time. The quantitative bibliometric analysis of the investigation is carried out with the help of Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny software to search through research articles in the Scopus database between the years 2014 and 2024, and 504 articles were identified initially, of which 209 were selected by using inclusion and exclusion criteria. The paper determines notable authors, journals, co-authorship groups, and dominant themes in this field. Organizations also find it informative to develop effective and sustainable HR Anlytics (HRA) systems to make more effective decisions and empower employees. This study aids in comprehending how trends of publications, referencing and collaboration between scholars and research in HRA has evolved over the years.

all.title: The Effects of AI Readiness, HRM Practices, and Continuous Learning Culture on HR Analytics Capability in Public Service Organizations
all.venue: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
all.abstract: The study aims to investigate the effect of AI Readiness, HRM Practices and Continuous Learning Culture to HR Analytics Capability in public sector enterprises in Indonesia. The research was conducted based on a quantitative approach and the survey technique. The research participants consisted of the workers of public sector organizations who have expertise in the use of digital information systems and management of personnel data. The data were collected using an online questionnaire through Google Forms. The questions used a five-point Likert scale. The sampling technique used purposive sampling. Multiple linear regression was used to explore HR Analytics Capability in relation to the three independent variables. The proposed study model indicates that AI Readiness, HRM Practices and Continuous Learning Culture are positively related to HR Analytics Capability. AI Readiness is expected to have the highest relative impact. Artificial intelligence preparation may enhance the organizational capacity to integrate, analyze and use personnel data. Quality information is available with good human resource management practices. Moreover, a culture of continuous learning promotes the enhancement of employees’ analytical skills, teamwork and flexibility. The report provides practical implications for public service companies in terms of the value of strengthening AI infrastructure, data quality, digital competences, human resource management practices and promoting a culture of continuous learning for achieving HR Analytics Capability.

all.title: Sustainable HRM for Organizational Performance and Sustainable Development: The Moderating Role of Analytics
all.abstract: Sustainable HRM and the associated concepts such as Green HRM and Social HRM, are gaining much prominence in contemporary strategic as well as scholarly discussions owing to their association with organizational performance. Owing to the various socio-economic and environmental challenges, organizations worldwide are expected to align their strategies and practices towards the accomplishment of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Data analytics implementation too, is garnering both business and research interest owing to its positive contribution to organizational performance. This paper aims to propose a model connecting all these concepts. Based on an extensive yet focused review of literature, the authors have designed a conceptual model explaining the relationship among sustainable HRM, HR analytics application, organizational performance, and sustainable development. It may be concluded that organizations can boost their performance by implementing sustainable HRM principles and practices while contributing to SDGs. This research also affirms the influence of HR analytics as a moderating variable in the relationship between the comprehensively defined sustainable HRM, organizational performance, and sustainable development. The emphasis is on understanding how sustainable HRM can help organizations improve their performance holistically by satisfying the different stakeholders while contributing to the attainment of SDGs.

all.title: A technical framework for HR-driven imbalanced classification: pipeline architecture, oversampling algorithms, ablation analysis, and threshold engineering for data scientist job-change prediction
all.abstract: Predictive modelling of employee job-change propensity from HR survey data presents a canonical cluster of machine-learning engineering challenges: structured mixed-type inputs with systematic missingness, moderate class imbalance, and self-reported labels susceptible to noise. This paper presents the technical design and implementation of an end-to-end HR analytics pipeline applied to the HR Analytics: Job Change of Data Scientists dataset ( \(N = 19{,}158\) ; positive rate \(\approx 24.9\%\) ). We formalise the leak-safe imbalanced-learn Pipeline architecture that confines synthetic oversampling strictly to training folds and empirically quantify—via a controlled leaky-versus-clean experiment—that naive pre-split oversampling inflates 5-fold cross-validated AUC by 0.014–0.018 units for SMOTE-family methods, a margin sufficient to reverse configuration rankings. Nine oversampling algorithms are instantiated and evaluated across 90 model \(\times\) sampler configurations. A systematic ablation study of the feature engineering pipeline identifies missingness indicator construction ( \(\Delta \textrm{AUC} = -0.008\) when removed) and out-of-fold smoothed target encoding ( \(\Delta \textrm{AUC} = -0.009\) ) as the two highest-value components. HistGradientBoosting on the unaugmented training distribution achieves the highest holdout ROC-AUC of 0.816 [95% CI 0.800, 0.832]; all pairwise sampler AUC differences fall within this \(\pm 0.016\) estimation band and are not statistically significant. With threshold optimisation applied uniformly across configurations, performance differences between the best unresampled and best oversampled alternatives are within the confidence interval (F1 \(= 0.644\) vs. 0.648; \(\Delta = 0.004\) , overlapping bootstrap CIs), though oversampled configurations achieve meaningfully higher recall (73.6% vs. 78.1%). Generalizable engineering recommendations are distilled for HR classification tasks with high-cardinality categoricals, systematic missingness, and self-reported labels.

all.title: Assessing HR Readiness for AI-Driven Talent Acquisition: A Framework for Embedding AI in HR Workflows
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is transforming the face of talent acquisition by replacing conventional HR tactics with intelligent recruiting technologies. Predictive analytics, NLP, and automated screening give businesses more automation. Many businesses want to use AI to maintain their competitiveness, but find it difficult to integrate the tools into a productive workflow. The primary obstacles include data silos, recruiters‘ hostility to algorithmic decision-making, and issues integrating with traditional HR systems. There is a void in the academic literature about organizational readiness, the fit of AI-enabled workflows, and the difficulty of integrating intelligent HR data because previous researches have mostly concentrated on AI adoption intention or initial technology acceptance. This paper proposes a new conceptual model for a systematic assessment of HR readiness for AI integration in the recruitment process based on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) paradigm and Task-Technology Fit (TTF) model. Overall, this paper contributes to the fields of intelligent data systems and AI-driven HR analytics and offers practical insights for ethical recruitment data management and sustainable digital transformation.

all.title: Digital talent management as an organizational capability in the public sector: a systematic literature review and future research agenda
MECHANISMS FOR INCREASING THE TECHNO-ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY OF MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS THROUGH THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF INTERNATIONAL PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT
all.abstract: The digital transformation of international personnel management has become an important determinant of technological productivity, organizational adaptability, and economic efficiency in multinational corporations. The geographical dispersion of business operations, differences in national labor markets, and increasing demand for technological competencies create substantial challenges for traditional human resource management systems. This study investigates the organizational, technological, and economic mechanisms through which digital human resource management contributes to improving the techno-economic efficiency of multinational enterprises. The research employs a structured synthesis of empirical studies, institutional reports, and theoretical approaches to digital transformation, strategic human capital management, and organizational performance. Particular attention is devoted to integrated human resource information systems, artificial intelligence, workforce analytics, digital competency development, international personnel coordination, and performance measurement. The study proposes an integrated techno-economic efficiency assessment framework linking digital HR investments with operational cost optimization, workforce productivity, competency development, and organizational resilience. The analysis indicates that the economic benefits of HR digitalization depend not merely on technological adoption but also on the quality of organizational integration, managerial capabilities, data governance, and strategic alignment. The proposed framework contributes to international management research by establishing a systematic relationship between digital personnel management capabilities and measurable organizational performance indicators. The study concludes that sustainable efficiency improvements require coordinated technological, organizational, and human capital transformation supported by transparent evaluation procedures.

all.title: Big Data Analytics and Its Impact on Risk Management in Financial Investments
all.venue: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
all.abstract: Today, the growth of technology and staying ahead of competitors heavily rely on Financial Information Systems (FIS) and Big Data Analytics (BDA). Increasingly, big data is being used to extract valuable insights from large datasets. In sectors such as e-commerce, data analytics tools improve product recommendations and operational efficiency. Internet businesses often turn to Flink to efficiently manage their vast data centers. This study examines the technological revolution through the IBMQSD framework, distributed computing, and deep learning methods for detailed financial analyses such as stock market forecasting and risk management. It starts with data cleaning and standardization, then uses domain-specific analysis to extract key features related to transportation, HR analytics, and energy trends. Regression Modeling uses tools like the Phillips-Perron test for financial behavior analysis. The Deep Learning Model uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Conventional Neural Network (CNN) for financial risk prediction, while Econometric Modeling analyzes investment-risk relationships for proactive risk mitigation and portfolio optimization. The High-Resolution Imaging Process applies complex algorithms for imaging, and Big Data Processing Platforms, such as Hadoop and Swift, enable fast, secure data management. Data integrity is maintained through reliable storage solutions with the latest encryption features. The result indicates accuracy, loss, data speed and write, resource utilization, precision, recall, and F1-score.

all.title: Prospectiva de la carrera de Psicología Organizacional para el Horizonte 2025–2035: Análisis de los campos académico, científico y profesional en la Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja
all.abstract: Introducción: Los cambios tecnológicos y normativos exigen actualizar la formación en psicología organizacional. Objetivo: Identificar qué elementos curriculares consolidar y qué innovaciones incorporar en la Carrera de Psicología Organizacional de la Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja para el horizonte 2025-2035. Método: Estudio prospectivo, exploratorio-descriptivo, mixto, en cuatro fases: comparación de mallas ecuatorianas con los 26 dominios SIOP/APA, revisión en Scopus y Web of Science con CAGR, consulta a actores clave y convergencia. Resultados: Destacaron IA generativa en reclutamiento (+42 % CAGR), IA y algoritmos en RR. HH. (+28,4 %), People Analytics/Big Data, salud mental laboral (+18,5 %), wearables, Green HRM, resiliencia y Job Crafting; el 38 % de graduados inicia en cargos operativos. Conclusión: El perfil debe transitar de operativo-transaccional a estratégico-preventivo, vinculado al Decreto Ejecutivo 255, el Acuerdo MDT-2025-102 y la Ley Orgánica de Salud Mental de 2024.

all.title: Qualified but Not Quite Employable? AI Uncovers the MBA SkillGap in India
all.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
institutions: University of Petroleum and Energy Studies
all.abstract: An MBA degree is traditionally regarded as a gateway to managerial careers, but does it necessarily guarantee industry readiness? In an era increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and digital transformation, the employability of Indian MBA graduates has emerged as a critical concern. While business schools continue to produce management graduates equipped with academic qualifications and leadership aspirations, employers increasingly demand specialised technical competencies, analytical capabilities, industry certifications, and practical experience. This study critically examines the widening disconnect between what MBA graduates offer and what contemporary employers actually seek, using AI-driven analytical techniques to uncover skill gaps across major management disciplines. The study employs an AI-enabled Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) framework to systematically compare MBA students' résumés with industry job descriptions. The methodological approach integrates Natural Language Processing (NLP), sentiment analysis, topic modelling, clustering, Google Trends analysis, and comparative visualisations to identify patterns in skill representation, employer expectations, and industry-specific competency requirements. Google Trends analysis provides contextual insights into the geographical and seasonal patterns of interest in MBA education across India, particularly in economically active regions such as Delhi, Maharashtra, and Haryana. The findings reveal a notable mismatch between graduate-reported competencies and employer expectations. MBA résumés predominantly emphasise conventional soft skills, including communication, teamwork, leadership, and problem-solving, alongside basic digital proficiencies. In contrast, employers increasingly prioritise advanced analytics, AI-enabled business applications, industry-recognised certifications, domain-specific expertise, and demonstrable practical experience. Functional analysis further identifies distinct competency gaps across Marketing, Human Resources, and Finance. Marketing positions increasingly require digital analytics and AI-supported marketing capabilities; HR roles emphasise workforce analytics, compliance, and HR technology; while Finance positions demand financial modelling, analytical proficiency, and technology-enabled decision-making. Sentiment analysis additionally highlights a contrast between the aspirational language of student résumés and the performance-oriented expectations reflected in job advertisements. The study challenges the assumption that possessing an MBA qualification necessarily translates into employability, highlighting the distinction between academic credentials and industry-relevant competencies. It demonstrates the potential of AI-driven skill mapping and labour-market analytics to support evidence-based curriculum redesign, personalised learning pathways, experiential education, and industry-aligned certifications. By positioning AI as both a driver of changing employer expectations and a tool for diagnosing competency gaps, the research offers actionable implications for management institutions, recruiters, policymakers, and MBA graduates seeking to strengthen employability in India's evolving digital economy.

all.title: Managing Convergence and Divergence in Global HRM Practices: A Strategic International Human Resource Management Framework for Enhancing Multinational Competitiveness
institutions: G.L. Bajaj Institute of Technology and Management Greater Noida
all.abstract: Multinational corporations (MNCs) have been forced by the growing globalization of business to create human resource management (HRM) systems that facilitate both local responsiveness and global integration. This issue has sparked a long-running discussion in International Human Resource Management (IHRM) about how HRM methods differ and converge between nations. Divergence proponents highlight the ongoing impact of institutional, cultural, and legal distinctions on HRM systems, whereas convergence advocates contend that globalization promotes standardized HR practices. In order to improve multinational competitiveness, this conceptual study explores the strategic role of IHRM in striking a balance between convergence and divergence practices. The study creates a conceptual framework that connects the convergence and divergence of global HRM practices with strategic IHRM dimensions, such as talent management, international staffing, leadership development, and cross-cultural management, by drawing on institutional theory, strategic HRM theory, and resource-based perspectives. The study makes the case that multinational corporations are more likely to achieve competitive advantage, innovation, organizational performance, and global responsiveness when they successfully combine uniform global HR practices with localized modifications. By providing a strategic framework that clarifies how global HRM configurations might improve multinational competitiveness in an increasingly dynamic international business environment, the study adds to the body of knowledge on IHRM.

all.title: ВЛИЯНИЕ ЦИФРОВИЗАЦИИ НА УПРАВЛЕНИЕ ЧЕЛОВЕЧЕСКИМИ РЕСУРСАМИ В ГОСУДАРСТВЕННОМ СЕКТОРЕ
all.abstract: The article provides a comprehensive legal analysis of the development of gender equality in international law and European Union legislation. It argues that the contemporary concept of gender equality has emerged through a long evolution of the legal status of women and men: from historical models of legal inequality and limited legal capacity to the recognition of equality as a fundamental principle of human rights, democratic statehood and good governance. The article examines the significance of the UN Charter, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the International Covenants on Human Rights, the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, the Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action, instruments of the International Labour Organization, Council of Europe standards and the Istanbul Convention. Particular attention is paid to EU law, where gender equality is embedded as a value, an objective and a horizontal principle of Union action. The article analyses the Treaty on European Union, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and key EU directives concerning equal treatment, equal pay, work-life balance, gender balance in corporate governance, pay transparency, combating violence against women and domestic violence, and standards for equality bodies. Particular emphasis is also placed on the need to further improve national legal and institutional mechanisms for ensuring gender equality in line with international standards and European Union law. It is concluded that, for Ukraine as a candidate country engaged in EU accession negotiations, gender equality standards have both human-rights and European integration significance, since they form part of the approximation of national legislation to the EU acquis, the strengthening of public administration capacity and the implementation of the state’s international obligations.

all.title: human-resource-management
ABORDAGEM INTEGRADA DE GESTÃO NO SETOR DE SAÚDE OCUPACIONAL: RASTREABILIDADE DE PROCESSOS E GERAÇÃO DE INFORMAÇÕES ESTRATÉGICAS PARA A GESTÃO DE PESSOAS
all.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
all.abstract: This article aims to analyze how the documentation and traceability of processes within the Occupational Health Department can support decision-making in Human Resource Management. An exploratory literature review with a qualitative approach was conducted based on scientific studies, institutional documents, and applicable technical regulations. The findings indicate that properly organized records can contribute to the generation of reliable information. It is concluded that such information can help improve the understanding of working conditions, support strategic decision-making, and inform the planning of actions aimed at protecting and promoting workers’ health in the organizational environment.

all.title: Strategic Human Resource Management in the Development of Institutional Capabilities in Madrasahs
all.venue: At Tadbir Islamic Education Management Journal
all.abstract: The development of institutional capabilities in madrasahs depends not only on the competence of educators, but also on the institution’s ability to organise and utilise that competence through strategic human resource management. This study aims to analyse strategic HRM practices in supporting the development of institutional capabilities at MTs Ma’arif Sidomukti Gresik. The study employs a qualitative approach using a single-case study design. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observation and document analysis, and were subsequently analysed using the explanation building technique. The research findings reveal three main mechanisms: the alignment of educators with academic and religious requirements through planning and recruitment; the development of competencies based on learning needs and assignments through peer coaching and mentoring amongst teachers; and the recognition of contributions through the utilisation of performance evaluation results in the awarding of incentives. These three mechanisms demonstrate the alignment of teacher competence management with institutional needs, although the continuity of decision-making across practices has not yet been fully illustrated. This study concludes that the strategic value of HR management lies in the organisation and utilisation of educators’ competencies in line with institutional needs. The study’s contribution is an interpretative framework for the development of institutional capabilities through strategic HR management that integrates the Ability, Motivation, and Opportunity (AMO) and Resource-Based View (RBV) perspectives.

all.title: Strategic Human Resource Management and Organizational Development
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The convergence of SHRM and OD approaches in today’s environment of growing volatility has become a very important topic for organizations. The present paper offers an integrated approach to understanding the relationship between SHRM and OD approaches in order to address such aspects as workforce capabilities, change and adaptation. Based on the latest literature on the subject from 2021 to 2026, this research aims to develop an integrative theoretical model that considers the impact of strategically oriented HR activities (HR flexibility, technical HRM, and strategic importance of workforce), which result in the emergence of organizational strategic human capabilities that ultimately influence performance. The mixed method research approach including both survey data collected among HR professionals and case analysis will be used. The analysis of four themes, namely, capability emergence, change readiness, integration of digital transformation, and intervention effectiveness, shows that when the alignment of SHRM and OD interventions is achieved, organizations have higher adaptive capacity and employee engagement.

all.title: Sustainable Human Resource Management Practices and Their Contribution to Corporate Social Responsibility
all.abstract: Purpose: This article examines how and under what conditions sustainable Human Resource Management (HRM) practices contribute to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), given that the HRM and CSR literatures have largely developed in parallel.Methodology: An integrative literature review synthesizes research on sustainable, socially responsible, green, and common-good HRM, CSR, and micro-CSR, drawing on stakeholder theory, the resource-based view, social identity and signaling, organizational justice, paradox theory, and institutional theory.Results: Sustainable HRM contributes to CSR through two pathways. It constitutes internal CSR by protecting employee well-being, developing employability, and ensuring fair, inclusive, and voice-based employment. It also enables external CSR by shaping employee perceptions of CSR authenticity, identification, justice, and green climate, and by building organizational CSR capability, legitimacy, and employer attractiveness.Conclusions: These contributions are strongest when HR is integrated into sustainability governance and supported by top management, while mandatory social reporting can drive both substantive change and symbolic decoupling.Limitations: The review relies on purposive source selection, and its framework and maturity model remain conceptual and untested.Contributions: The article offers a comparative typology of HRM approaches, an integrative framework with eight propositions, a maturity model, reporting indicators aligned with international standards, and a research agenda for scholars and practitioners.

all.title: Green Human Resource Management Strategies in the Hospitality Industry: A Systematic Literature Review
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
all.abstract: The hospitality industry faces pressure to balance business growth with environmental responsibility, and Green Human Resource Management (Green HRM) has emerged as a strategy that links HR practices with sustainability goals. This study aims to synthesize recent evidence on Green HRM practices in the hospitality sector, the mechanisms linking them to work outcomes, and the challenges of their implementation. A systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA principles, searching Scopus- and Web of Science-indexed journals published between 2021 and 2026. From an initial pool of 860 records, 30 articles met all inclusion criteria and were synthesized thematically. The findings show that Green HRM practices in hotels generally comprise green recruitment, green training, green performance management, and green reward, which influence environmental and sustainable performance through a series of mechanisms such as employee green behavior, environmental commitment, green knowledge sharing, work engagement, and green innovation. Green transformational leadership and organizational support act as reinforcers, while limited resources and low awareness are the main barriers. This review contributes by mapping the pattern of Green HRM relationships in hospitality and offering a research agenda, particularly for underrepresented local hotels in developing countries.

all.title: Green Human Resource Management Practices and Their Effect on Environmental Sustainability and Food Security in Nigeria
all.abstract: The goal of this research is to assess the influence of green human resource management (G-HRM) practices on environmental sustainability (ES) and food security (FS) in Nigeria. The survey method was used in this study to examine 20 oil firms in the Niger Delta Area of Nigeria. A total of 800 workers constituted the study population from which 40 respondents from each oil firms were selected using convenient sampling technique. From the population, a sample size of 260 workers was chosen based on Krejcie and Morgan's table. This study adopted a questionnaire as the research instrument, and simple random sampling technique was applied in questionnaire administration. The study employed descriptive and inferential statistical methods for analysing data. The results disclosed a favourable influence of G-HRM practices on ES (β = 0.947, t = 73.314, P = 0.000 < 0.05) and FS (β = 0.897, t = 51.281, P = 0.000 < 0.05) and a favourable influence of ES on FS (β = 0.925, t = 47.885, P = 0.000 < 0.05). The study concluded that advancing G-HRM practices can promote the conservation of the environment.

all.title: Sun'iy intellekt texnologiyalarini inson resurslarini boshqarish jarayonlariga joriy etish imkoniyatlari
all.abstract: Maqolada sun'iy intellekt texnologiyalarini inson resurslarini boshqarish jarayonlariga joriy etishning nazariy asoslari, amaliy yo'nalishlari va xatarlari tahlil qilingan. Inson resurslarini boshqarishning rejalashtirish, yollash va tanlash, adaptatsiya, o'qitish, faoliyatni baholash, rag'batlantirish, xodimlarni saqlab qolish va HR-xizmat ko'rsatish jarayonlari bo'yicha sun'iy intellektni qo'llash imkoniyatlari tizimlashtirilgan. Muallif tomonidan har bir HR jarayoni uchun sun'iy intellektdan foydalanish rejimini "avtomatlashtirish – kuchaytirish – inson qarori ustuvor" turlari bo'yicha aniqlash, jarayonlarni ma'lumotlar mavjudligi, vazifaning takrorlanuvchanligi, kutilayotgan samara va xatar darajasi mezonalari asosida ustuvorlik indeksi orqali saralash hamda sun'iy intellektni bosqichma-bosqich joriy etish yondashuvi taklif etilgan.

all.title: Leadership and voice in the future of work: the unexpected cost of empowering HRM practices
Human Resource Management for ESG: A Structured Literature Review and Research Agenda
all.venue: International Journal of Advanced Multidisciplinary Research and Studies
institutions: Hanoi University of Natural Resources and Environment
all.abstract: Purpose: Environmental, social and governance (ESG) commitments are made in boardrooms but carried out by employees. This review asks what the literature knows about how human resource management (HRM) contributes to each ESG pillar, through which mechanisms, under what conditions, and how HRM itself is captured in ESG disclosure. Design/methodology/approach: Guided by the assembling, arranging and assessing stages of the SPAR-4-SLR protocol, we combined keyword searches of Scopus and Web of Science (articles published from 2011 onward) with backward and forward citation chaining and selected a purposive set of 29 core empirical studies, which were coded on HRM stream, ESG pillar, level of analysis, design and context, and 17 prior reviews were used to position the contribution. Findings: The evidence base is lopsided. Over half of the coded studies address the environmental pillar through green HRM, mostly with cross-sectional employee surveys from Asian service and manufacturing firms. The social pillar is studied mainly through socially responsible HRM and employee well-being, while governance appears only in work on ESG-linked executive pay and board diversity. Three streams that rarely cite one another, namely micro-level HRM research, corporate finance studies of employee welfare and accounting research on disclosure, are integrated here into a framework linking HRM architecture, mechanisms, pillar-specific outcomes, disclosure and firm value, with a feedback loop from ESG performance to HR investment. Originality/value: To our knowledge, the review is the first to organise HRM-ESG research by pillar rather than by HR practice and to connect it with the new generation of human capital reporting rules (ESRS S1, ISO 30414:2025, the SEC human capital rule and Vietnam’s Circular 96/2020/TT-BTC). A research agenda of six themes, each with questions, theories and designs, is proposed, with particular attention to emerging economies.

all.title: Integrating Ethics in Zimbabwe's Local Government Human Resource Management Practice
all.abstract: There is limited literature on integrating ethics into human resource management (HRM) in Zimbabwe, despite HRM serving as a moral compass in both public and private organisations. This chapter examines the integration of ethics into local government HRM processes in Zimbabwe under the New Public Management paradigm. It argues that local governments that embrace ethical practices are better positioned to navigate political, social, and economic challenges, while ethical misconduct directly undermines performance and good corporate governance. Using an analytical desk-research method, the chapter contends that ethics can be embedded in human resource (HR) systems to create sustainable, transparent, and morally sound local authorities. It is particularly crucial to infuse ethics into HRM processes to curb operational misconduct, such as nepotism, partisanship, unfair dismissals, and failures, to meet basic employer obligations. Integrating ethics can improve public image, reduce litigation costs, and enhance local authorities’ capacity to deliver timely and effective public services. The chapter thus recommends a systematic integration of ethics into HR functions – recruitment and selection, training and development, performance management, and reward management – to foster ethical local authorities in Zimbabwe.

all.title: Human Resource Management and Pro-Environmental Behaviour of Young People in the Context of Industry 5.0
all.abstract: Industry 5.0 shifts the focus of enterprise transformation towards sustainability and human-centricity. This places new demands on human resource management (HRM), which needs to understand the pro-environmental values and behaviour of young people as the future workforce. The aim of the paper is to identify how young people in Slovakia experience climate change, to what extent their pro-environmental attitudes are reflected in their economic decisions and what this implies for HRM. The empirical basis is an online questionnaire survey of 427 young adults aged 18 to 30 in Slovakia in 2026. Climate change experience is measured by the Climate Change Anxiety Scale, and economic decision-making by willingness to pay more for green products and services, saving for green investments and limiting expenditures due to climate change. Descriptive statistics are used. Young people experience climate change mainly through behavioural engagement in everyday sustainable practices, whereas cognitive-emotional and functional impairment are rare. When saving for green investments, economic motives, particularly reducing household costs and gaining energy independence, prevail over environmental ones, and decisions requiring financial resources are made only by a minority. The pro-environmental economic decisions of the future workforce thus follow primarily an economic logic. For HRM, this implies connecting sustainability initiatives with tangible employee benefits, such as support for green investments or sustainable mobility, and bridging individual values and organisational environmental goals through green HRM practices.

all.title: Human resource management practices in Jordan’s telecommunications companies: the influence of IT determinants, specifically IT knowledge, IT operations and IT infrastructure
all.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings IT knowledge has a significant positive effect on HRM practices, particularly performance management. IT operations have a positive effect on HRM practices, training and development, recruitment and selection and performance management. IT infrastructure has the strongest positive effects on HRM practices, particularly on training and development and recruitment and selection. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

all.title: Generative artificial intelligence in human resource management: a bibliometric analysis and research agenda
all.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), epitomised by large language models such as ChatGPT, is rapidly reshaping human resource management (HRM), yet research at this intersection remains fragmented across management, information systems and computer science. This study maps the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of the emerging GenAI-HRM field and proposes an agenda for future inquiry. Following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 340 peer-reviewed articles and reviews published between 2023 and July 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus database and analysed through bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping, combining keyword co-occurrence, country co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, thematic mapping based on centrality and density, and trend-topic analysis. The results show that the field is young but expanding exponentially, growing from 8 documents in 2023 to 137 in the first seven months of 2026 and accumulating 4,803 citations, with output led by the United States, China, India and the United Kingdom and dispersed across management, information systems and applied computing outlets. Four thematic clusters emerge: AI-enabled recruitment and talent acquisition; technology adoption and acceptance; ethics, bias and governance; and knowledge management and augmented decision-making. The strategic diagram identifies the managerial recruitment-ethics cluster and the technical language-processing cluster as the field's motor themes, while trend analysis reveals a shift from broad conceptual debates towards operational applications and rapidly refreshing model ecosystems. Theoretical grounding remains thin and organisation-level empirical evidence scarce. The study offers one of the first consolidated bibliometric maps of GenAI in HRM, providing scholars with a structured research agenda and offering managers an evidence-based orientation for adopting generative tools responsibly.

all.title: Effectiveness of Human Resource Management in the Warehouse of PT Indotruck Utama, Medan Branch
all.abstract: Kinerja gudang tidak hanya ditentukan oleh fasilitas dan sistem, tetapi juga oleh tenaga kerja yang mengoperasikannya. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan dan menilai efektivitas pengelolaan sumber daya manusia (SDM) di gudang PT Indotruck Utama Cabang Medan, perusahaan yang bergerak dalam distribusi, penjualan, dan layanan purna jual alat berat, truk, suku cadang, dan bus. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Data diperoleh melalui wawancara dengan kepala gudang, dilengkapi observasi lapangan sebagai pembanding keterangan informan, kemudian dianalisis dengan model interaktif (reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan). Efektivitas dinilai melalui enam fungsi pengelolaan SDM (pembagian tugas, perencanaan, penempatan, pelatihan, pengawasan, dan penilaian kinerja) serta tiga capaian operasional (ketepatan pencatatan, ketepatan waktu, dan keselamatan kerja). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa pengawasan, keselamatan kerja, dan ketepatan pencatatan berada pada kategori efektif; perencanaan dan penempatan, pembagian tugas, pelatihan, serta ketepatan waktu tergolong cukup efektif; sedangkan penilaian kinerja perlu diperbaiki karena belum memiliki indikator terukur. Kelemahan utama terletak pada seluruh pekerjaan pelaksana gudang yang bertumpu pada satu karyawan sehingga keterlambatan bongkar muat muncul ketika pengiriman menumpuk

all.title: Rescuing declining schools: A data-driven turnaround strategy through a human resource management lens
all.abstract: This qualitative multiple-case study examines how data-driven decision-making and human resource management (HRM) were understood and used in three secondary schools experiencing decline. Data were drawn from semi-structured interviews with 15 participants, non-participant observations, and school documents. The findings identify four interrelated phases in the schools’ turnaround processes: data-based diagnosis, strategic intervention design, phased implementation, and continuous monitoring. Across the cases, documented practices included the use of performance information to identify school needs, professional development and coaching, performance feedback, staff collaboration, and monitoring of selected indicators. Participants’ accounts suggest that these practices may help connect organizational diagnosis with staff development and school-improvement planning. However, the study does not establish that HRM practices caused improvements in employee outcomes or sustained school recovery. The resulting human-capital-centered model should therefore be understood as an evidence-informed interpretation and a proposition for further application and evaluation, rather than a validated causal model.

all.title: Green HRM Practices and Sustainable Performance: A Case Study of CCL, Ranchi
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The present research study is an exploration into the process of integration of Green HRM strategy and its implications for sustainable performance at Central Coalfields Limited (CCL), Ranchi. As of the leading Miniratna subsidiaries of Coal India Limited, CCL works in the energy intensive field of coal mining, where it is important to make a shift towards sustainability for long term growth and survival. In this respect, the research study focuses on the significant research gap, that is the issue of application of HR measures that are focused on humans. Using, a quantitative approach in research methodology, data was collected using a sample size of 59 employees from the headquarter of CCL in Ranchi. In this analysis, descriptive statistic were used to describe the demographic scenario while inferential statistics, regression analysis were employed to analyse the hypothesis. It was found that there exists a statistically significant positive correlation between GTD and sustainable performance. Important discoveries include the fact that only 18.2% of employees consider Green HRM to be costly affair while 81.8% believe that it is a cost-effective tool. Another, key finding shows that 95.5% of the participants strongly support the idea that green policies are well aligned with company’s core purpose and values. At the same time, the study has found the presence of a perception gap concerning the impact that green activities have on career progress as 47.4% of employees have no clear understanding of how these two aspects are related. Concluding the project, it should be stated that although the company succeeded in cultivating high environmental consciousness among workers, it is necessary to move further and create specific Green HRM and rewarding systems to make CCL the leading organisation in sustainable energy production.

all.title: Decentralized Quantum-Blockchain Ecosystems for Trustworthy Financial Governance and Intelligent Human Resource Management
all.abstract: Quantum computing, blockchain technology, and artificial intelligence convergence create new opportunities to substantially transform financial governance systems and human resource control mechanisms. In this paper, a new decentralized quantum-blockchain ecosystem (DQBE) is presented, which uses quantum cryptography to provide enhanced security, smart contracts to enable autonomous self-governance, and machine learning algorithms to support intelligent decision-making. The issues faced by traditionally centralized systems—such as lack of security, limited transparency, and poor scalability—are addressed by the proposed framework. We use theoretical reasoning and simulation experiments to show that the DQBE architecture is capable of achieving a transaction security level of 99.97%, a governance overhead reduction of up to 78 times, and a 34% improvement in HR decision accuracy compared to traditional systems. With the introduction of quantum-resistant cryptographic protocols, long-term viability against emerging quantum threats is ensured, along with operational robustness in distributed environments.

all.title: Challenges and opportunities in implementing green human resource management in Indian higher education institutions
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Requests are being made on Indian higher education institutions for them to take action on sustainability but it is not a simple task to implement green human resource management (GHRM). This study analyzes the problems and possibilities the employees encounter while implementing GHRM. A cross-sectional survey was conducted on 500 respondents (employees) selected from various central, state, private and deemed universities and colleges by using stratified random sampling and simple random sampling techniques. Eight challenge statements and eight opportunity statements were evaluated on a 5-point Likert Scale by the majority of respondents. Percentages, means and standard deviations were used to analyse the data. Opportunities (average 3.82 (69.9 percent)) were agreed more than challenges (average 3.46 (55.6 percent)). Financial resources were perceived to be the greatest obstacle (3.66 with 64.6 percent agreement) followed by monitoring green initiatives (3.56) and lack of training (3.54). The respondents indicated the least resistance by employees (43.0 percent agreement, 3.16). The opportunities were ranked with contribution to long-term institutional sustainability at 78.0 per cent agreement (4.01), positive institutional image (3.94) and a stronger reputation (3.91). The lowest score was for reducing operational costs (3.56). The findings are based on employees' perceptions, and not on costs or realized benefits. The study contributes employee based evidence of implementation of GHRM in higher education in India. It is not about unwilling staff, it's about resources and systems. Institutions can thus start with incremental budgets, regular green training and easy monitoring instruments, and continue by the deep conviction that GHRM contributes to the sustainable development of the institution and a favourable institutional image.

all.title: Artificial intelligence capabilities and human resource management functions: Evidence from Saudi Arabia
all.venue: SA Journal of Human Resource Management
all.abstract: Orientation: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in human resource management (HRM), yet evidence remains limited on how specific AI capabilities relate to distinct HRM functions in Saudi private-sector organisations. Research purpose: This research explored the connections of knowledge sharing systems, decision support systems and smart systems with recruitment, training and performance appraisal. Motivation for the study: Prior research often treats AI as a broad organisational technology, providing limited insight into capability-specific relationships across HRM functions in the Saudi context. Research approach/design and method: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among workers in private-sector organisations in Saudi Arabia. Purposive sampling, supplemented by snowball sampling to improve access across organisations and regions, yielded 431 respondents. Data were collected electronically between November 2025 and February 2026 using a structured questionnaire adapted from established scales and analysed using structural equation modelling. Main findings: Knowledge sharing systems showed a positive correlation with recruitment (β = 0.784, p < 0.001). Decision support systems demonstrated a positive correlation with training (β = 0.854, p < 0.001). Smart systems showed a positive correlation with training (β = 0.119, p = 0.029) and performance evaluation (β = 0.798, p < 0.001). Other hypothesised relationships were not significant. Measurement model fit was mixed, warranting cautious interpretation. Practical/managerial implications: Human resource decision-makers should consider the functional characteristics of AI capabilities when evaluating their use across HRM activities while maintaining human oversight. Contribution/value-add: The study distinguishes capability-specific AI-HRM relationships and provides empirical evidence from the Saudi private-sector context.

all.title: The Effects of Organizational Knowledge Sharing, Human-AI Collaboration Capability, and Strategic HRM on Organizational Ambidexterity in State-Owned Enterprises
all.venue: Best Journal of Administration and Management
all.abstract: This research aims to analyze the effect of Organizational Knowledge Sharing, Human-AI Collaboration Capability, and Strategic HRM on Organizational Ambidexterity on State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) in Indonesia. The research is quantitative in nature, employing the survey technique and is carried out among the personnel of SOE in a number of industrial sectors. We applied purposive sampling in which the respondents had to be working employees with at least one year of working experience and knowledge of knowledge sharing activities, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, and human resource management practices in their organizations. The data collection is proposed to be done through an online questionnaire by using a five-point Likert scale via Google Form. Multiple linear regression is used for data analysis. The study model presented shows positive associations of Organizational Knowledge Sharing, Human-AI Collaboration Capability, Strategic HRM and Organizational Ambidexterity. This study has practical implications. To help balance exploitation capability and exploration capability, it is suggested that SOEs improve knowledge management systems, human-AI collaboration, digital competencies, strategic workforce planning and innovation-oriented performance management. These three elements are expected to strengthen and improve Organizational Ambidexterity, and through this, enhance competitiveness and support the sustainability of business transformation in SOEs.

all.title: Examining Green HRM Practices towards Sustainability and Circular Economy Using Fuzzy AHP: A Case
all.abstract: The transition from a linear “take–make–dispose” model to a circular economy (CE) requires organizations to integrate sustainability principles into human resource management (HRM). Green HRM practices—such as sustainable recruitment, environmental training, green performance appraisal and employee engagement—play a critical role in embedding environmental responsibility into organizational culture. However, evaluating the relative importance of multiple HR parameters influencing sustainability remains complex due to uncertainty and subjective judgments. This study proposes a Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (Fuzzy AHP)-based multi-criteria decision-making framework to prioritize Green HRM practices contributing to sustainability and circular economy adoption. Data were collected from 50 middle-management employees of Dayal Fertilizers, Meerut. Twelve HR-related sustainability parameters were structured into a hierarchical decision model and evaluated using pairwise comparisons with triangular fuzzy numbers. Results indicate that training and awareness, sustainable recruitment and incentive mechanisms are the most influential drivers of circular economy implementation, while safety assurance and research integration require improvement. The study contributes a quantitative prioritization framework for managers and extends the application of FAHP to Green HRM evaluation.

all.title: The initial steps in succession planning
Implementing and maintaining the succession plan
Touchdown or fumble: strategic talent acquisition in the National Football League
all.abstract: Research methodology This case is based on multiple media reports before and during the Kansas City Chiefs’ 2024 season, specifically in early October 2024, after two of the Chiefs’ wide receivers were injured. Primary sources included YouTube recordings of interviews with Brett Veach, numerous Chiefs’ players and officials, various commentators discussing the team’s activities and the ESPN six-part documentary series “The Kingdom.” These were supplemented with various published, online and broadcast sports reports. The YouTube videos were transcribed using Transkriptor, a web-based AI application. The ESPN documentary audio “The Kingdom” was transcribed from closed caption text. A complete set of references is contained in the case footnotes and the teaching notes’ reference section. Case overview/synopsis Brett Veach, General Manager of the Kansas City Chiefs National Football League (NFL) team, needed to find an additional wide receiver. The Chiefs and most NFL teams typically had six wide receivers on the team. The Chiefs had only four wide receivers in early October after their top two wide receivers suffered long-term injuries and might not play again in the 2024 season. Veach had until the NFL’s November 5th trade deadline to identify a candidate and negotiate a trade with another NFL team. The Chiefs were trying to get to their third consecutive Super Bowl, a first in the NFL and had 12 more regular-season games plus up to three playoff games to play. Could Veach find an available wide receiver that could meet the Chiefs’ on-the-field needs, fit with the Chiefs’ culture and save the Chiefs’ chance at a third Super Bowl by the November 5th trade deadline? Complexity academic level The case was designed for both undergraduate and graduate Human Resource Management courses. The case may be useful in introductory-level human resource management courses, as well as in upper-level talent acquisition or strategic human resource management courses that cover selection. The case has been classroom tested at the undergraduate and graduate levels, in both in-seat and asynchronous online modalities. The case is designed to apply the Attraction-Selection-Attrition (ASA) framework (Schneider, 1987) to guide a selection decision. The case explores three general themes within the ASA framework: understanding overall organizational culture; analyzing organizational skill gaps; and making selection decisions from a pool of imperfect candidates. The case takes a behind-the-scenes look at NFL talent acquisition as an application of the ASA framework.
