all.title: Gestión del talento de trabajadores jóvenes en el sector logístico: el caso español
all.abstract: La incorporación del talento joven al sector logístico constituye uno de los principales retos estratégicos para las organizaciones, en un contexto fuertemente marcado por la digitalización y el cambio generacional. Objetivo: conocer la valoración de las personas responsables de gestionar los recursos humanos acerca de los procesos actuales de captación, gestión y retención del talento de los jóvenes trabajadores centennials y millennials en el sector logístico. Metodología: se empleó análisis cualitativo sobre los datos que se han obtenido a partir de una serie de entrevistas semiestructuradas realizadas a profesionales expertos en la gestión de recursos humanos en el ámbito logístico. Resultados principales: cuestiones como la formación continua, el desarrollo profesional y el employer branding influyen significativamente en la atracción y fidelización del talento joven en la logística. Conclusiones: las empresas han de adaptar la forma de gestionar las políticas de recursos humanos teniendo en consideración las expectativas laborales de los empleados más jóvenes, con el fin de poder cubrir de forma eficiente las vacantes en perfiles técnicos y operativos en los que centennials y millennials tienen una mejor formación que los profesionales de mayor edad.

all.title: Influence of Succession Planning on Service Delivery at Nakuru County Referral and Teaching Hospital, Kenya
all.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN MANAGEMENT FIELDS
all.abstract: Public referral hospitals in Kenya must keep services running while leaders and skilled staff change posts, yet it is not clear how far planned succession supports the quality and timeliness of care. The study determined the influence of succession planning on service delivery at Nakuru County Referral and Teaching Hospital, Kenya. It was guided by Lewin’s Change Management Theory. A descriptive cross-sectional research design was used. The unit of analysis was the hospital, and the unit of observation was the employee. The target population was 968 employees in clinical, allied health, administrative and support categories. Yamane’s formula and proportionate stratified random sampling gave a sample of 283. Primary data was collected with a structured questionnaire on a five-point Likert scale, with open-ended questions to corroborate the ratings. Data was analyzed in SPSS version 29 using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and simple linear regression, after tests of the residuals and of normality. Respondents rated succession planning moderately unfavourably (mean = 2.78, SD = 1.31). Succession planning had a moderate, positive and significant relationship with service delivery (r = .583, p < .001) and explained 34.0 percent of its variance (B = 0.478, t = 10.70, p < .001), so the null hypothesis was rejected. The study concluded that succession planning has a significant positive influence on service delivery, although current practice is informal and reactive. It recommended a documented, merit-based succession framework supported by mentorship and early identification of future leaders. Keywords: Succession planning, service delivery, referral hospital, Kenya

all.title: Synergizing Quantum Computing and Blockchain for Secure Talent Management and Predictive Financial Intelligence
all.abstract: The convergence of quantum computing and blockchain technology presents unprecedented opportunities for revolutionizing talent management systems and financial intelligence platforms. To address the growing need for secure, scalable, and predictive enterprise systems, this research proposes a novel framework that integrates quantum computing capabilities with blockchain security. The hybrid quantum-classical architecture leverages quantum machine learning algorithms, post-quantum cryptographic protocols, and distributed ledger technology, evaluated through theoretical modeling, security analysis, and performance benchmarking. Findings indicate a 340% improvement in predictive accuracy for talent performance metrics and a 280% enhancement in financial forecasting precision compared to classical approaches, while achieving resistance against both classical and quantum attacks and improving processing speeds by up to 450% for complex analytical tasks. These results highlight the transformative potential of quantum-blockchain synergy in delivering next-generation enterprise solutions with unmatched security, computational efficiency, and predictive intelligence.

all.title: Utilization of Corporate Governance in Succession Planning for Sustainable Family-Owned SMEs in Uganda’s Central Region
all.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
all.abstract: The study examined how Corporate Governance Strengthens Succession Planning to promote Sustainability in Family-Owned Small and Medium Enterprises in Central Uganda.Objectives were: to explore how Human Resource policy, organizational culture, and employee engagement influence succession planning for sustainable family-owned SMEs in the Ugandan central region, a case of selected family-owned Enterprises.A mixed-methods research methodology was employed, and data were collected using structured questionnaires from 166 respondents, complemented by key informant interviews held with enterprise owners and managers, to survey governance practices, succession planning, and sustainability indicators.Cronbach's Alpha measured reliability while expert review ensured validity.Correlation and Regression analyzed quantitative data, while qualitative data were thematically analyzed using structural equation modelling.Findings revealed that Human Resource policies significantly predicted successor identification (β = 0.228, P = 0.004) and training (β = 0.121, P = 0.027).While organizational culture supported ethical behavior and transparency, it showed a lower direct influence on sustainability (β = 0.047, P = 0.515).Employee engagement positively predicted successor identification (P = 0.242, P = 0.015), training (β = 0.425, P = 0.001), and sustainability (β = 0.258, P = 0.003); however, a weak influence on communication of succession intent was noted.Corporate Governance indicated a strong positive effect on sustainability (β = 0.492, P = 0.001) while communication of intent emerged was a key predictor (β = 0.209, P = 0.001).Implications for theory and practice indicate that structured HR policies, inclusive governance, and transparent communication are essential for integrating sustainability in family-owned SMEs.

all.title: The Impact of Succession Planning on Enhancing Organizational Reputation: An Empirical Study at Zain Iraq Telecommunications Company
all.abstract: This study measures and analyzes the impact of succession planning practices (top management support, competency identification and talent development and preparation dimensions in Rothwell model) on organizational reputation through its four dimensions (governance, leadership, workplace environment and performance) based on RepTrak framework in Zain Iraq Telecommunications Company. The main problem was reflected in the gap between leadership replacement mechanisms and successor leaders' preparation to respond to the rapid changes that characterize competitive environments in the telecommunication sector

all.title: Dataset for: Inclusive Talent Management for Border-Region MSMEs: A PRISMA 2020 Systematic Literature Review
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This dataset supports a PRISMA 2020 systematic literature review on inclusive talent management in micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), with a focus on border regions. It contains the full Scopus search strings, record counts for each PRISMA stage, Scopus result screenshots, and the authors' coding of all 76 unique articles (2015–2026; 68 synthesised), including evidence category, inclusive-TM evidence, MSME fit, border context, text availability, primary theme, MMAT-based confidence rating, theory codes (TCCM), and coded findings. A five-year subset (2022–2026; 63 unique, 55 synthesised) is flagged in the same file. Author-keyword co-occurrence maps and a codebook are included. No abstracts or full texts are redistributed.

all.title: The Impact of Talent Management Practices on Entrepreneurship A Field Study of Employees at Libya Telecom & Technology in Benghazi
all.venue: Journal of Insights in Basic and Applied Sciences
all.abstract: هدفت الدراسة إلى التعرف على أثر ممارسات إدارة المواهب بأبعادها المتمثلة في (استقطاب واختيار المواهب، وتدريب وتطوير المواهب، والاحتفاظ بالمواهب) في تعزيز ريادة الأعمال بشركة ليبيا للاتصالات والتقنية بمدينة بنغازي. ولتحقيق أهداف الدراسة، اعتُمد المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، واستخدمت الاستبانة أداةً رئيسة لجمع البيانات. وتكوّن مجتمع الدراسة من (320) عاملًا، وبلغ حجم العينة المستهدفة (175) مفردة. وحُللت البيانات باستخدام برنامج الحزم الإحصائية للعلوم الاجتماعية (SPSS). أظهرت النتائج أن المستوى العام لممارسات إدارة المواهب جاء مرتفعًا، بمتوسط حسابي بلغ (3.710)، كما جاء مستوى ريادة الأعمال مرتفعًا بمتوسط حسابي بلغ (3.585). وكشفت نتائج الانحدار المتعدد عن وجود أثر ذو دلالة إحصائية لممارسات إدارة المواهب في ريادة الأعمال، حيث بلغ معامل التحديد (R²=0.479)، مما يشير إلى أن ممارسات إدارة المواهب تفسر ما نسبته (47.9%) من التباين في ريادة الأعمال. كما أظهرت النتائج أن بُعد الاحتفاظ بالمواهب كان الأكثر إسهامًا في تفسير ريادة الأعمال، يليه بُعد تدريب وتطوير المواهب، في حين لم يظهر بُعد استقطاب واختيار المواهب إسهامًا مستقلًا ذا دلالة إحصائية ضمن نموذج الانحدار المتعدد. وأوصت الدراسة بضرورة تعزيز سياسات الاحتفاظ بالمواهب، وتطوير برامج التدريب وتنمية الكفاءات، وتحسين آليات الاستقطاب والاختيار، بما يدعم الإبداع والابتكار والمبادرات الريادية داخل الشركة.

all.title: Digital CSR communication and sustainable talent management discourses on Facebook and YouTube: a computational analysis from Jordan
all.abstract: This study examines how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and sustainable talent management themes are represented and received in public Facebook and YouTube interactions in Jordan. The analysis draws on 34,150 anonymized digital-trace records collected between 1 January and 30 June 2025, comprising 18,430 Facebook interactions and 15,720 YouTube interactions. A computational content analysis design integrates topic-model-derived labels, sentiment scoring, engagement metrics, and a descriptive centrality indicator. Five substantive topics were represented in the corpus, led by sustainable work practices (28.1%) and youth empowerment (22.1%). Sentiment was predominantly positive on both platforms, but the platform difference in categorical sentiment was not statistically significant, χ 2 (2, N = 34,097) = 4.44, p = 0.109, Cramér's V = 0.011. Mean sentiment polarity likewise did not differ significantly between Facebook and YouTube, t (34,148) = 1.45, p = 0.147, d = 0.016. Total engagement was also statistically similar across platforms and content formats. These findings qualify stronger platform-difference claims and suggest that, within this corpus, substantive CSR and talent-related discourse is more stable across Facebook and YouTube than a platform-deterministic interpretation would imply. The study contributes a cautious conceptual–computational framework for examining CSR-related talent discourse in an underrepresented Global South setting while distinguishing digital representations and audience traces from direct evidence of internal human resource practices.

all.title: Using Generative AI to Formulate Small Business Succession Planning Research: An Illustrated Workflow and Proposed Mixed Methods Study
all.venue: International Journal of AI in Pedagogy Innovation and Learning Futures
all.abstract: A business may have written ownership-transfer terms while leaving future leadership authority and essential work unresolved. This methods article illustrates a disciplined use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to formulate succession-planning research: generating alternative definitions, comparing design options, exposing ambiguous survey items, and converting suggestions into researcher-owned methodological decisions. It proposes an explanatory sequential study of privately held U.S. businesses with 5 to 99 employees. The survey measures reported actions across voting ownership, leadership, and continuity of essential work; follow-up interviews explain why preparation advances unevenly across those domains. A worked example separates an outgoing owner’s financial preparation from decisions about the owner’s future role. A draft questionnaire, coding and routing rules, and an integration display demonstrate how the proposed design could be implemented. AI serves as a design aid, not as evidence; the questionnaire and study remain proposed and require empirical testing.

all.title: Tech reports: 2022-2025 S&P 500 (Standard & Poor's 500) executive succession risk share
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: No verified 2022-2025 S&P 500 tech succession-risk share; FTSE 250 formal CEO succession plans stand at 35%, and unplanned CEO exits cost an average $1.2M each. Independent technical note mirroring the canonical version: https://issues.house/blog/tech-reports-2022-2025-sp-500-standard-poors-500-executive-succession-risk-share.php

all.title: Navigating rural idyll rules and farm succession in the 21st century
all.abstract: Farm succession in Australian agriculture extends beyond a business transition; it encompasses social and cultural aspects that can significantly impact farming families and communities. The traditional rural idyll continues to influence succession practices; however, modern challenges including gender equity, climate change, and globalisation can create conflicting pressures on farming families. This research examines these social and cultural impacts to better inform farm support services in assisting farming families through succession planning. A scoping review of peer-reviewed and academic literature published between 2016 and 2026 was undertaken, followed by a reflexive thematic analysis of the scoped dataset. The findings reveal that many farming families face a difficult choice which can impact their mental health: whether to maintain traditional succession norms at the expense of some family members' wellbeing or to prioritise family farm continuity despite challenges stemming from climate change and globalisation. Alternatively, they may consider selling the farm, disappointing potential successors, or postponing retirement. The research demonstrates that while professional advisors typically approach succession through a legal, financial, or agricultural lens, the impacts run deeper than these singular considerations. The study highlights the need for a holistic approach to succession planning which prioritises farming families’ wellbeing.

all.title: When the Founder Is the Franchise: Nvidia's Leadership Crisis and the Price of Key-Person Risk
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Jensen Huang's abrupt exit from the company he co-founded 33 years ago has left the world's most important AI chipmaker searching for a leader. The episode is a case study in succession planning, board independence and key-person risk, with direct lessons for India's founder-led companies. Published in Ahmedabad Business Review, article ABR-2026-0011: https://theabr.in/articles/when-the-founder-is-the-franchise-nvidias-leadership-crisis-and-the-price-of

all.title: Financial Literacy as a Governance-Enabling Capability in Family Business Succession: Evidence from the UAE
all.abstract: This study examines whether financial literacy is associated with formal succession planning, ease of succession, and expected post-succession business performance in UAE family businesses. Survey data from 188 owners, successors, and senior managers are analysed using a principal-component-based financial literacy index. Ordered logistic regression is used to examine formal planning, while ordinary least squares regression is used to assess transition ease and expected performance. Financial literacy is positively associated with formal succession planning and expected post-succession performance. Its direct association with ease of succession is not statistically significant when formal planning and successor preparedness are included. Successor preparedness is positively associated with both formal planning and transition ease, while engagement with external advisers is positively associated with formal planning. The study frames financial literacy as a capability that enables governance and develops a Capability-Based Succession Pathway distinguishing governance preparation, leadership transition, and expected post-succession outcomes. The findings suggest that financial literacy is especially relevant to formalising succession arrangements, whereas transition ease depends more directly on planning and successor preparedness. Practically, integrating financial literacy development into succession preparation may support continuity and wealth preservation. Because the data are cross-sectional and self-reported, causal inference is limited. Future research should use longitudinal, multi-respondent designs and accounting-based performance indicators. JEL codes: G53; M10; M13; G32; L26

all.title: Addressing the inverse training law: developing, sustaining and expanding GP training in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighbourhoods: A Qualitative Study
all.abstract: Background Training in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighbourhoods offers unique educational opportunities for developing competence in navigating complexity, cultural diversity, and health inequalities. The Deep End (DE) Network supports general practices serving the most socioeconomically disadvantaged communities. Despite greater population need, the inverse training law means that registrars have fewer opportunities to learn in these settings. Previous evaluation of the TrainDEEP (TRaining Assistance INitiative in DEep End Practices) intervention demonstrated that investment in trainer development and protected time could successfully establish new GP training practices within DE communities. The intervention has evolved to support training continuity and growth within established training practices. This study aimed to explore how training capacity can be developed, sustained, and expanded in DE settings, while examining the learning experiences and professional development of those involved in training and delivering care in these contexts. Methods A qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with professionals across 8 DE practices in the North East and North Cumbria, England. Participants included GP trainers, intending trainers, registrars, GPs and practice managers. Results 23 interviews were conducted between January-May 2026. Four key themes were identified. (1) Learning in the Deep End described how exposure to clinical complexity, cultural diversity, and health inequalities enhanced learning, while also presenting emotional and professional challenges. (2) Developing and sustaining educational capacity highlighted the importance of protected time, trainer development, succession planning, and organisational support. (3) Preparing and supporting learners in disadvantaged settings identified gaps in training related to health inequalities, consultation skills, and complex biopsychosocial care, alongside a need for enhanced peer support. (4) Influence on professional identity and career intentions demonstrated how DE placements increased confidence in working with underserved populations and, for some trainees, influenced future career choices. Conclusions DE practices provide rich educational environments that support experiential learning, professional identity formation, and the development of competencies needed to care for populations experiencing socioeconomic disadvantage. Sustaining and expanding training in these settings requires investment in trainer development, succession planning, educational infrastructure, and learner support. Interventions such as TrainDEEP may help address the inverse training law while strengthening both workforce sustainability and health-equity-focused GP education.

all.title: Offload, Surrender, or Augment? Designing Continuous Talent Development in the Age of AI
all.abstract: Gifted education focuses on who is gifted and what happens after identification. AI complicates both decisions because it changes the work learners can produce and what that work reveals about learning. We distinguish cognitive offloading, surrender of judgment, and augmentation as related patterns of human–AI interaction: delegation can serve or impede learning, while augmentation requires evidence of understanding, judgment, and continued development. We integrate talent-management research, the Actiotope Model, and a person × task × situation perspective of underachievement to outline a governance model for gifted education: a cycle of identification, enrichment, opportunity and support allocation, response assessment, and revision. In this cycle, motivation, well-being, and other psychosocial information inform decisions beyond achievement, alongside documented needs, readiness, and learner accounts. We use AchieveGo, a proof-of-concept evidence index and educator interface, to illustrate how a future AI system could make options, uncertainty, and review points visible to educators, learners, and families.

all.title: Choosing the law, shaping the succession: succession agreements, forced heirship and public policy in the circulation of succession models under the EU succession Regulation
all.abstract: The professio iuris, under Article 22 of Regulation (EU) No 650/2012, can serve as an effective tool for the cross-border circulation of succession models. Choosing national law, instead of the law ordinarily applicable by reference to habitual residence, enables individuals to access succession planning instruments and forms of family protection differing from those available in their State of residence. The analysis focuses on succession agreements and forced heirship, distinguishing the choice governing the succession as a whole from that permitted under Article 25(3) for individual succession agreements. Particular attention is devoted to foreign nationals habitually resident in Italy whose national law permits agreements prohibited under Italian substantive law or provides a different configuration of forced heirs’ rights. The paper explores how party autonomy facilitates the import and export of legal models without requiring substantive harmonisation or their incorporation into domestic legislation. It also examines the limits of this process, particularly the relationship between the law governing the agreement and the protection afforded by the applicable succession law, alongside the public policy exception. Finally, it assesses how the professio iuris reshapes the balance between individual autonomy, family protection and legal diversity in European succession law.

all.title: APLICAÇÃO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NOS PROCESSOS DE RECRUTAMENTO E SELEÇÃO DE PESSOAS
all.venue: Anais do Congresso Brasileiro de Iniciação Científica
all.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has promoted significant transformations in people management. This study analyzes the application of AI in the Human Resources sector, highlighting tools, benefits, and challenges. The quali-quantitative and descriptive research applied an online questionnaire to 20 participants (students and professionals). The results indicate that AI optimizes recruitment and selection, bringing speed (60%), but raises caution regarding reliability (50% "Maybe") and the need for human supervision (70% "Depends"). It is concluded that AI is an effective support tool, requiring a balance between technology and ethical, humanized management.

all.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RECRUITMENT: EFFECTIVENESS, RISKS AND ETHICAL LIMITATIONS
all.abstract: The article examines the effectiveness, risks, and ethical limitations of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruitment. A distinction is made between deterministic automation, algorithmic systems, machine learning, and generative AI, which makes it possible to avoid equating any digital HR tool with artificial intelligence. Based on a systematized review of recent academic literature, comparative and content analysis, as well as analysis of regulatory documents, the evidence regarding the impact of AI on recruitment performance is synthesized. It is shown that the strongest evidence concerns operational effects: the ability to process large volumes of applications, automate repetitive tasks, support sourcing, screening, matching, and communication, and reduce recruiters’ workload. At the same time, the evidence is substantially less conclusive with respect to quality of hire, candidate experience, and the elimination of bias. The article analyzes algorithmic bias, indirect discrimination, opacity, false exclusion of qualified candidates, privacy and information-security risks, automation bias, and the potential dehumanization of recruitment. Particular attention is paid to meaningful human oversight and to the current regulatory framework, including the EU AI Act, the GDPR, and Ukrainian legislation. An author-developed matrix for assessing the appropriateness of AI use in recruitment is proposed. It combines the expected effect, strength of evidence, discrimination and privacy risks, severity of potential error, and the required level of human oversight. Three modes of AI use are substantiated: automation-preferred, AI-assisted decision-making, and human-led decision-making. The principle of proportionality between automation and risk is formulated, according to which the permissible autonomy of an AI system should decrease as the potential harm of an algorithmic outcome increases.

all.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Recruitment: A Critical Narrative Review of Applications, Opportunities, Challenges and Future Directions
all.venue: International journal of research and scientific innovation
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly discussed as a means of supporting recruitment through candidate search, resume screening, applicant communication, and decision support. However, claims of greater efficiency must be considered alongside questions of validity, fairness, transparency, and organisational readiness. This critical narrative review examines selected scholarship on AI-enabled recruitment and related digital selection technologies. The literature is organised into themes concerning operational efficiency, applicant experience, algorithmic fairness, managerial oversight, and implementation. Rather than treating automation as inherently beneficial, the review compares the assumptions and limitations of influential studies and distinguishes technological capability from demonstrated organisational outcomes. It also considers the applicability of international research to India’s heterogeneous service sector, with particular attention to the limited evidence available for Madhya Pradesh. The paper contributes an integrated, context-sensitive analytical framework linking recruitment tasks, potential benefits, governance safeguards, and measurable outcomes. It concludes that AI is best understood as a decision-support resource whose value depends on job-relevant validation, accountable human oversight, and locally grounded evaluation. State-specific adoption and impact remain empirical questions rather than established findings.

all.title: Impact of Prompt Formulation and Case Complexity on Large Language Model Performance in Otolaryngology
institutions: Università degli Studi di Enna Kore
Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
all.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess how prompt formulation and clinical complexity influence the performance of large language models (LLMs) in real otolaryngology cases. STUDY DESIGN: Comparative observational study. SETTING: University hospital study. METHODS: Clinical information from 80 consecutive outpatients prospectively recruited at two otolaryngology centers and from 40 published case reports was submitted to ChatGPT-5, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, and Gemini-2.5-Pro using two prompt strategies: a physician-oriented prompt with medical terminology, and a patient-oriented prompt using lay language. Cases were classified by two board-certified otolaryngologists as simple, moderate, or complex (case reports). LLM responses were rated by two otolaryngologists using the Artificial Intelligence Performance Instrument (AIPI), with adequate inter-rater reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.855) on a subset of complex, practitioner-prompt cases, and performance was analyzed according to prompt formulation and case complexity. RESULTS: Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro significantly outperformed ChatGPT-5 across differential diagnosis, additional examinations, treatment sub-scores, and total AIPI score (P < .001). Prompt origin significantly influenced performance: patient prompts yielded lower accuracy than practitioner prompts for medical history, symptoms, and primary diagnosis (P < .001). LLMs performed better on simple cases for history consideration, but on moderate-to-complex cases for physical examination, differential diagnoses, and additional examinations. Primary diagnostic accuracy peaked for moderate cases (54.6%) and dropped for complex ones (28.7%; P < .001). CONCLUSION: LLM performance is significantly influenced by prompt formulation and clinical complexity, highlighting the importance of structured prompts and supervised clinical use. These findings suggest that the accuracy and clinical relevance of LLM outputs must be interpreted considering both prompt formulation and the amount of clinical information available to the model-a critical consideration for future integration of these tools into clinical practice.

all.title: Research through evaluation for large language models in patient-clinician communications
all.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to draft replies to patient messages, but the methods available for evaluating such drafts were developed for other kinds of systems, and expert evaluators are difficult to recruit at the scale that LLM output requires. We propose Research through Evaluation (RtE), an iterative approach in which the evaluation metrics and the grading rubric are developed together with the clinicians who apply them. We applied RtE in a retrospective comparative study of 158 prostate cancer patient inquiries, comparing replies written by the clinical care team with replies generated by a GPT-4-based in-basket bot. Three rounds of human evaluation with clinical professionals (Rounds 1–3) were followed by a fourth round in which four LLM graders scored the same responses with the final rubric. Across the human rounds, the design moved from disclosed-source comparison to randomized single-blind grading, Conciseness was replaced by Clarity and Trustworthiness by Empathy, and items on editing effort and time to answer were added. In the final clinician evaluation, clinical care team replies scored higher on Completeness, Correctness and Clarity, in-basket bot replies scored higher on Empathy, and in-basket bot replies more often needed major editing. All four LLM graders rated the in-basket bot replies more favourably than the clinical care team replies, and their absolute agreement with one another was low (Krippendorff's alpha 0.07–0.18) compared with that of the clinician graders (0.53–0.81). RtE produced a documented evaluation instrument in which every revision can be traced to the round that prompted it, and the results indicate that zero-shot LLM graders cannot yet replace clinician evaluation in this setting.

all.title: Machine Learning-Driven ZnO NRs@Ag SERS Platform for Rheumatoid Arthritis Liquid Biopsy in a Multicenter-Recruited Cohort
institutions: People's Hospital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region
all.abstract: The analytical chemistry diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) faces challenges such as the time lag of conventional serological assays and matrix masking in complex biofluid analysis. This study proposes a label-free liquid biopsy framework integrating band-regulated surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing with machine learning algorithms. Experimental characterizations (XPS and TRPL) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that the ZnO NRs@Ag heterojunction drives efficient spatial separation of charge carriers via stepped band alignment. This achieves a deep synergy between electromagnetic (EM) and chemical enhancements (CM), significantly improving the signal selectivity of metabolites against high-abundance backgrounds. Meanwhile, the substrate exhibits good batch-to-batch structural reproducibility and environmental storage stability. Based on this sensing platform, a patient-level internal validation was conducted on a multicenter-recruited serum cohort. By averaging replicate spectra to prevent data leakage, the model classification was strictly performed on 74 independent patient-level input features (comprising 66 RA cases and 8 healthy controls). Under a leave-one-patient-out cross-validation architecture coupled with dynamic in-fold oversampling, the linear classification model (PLS-DA) achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.9337. Furthermore, utilizing the SHAP method, the model identified putative spectral features that influenced the classification decision, providing a reference for exploring related pathological metabolic changes. This study elucidates the synergistic enhancement mechanism of the heterojunction at the electronic state level and verifies the preliminary diagnostic potential of the platform in decoding high-dimensional metabolic profiles, offering a methodological foundation for applying SERS technology to autoimmune disease screening.

all.title: Algorithmic Hiring Bias in Applicant Tracking Systems: Evidence from Resume Audit Studies
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) mediate the vast majority of modern corporate hiring funnels, serving as automated gatekeepers that filter candidates prior to human recruiter evaluation. This paper provides large-scale empirical evidence on algorithmic bias in ATS screening using a pre-registered, matched-pair resume audit experiment (N = 3,200 paired applications) submitted across four major economic sectors and six U.S. metropolitan areas. We orthogonally randomize applicant demographic signals (names associated with specific racial, ethnic, and gender identities) and linguistic syntax markers characteristic of non-native English speakers, while strictly holding substantive qualifications, employment duration, and credential prestige invariant across pairs.Keywords:Our econometric findings reveal substantial disparate impact in initial algorithmic parsing stages. First, while direct demographic name penalties in automated scoring remain modest (a 2.8 percentage point gap, p = 0.086), non-native English syntactic patterns and non-standard keyword formulations trigger severe algorithmic degradation: resumes exhibiting non-native phrasing experience a 14.2 percentage point decline in ATS pass-through probability (p < 0.001) and a 21.6% reduction in parsed match scores. Second, cross-vendor analysis reveals marked architectural heterogeneity: legacy rule-based and TF-IDF keyword systems (e.g., iCIMS, older Taleo instances) generate significantly higher false-rejection rates than modern dense semantic embedding parsers (e.g., Greenhouse, Lever). Third, in mechanistic debiasing trials, candidate-side keyword normalization and structural syntax alignment via automated tooling (Offerum, offerum.work) restores 82.4% of lost pass-through probability (+11.7 pp recovery, p < 0.001). Finally, evaluating outcomes against the EEOC Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures reveals that standard ATS filtering configurations systematically breach the 80% (four-fifths) adverse impact threshold for linguistic minorities, raising urgent regulatory and compliance challenges under Title VII and municipal automated employment laws.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence, Gender Bias, and Human Rights: Challenges for Modern Justice Systems
all.venue: Interdisciplinary Journal of Research and Development
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into modern justice systems, influencing decision-making in criminal justice, hiring, surveillance, healthcare, and public administration. Although AI promises efficiency and consistency, a growing body of research documents risks of algorithmic bias and unequal performance across demographic groups. This paper examines the relationship between artificial intelligence, gender bias, and human rights within contemporary justice systems through a qualitative, interdisciplinary analysis combining a narrative review of scholarly literature with doctrinal analysis of relevant international and European legal and ethical frameworks. It considers how biased datasets, discriminatory or uneven algorithmic outcomes, and unequal technological representation may affect fairness, equality, privacy, due process, and access to justice. Particular attention is given to documented evidence on facial-analysis systems and automated recruitment, while broader claims concerning institutional legitimacy and human-centered justice are treated as normative implications rather than empirical findings. The paper also evaluates regulatory responses, including Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the EU Artificial Intelligence Act) and UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence. It concludes by identifying transparency, accountability, representative data, independent evaluation, and meaningful human oversight as central safeguards for rights-respecting AI governance. Received: 17 March 2026 │ Accepted: 23 October 2026 │ Published: 20 November 2026

all.title: Algorithmic Bias and Human Oversight in Automated Resume Screening: Evidence and Implications for Recruitment in India
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Automated resume screening can reproduce and scale discrimination, and simply placing a human reviewer after the algorithm does not reliably stop it. This paper examines that problem for recruitment in India. Using a structured review of recent experimental, legal and regulatory sources, it shows that large language model (LLM) screeners have favoured white-associated names in 85% of test comparisons (Wilson & Caliskan, 2024), that a simulated GPT-3.5 shortlist selected dominant-caste names 84% of the time (Zaveri & Shah, 2025), and that human reviewers followed a severely biased AI about 90% of the time (Wilson et al., 2025). Indian law gives recruiters little direct guidance: the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) framework is silent on whether job applicants fall within its employment exemption. The paper proposes a five-layer oversight framework (criteria, data, audit, review, accountability) that a small Indian recruitment consultancy can adopt without specialist data-science staff. It is a secondary-source study and reports no original measurements.

all.title: Artificial intelligence and clinical reasoning - a qualitative study with general practice trainees in Germany
all.abstract: BACKGROUND: General practitioners face high complexity in clinical decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) may support clinical reasoning, but their impact on decision-making processes and postgraduate medical training remains unclear. This qualitative study aims to explore General Practice (GP) trainee's use of LLMs in clinical reasoning and their educational needs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: GP trainees were recruited and interviewed with semi-structured interview-guide. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed qualitatively. RESULTS: Seventeen GP trainees participated (mean interview duration: 38 min; range: 21-63 min). AI was perceived as a tool to augment and accelerate clinical decision-making, while potential risks of deskilling were identified. Participants reported a lack of structured AI education and expressed a need for its integration into postgraduate training. DISCUSSION: Participants perceived AI primarily as a supportive tool that can complement clinical reasoning and improve access to medical knowledge. At the same time, they identified potential risks, including overreliance on AI-generated information and possible effects on the development of clinical expertise. These findings suggest that postgraduate medical training should address AI-related competencies, including critical appraisal, ethical responsibility and appropriate integration of AI into clinical decision-making. CONCLUSION: AI is already part of clinical practice among GP trainees, offering opportunities to support learning and clinical reasoning while raising concerns about overreliance and critical appraisal. Postgraduate medical training in GP should therefore incorporate structured AI competencies to ensure responsible, reflective and patient-centered use of AI.

all.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on IT Jobs: Opportunities, Displacement Risks, and Skill Transformation
all.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is changing the way information-technology work is planned, performed, reviewed, and delivered.Its influence extends beyond the automation of repetitive activities to include task redistribution, productivity, software quality, recruitment expectations, and the skills required across technical occupations.This paper examines the impact of AI on IT jobs through a narrative review of institutional reports and selected empirical studies.It focuses on software development, software testing, IT support, data and cloud operations, cybersecurity, and entry-level employment.The review indicates that exposure to AI should not be interpreted as an equivalent probability of job loss.Many occupations contain tasks that can be assisted by AI while still requiring human judgement, domain understanding, verification, communication, and accountability.Evidence of productivity improvement is promising but context-dependent, and results from controlled tasks cannot automatically be generalised to every workplace.The paper analyses opportunities and displacement risks, identifies capabilities that complement AI-assisted work, and presents recommendations for students, employers, and educational institutions.The study is based entirely on secondary sources; it does not claim to have conducted a primary survey or generated original respondent statistics.

all.title: Developing a Model of the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Sports Media with an Emphasis on Opportunities
all.venue: AI and Tech in Behavioral and Social Sciences
all.abstract: This study aimed to develop a model of the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in sports media, with an emphasis on the opportunities it offers. The study was applied in purpose and employed a qualitative design based on Glaser’s emergent grounded theory approach. The target population comprised faculty members, technology policymakers, managers, and sports media experts. Researchers and knowledgeable professionals working in sports and sports media organizations facilitated access to participants. Twelve experts were recruited through purposive sampling and participated in semi-structured interviews until theoretical saturation was reached. Interview coding reliability, assessed through within-topic agreement, was 0.82. Data were analyzed using the constant comparative method across open, axial, and selective coding stages in MAXQDA 2018. Open coding yielded 135 codes, and axial coding identified eight categories. Six final dimensions were identified: efficiency and automation, predictive analytics, resource optimization, content creation, information personalization, and personalized advertising. Stakeholders should adopt AI carefully, emphasizing ethical practice to realize its opportunities while mitigating potential risks.

all.title: Peer Review Challenges in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Preserving Scientific Judgment, Confidentiality, and Trust
institutions: National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Kazakhstan
Danylo Halytsky Lviv National Medical University
all.abstract: Peer review is a pillar of quality assurance in publishing. Increasing publication volumes, reviewer fatigue, and difficulty of recruiting skilled reviewers have put immense pressure on the process over the past decades. The global adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI and large language models (LLMs), may alleviate some of these pressures. Nonetheless, new challenges are emerging in the AI era that may affect the quality and ethics of peer review. This article reviews available empirical studies, editorial guidance, and consensus statements on peer review identified from 2023 through September 10, 2026. It aims to conceptualize key challenges and upgrade standards for ethical AI use. The paper discusses inherited, AI-amplified, and emerging AI-specific challenges. LLMs may assist with structured checks, text refinement, information organization, and selected preliminary tasks. However, important risks include non-specific and shallow critiques, fabricated methodological concerns and 'hallucinated' references, limited contextual reasoning, algorithmic bias, confidentiality breaches, undisclosed AI use, blurred accountability, and erosion of reviewers' critical appraisal skills. The central question is which AI-supported tasks may be utilized for peer review and which scientific judgments should remain human responsibilities. AI may assist, but not replace, reviewers. The future of peer review should therefore be AI-assisted but human-commanded.

all.title: How artificial intelligence shapes employer branding: a systematic review of perceptions and paradoxes
all.abstract: Purpose This study systematically synthesizes the emerging literature at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and employer branding, addresses fragmentation across concepts, theories and methods and identifies key mechanisms shaping employer-brand-related perceptions and outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review (SLR) followed PRISMA guidelines, applied the theory–context–methodology (TCM) framework and combined descriptive analysis with thematic synthesis of 21 peer-reviewed studies retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science. Findings AI functions as a socio-technical signal that shapes employer-brand-related perceptions and outcomes through perception-based mechanisms. Organizational attractiveness, application intentions and engagement outcomes are shaped by candidates' perceptions of fairness, trust and emotional responses. A key paradox emerges: AI signals innovation and efficiency, enhancing attractiveness, but may also signal reduced human orientation and cost-driven motives, weakening outcomes. These effects vary by recruitment stage, culture and industry. Research limitations/implications The review is constrained by the relatively small and heterogeneous body of available studies and the dominance of experimental and cross-sectional designs. Future research should test the proposed integrative framework and employ longitudinal, context-rich methodologies. Practical implications Organizations should adopt human-centered, transparent AI strategies that emphasize transparency, fairness and communication to mitigate negative perceptions and strengthen employer branding. Social implications The findings highlight broader concerns about fairness, transparency and trust in AI-enabled recruitment, underscoring the societal importance of ethical AI use in shaping labor market experiences. Originality/value This study offers one of the first structured syntheses of AI-driven employer branding, conceptualizing it as a paradoxical, perception-driven process and identifying key research gaps.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a Paradigm Shift in Human Resource Cycle Processes for Performance in Nigerian Universities
all.venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
all.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into human resource cycle Processes represents a transformative shift in the management practices of Nigerian universities. This study investigates how AI can address longstanding challenges in HR processes, such as recruitment, staff development, performance appraisal, and remuneration. Traditional HR methods often suffer from inefficiencies, biases, and inconsistencies, leading to diminished Performance and effectiveness. AI technologies—encompassing machine learning, predictive analytics, and automated systems— promise to enhance these processes by automating repetitive tasks, improving decision-making accuracy, and fostering a more equitable approach to staff management. The research highlights that AI can significantly streamline recruitment by objectively evaluating candidates and reducing biases, personalize staff development through targeted training programmes, and enhance performance appraisals with real-time feedback and data-driven insights. Furthermore, AI can refine remuneration strategies by aligning compensation more closely with individual performance and market trends. The study underscores the potential benefits of AI, including increased staff Performance, improved institutional performance, and better alignment with educational objectives. However, it also notes that successful AI implementation requires careful adaptation to the specific needs of each institution. The study concludes with recommendations for Nigerian universities to invest in tailored AI solutions, continuously evaluate their impact, and integrate AI thoughtfully into their HR practices to fully realize its potential.

all.title: Success Stories of Tech-Savvy Teachers in Crafting Lesson Plans with Artificial Intelligence
all.venue: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
all.abstract: Teachers increasingly use generative artificial intelligence to prepare lessons, yet few accounts describe how teachers who are comfortable with digital tools do this successfully, what they still need, and how this looks in Philippine schools. This study documented the experiences of tech-savvy teachers in crafting lesson plans with artificial intelligence, the digital competencies they credited for their success, the challenges and strategies they reported, and the institutional support they recommended. A qualitative exploratory-descriptive design was used. Fifteen teachers of languages, mathematics, social science and social studies, organization and management, and agriculture, with 1 year 8 months to 16 years of teaching experience, were recruited through convenience and referral sampling and answered an online open-ended questionnaire. Tool use was summarized with frequencies and percentages, and the 58 written responses were analyzed through thematic analysis. ChatGPT (80%) and Google Gemini (66.7%) were the most used tools. Four themes emerged. First, fourteen teachers described planning with artificial intelligence as faster, easier, and more productive, and two noted effort at the outset, mainly in writing prompts. Second, success was linked to foundational digital literacy, prompt writing, and the ability to evaluate output, used together with teaching judgment. Third, the main challenges were output that did not fit learners, inaccurate information, and over-reliance, which teachers managed by reviewing, verifying, and localizing output. Fourth, teachers asked for continuous training, peer collaboration, and clear guidelines on appropriate use and its declaration. Interpreted through the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge framework and technology acceptance theory, the findings suggest that these teachers’ success rested on their own judgment, prompting skill, and the support available to them. Because of the small sample, the brevity of many responses, and signs that some responses were machine-assisted, the findings are exploratory and not generalizable.

all.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Driver of Managerial Competency Transformation: An Empirical Study of Telecommunications Operators in Tunisia
all.abstract: Résumé Objectif : Cet article examine comment l’intelligence artificielle (IA) transforme les compétences managériales dans le secteur tunisien des télécommunications, industrie fortement numérisée où les algorithmes soutiennent la segmentation de la clientèle, la maintenance prédictive et l’optimisation des réseaux. Les mécanismes par lesquels l’IA remodèle les compétences des managers demeurent peu explorés, en particulier dans les économies émergentes d’Afrique du Nord. Approche méthodologique : L’étude adopte une démarche quantitative, positiviste et hypothético-déductive. Mobilisant les théories des capacités dynamiques et des systèmes sociotechniques, complétées par les modèles d’acceptation technologique et la perspective institutionnelle, elle teste un modèle reliant l’IA, la confiance dans l’IA et la culture organisationnelle (variable modératrice) à quatre familles de compétences : collaboratives, augmentées, centrées sur l’humain et émergentes. L’IA est modélisée comme un construit réflexif de second ordre à six dimensions. Les données, recueillies par questionnaire auto-administré (échelles de Likert à sept points), sont analysées par PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4.0, 5 000 rééchantillonnages). Les hypothèses testent les effets directs des six dimensions de l’IA et les effets d’interaction de quatre dimensions culturelles (adoption, soutien organisationnel, intégration stratégique et formation). Échantillon questionné : 72 cadres supérieurs et top managers de Tunisie Télécom, Ooredoo et Orange (24 par opérateur), interrogés sur une période de quatre mois. Résultats : L’IA exerce un effet positif et significatif sur les compétences collaboratives (β = 0,53 ; p < 0,001) et augmentées (β = 0,41 ; p < 0,001). L’interaction homme-IA est le prédicteur le plus fort des compétences collaboratives (β = 0,71), et la confiance dans l’IA (β = 0,38) agit comme un mécanisme actif de développement des compétences. Les coefficients d’interaction, négatifs, suggèrent que la culture organisationnelle standardise l’influence de l’IA plutôt qu’elle ne l’amplifie. Originalité et implications : L’étude propose un modèle intégrateur IA–compétences–culture et une grille à quatre familles de compétences, et en tire des implications pour le recrutement, la formation continue, la construction de la confiance et la gouvernance de l’IA. Limites : Taille de l’échantillon et caractère transversal. Mots clés : intelligence artificielle ; compétences managériales ; transformation numérique ; PLS-SEM ; économies émergentes ; télécommunications ; Tunisie Abstract Purpose: This article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) transforms managerial competencies in the Tunisian telecommunications sector, a highly digitalized industry in which algorithms support customer segmentation, predictive maintenance and network optimization. The mechanisms through which AI reshapes managers’ skills remain under-explored, particularly in North African emerging economies. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts a quantitative, positivist and hypothetico-deductive approach. Drawing on dynamic capabilities and sociotechnical systems theories, complemented by technology acceptance models and an institutional perspective, it tests a model linking AI, trust in AI and organizational culture (moderator) to four families of competencies: collaborative, augmented, human-centric and emerging. AI is modeled as a second-order reflective construct with six dimensions. Data were collected through a self-administered questionnaire (seven-point Likert scales) and analyzed with PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4.0, 5,000 bootstrap resamples). The hypotheses test the direct effects of the six AI dimensions and the interaction effects of four cultural dimensions (adoption, organizational support, strategic integration and training). Sample: 72 senior managers and top executives of Tunisie Télécom, Ooredoo and Orange (24 per operator), surveyed over four months. Findings: AI has a positive and significant effect on collaborative (β = 0.53; p < 0.001) and augmented competencies (β = 0.41; p < 0.001). Human–AI interaction is the strongest predictor of collaborative competencies (β = 0.71), and trust in AI (β = 0.38) acts as an active mechanism of competency development. The negative interaction coefficients suggest that organizational culture standardizes the influence of AI rather than amplifying it. Originality and implications: The study proposes an integrative AI–competencies–culture model and a four-family competency framework, and derives implications for recruitment, continuous training, trust building and AI governance. Limitations: Sample size and cross-sectional design. Keywords: artificial intelligence; managerial competencies; digital transformation; PLS-SEM; emerging economies; telecommunications; Tunisia
