Data were gathered through a cross-sectional survey on a five-point Likert scale, yielding 127 usable responses (64 Managers and 63 Supervisors). Separate questionnaires were administered to employees and to their supervisors so that common method bias could be limited. The data were analyzed with descriptive statistics, an independent samples t-test and Pearson correlation. Performance Appraisal scores were low overall (M = 2.47 out of 5). Managers (2.38) were rated significantly lower than supervisors (2.56) (p < .05). A weak but positive correlation was observed between Emotional Intelligence and appraisal scores (r = .18, roughly 3% shared variance), although its significance should be verified against the original output. Managers recorded higher scores on five of the six Emotional Intelligence domains but lower scores on adaptability and flexibility. The proposed relational model holds that Emotional Intelligence affects Organizational Behaviour directly (P1) and indirectly via Performance Appraisal (P2); both paths were specified for testing through bootstrapping. Because no Organizational Behaviour data were available, these paths could not be estimated. The findings suggest that organizations should train appraisers in emotional competencies and treat Performance Appraisal as a two-way feedback conversation. Since convenience sampling and a cross-sectional design were used, the results cannot be generalized and no causal claims can be made. Keywords: Emotional Intelligence; Performance Appraisal; Organizational Behaviour; Employee performance; Project based; Pakistan.

all.title: The Effect of Performance Appraisal on the Work Performance of Employees in Indian Hotels.
all.abstract: This research aims to examine the effect of performance appraisal on employee work performance in Indian hotels, with particular emphasis on its relationship with employee motivation. The study adopts an explanatory research design using both qualitative and quantitative approaches. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire distributed via Google Forms among employees working in various departments of the hospitality industry. A five-point Likert scale was used to measure respondents' perceptions and experiences. Secondary data were gathered from books, research articles, journals, and online sources. The findings indicate that performance appraisal plays a significant role in influencing employee work performance and has a positive relationship with employee motivation. The study highlights the importance of effective performance appraisal systems in improving employee productivity, motivation, and overall organizational performance in the Indian hotel industry.

all.title: THE HIDDEN COST OF AI-AUGMENTED PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL: ALGORITHMIC EVALUATION ANXIETY, EMPLOYEE SILENCE, AND THE BUFFERING ROLE OF HR TRANSPARENCY
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

all.title: Continuous Performance Management and Employee Development: A Systematic Literature Review of Coaching, Feedback, and Learning Mechanism
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
all.abstract: Traditional annual performance appraisals fail to drive agile competency growth in dynamic modern organizations, making continuous performance management (CPM) critically important for talent retention. However, previous literature reviews often overlook the granular interactions among coaching, feedback, and learning mechanisms in corporate employee development, thereby leaving a significant gap in the research (research gap). To address this limitation, this study examines how these specific internal mechanisms interact within the CPM environment to drive professional growth. By applying the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach as the primary methodology, this study thoroughly screens and analyzes 30 global empirical articles from the 2020–2025 period using rigid thematic synthesis stages. The novelty of this research (novelty) lies in formulating a new integrative model based on a picture of research results demonstrating that daily coaching and feedback interactions consistently trigger work engagement as the primary mediating mechanism. Meanwhile, the effectiveness of training content absorption on digital learning platforms is proven to be accelerated by (moderating boundary conditions) in the form of organizational learning climate flexibility and leader humility. Therefore, it is recommended that future studies extend these conceptual dynamics through sector-specific empirical tracking.

all.title: THESIS FOR THE DEGREE OF MASTER OF BUSINESS ADMINSTRATION IN BUSINESS PROGRAM THE RELATION BETWEEN PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT THESIS FOR THE DEGREE OF MASTER OF BUSINESS ADMINSTRATION IN BUSINESS PROGRAM THE RELATION BETWEEN PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT THESIS FOR THE DEGREE OF MASTER OF BUSINESS ADMINSTRATIONIN BUSINESS PROGRAM THE RELATION BETWEEN PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT AND EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT
Transformational Leadership and Employee Productivity: The Mediating Role of Employee Engagement and Moderating Role of Organizational Culture
all.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between transformational leadership and employee productivity, with employee engagement as a mediating variable and organizational culture as a moderating variable, among officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Dutse, Jigawa State. Employee productivity remains a critical concern in Nigerian public security institutions. The study was anchored on Bass and Avolio's Full Range Leadership Model, Kahn's Psychological Engagement Theory, and Cameron and Quinn's Competing Values Framework. A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted, with data collected from 59 respondents and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4.0. Findings revealed that transformational leadership significantly predicts employee productivity, and that employee engagement both significantly predicts productivity and partially mediates the transformational leadershipproductivity relationship. Organizational culture was found to significantly moderate both the leadership–productivity and engagement–productivity relationships. The model explained 84.7% of the variance in employee productivity. The study concludes that transformational leadership, employee engagement, and a discipline-oriented organizational culture jointly enhance productivity in Nigerian paramilitary organizations such as the NSCDC. It recommends sustained investment in transformational leadership development, targeted employee engagement interventions within the security sector, reinforcement of a disciplineoriented culture, and alignment of formal performance appraisal systems with transformational leadership behaviors.Originality/Value: This is the first PLS-SEM moderated mediation study of the leadership-productivity nexus in a Nigerian Security and Civil Defence paramilitary organization

all.title: The Effect Of Performance Management On Employee Performance Through Civil Servant Professionalism At The Gorontalo High Court
all.venue: International Journal of Economics Business and Innovation Research
all.abstract: This study examines the effect of performance management on employee performance through civil servant professionalism at the Gorontalo High Court. A quantitative survey design was employed, and data were collected from 53 civil servants using a saturated sampling technique. The analysis used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results show that performance management has a positive and significant effect on both employee performance and civil servant professionalism, and that professionalism has a positive and significant effect on employee performance. Professionalism partially mediates the effect of performance management on employee performance. The model explains 81.0% of the variance in employee performance but only 9.2% of the variance in professionalism, indicating that professionalism is largely shaped by factors beyond performance management. The study underscores the importance of linking the performance management cycle to professional development to improve employee performance in the judicial sector.

all.title: The Effects of Green HRM Practices, Organizational Commitment, and Knowledge Sharing Behavior on Sustainable Employee Performance among Employees of State-Owned Enterprises in Indonesia
all.venue: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
institutions: Universitas Islam Negeri Sultan Syarif Kasim Riau
all.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the impact of Green HRM Practices, Organizational Commitment and Knowledge Sharing Behavior on Sustainable Employee Performance. The study was conducted among workers of SOE (State-Owned Enterprises) in Indonesia. The research was of quantitative nature and survey technique was used as a tool for data collection from the personnel of SOEs from different industrial sectors. The authors used a purposive sampling approach. The respondents were active employees with at least one year of service who had knowledge of human resource management procedures and experience in work activities related to organizational sustainability and knowledge sharing. The data was collected using an online questionnaire through Google Form. Data analysis was performed using multiple linear regression. The analytical model indicates positive relationships between Green HRM Practices, Organizational Commitment, Knowledge Sharing Behavior and Sustainable Employee Performance. These three variables may enhance sustainable performance through strengthening environmentally oriented HRM practices and enabling a sharing information culture that fosters learning and cooperation. The results of this study have practical implications for SOEs, which have to reinforce green training and development, green performance management, knowledge management systems, best practice sharing and continuous improvement to enhance productivity, work quality, resource use efficiency and employees’ adaptability.

all.title: Performance Appraisal Practices, Teacher Motivation, and Job Performance: An Analytical Study of Private Schools
all.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
authors: Abhay Ramkripal Tripathi, Bhawna Sharma Padroo
all.abstract: Performance appraisal is one of the key tools of human resource management. It helps in evaluating the effectiveness of the employees, appreciating their professional achievements and identifying areas of improvement. Performance appraisal practices in private schools are important to evaluate the contribution of teachers, to improve professional development and to uphold the standards of education. The fairness and transparency of evaluation procedures, the quality of feedback, the recognition of achievements, and opportunities for career advancement can influence their effectiveness. The present study is intended to study the effect of performance appraisal practices on teacher motivation and job performance in private schools. The aim is to analyse the relationship between appraisal mechanisms and teachers’ professional commitment, job satisfaction and work effectiveness. The study also investigates teachers’ perceptions of performance appraisal systems and the possible role of constructive criticism, performance-based recognition, and transparent evaluation criteria in enhancing motivation and professional growth. The study suggests a quantitative research design employing primary data from teachers of selected private schools, collected through a structured questionnaire. Statistical techniques will be employed to analyse the data collected and determine the relationships between performance appraisal practices, teacher motivation and job performance. It is expected that the study will be useful to school administrators, management professionals and educational policy makers in developing effective, transparent and equitable performance appraisal systems. The findings may inform the development of strategies to improve teacher motivation, continuous professional development and institutional effectiveness. Overall, the research indicates the importance of effective performance management practices in creating a positive work environment and supporting quality education in private schools.

all.title: Factors Influencing Shift from Open Performance Review and Appraisal System to Public Employees’ Performance Management Information System at the NSSF, Dodoma
all.venue: American Journal of Operations Management and Information Systems
all.abstract: The transition from OPRAS to PEPMIS indicates significant digital transformation for performance management in the Tanzanian public sector. This study assessed factors influencing the shift from OPRAS to PEPMIS at the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) in Dodoma. Specifically, the study focused on users’ perceptions that influence the shift from OPRAS to PEPMIS, the influence of organizational policies and regulations on the shift to PEPMIS, and the evaluation of training and support needs for successful implementation of PEPMIS. A descriptive research design was used, utilizing mixed approaches that combine both qualitative and quantitative approaches. A sample size of 44 respondents was employed, selected through simple random sampling and purposive sampling techniques. The study collected both primary data and secondary data using questionnaires, interviews, and documentary review as the methods. The study was anchored on expectancy theory and goal-setting theory to provide deep insight. The findings of the study revealed that users’ perceptions were positive about PEPMIS compared with OPRAS and were highly satisfied with PEPMIS, also it was noted that PEPMIS was transparency because provided transparent appraisal process. The study indicates that OPRAS could not handle modern performance evaluation needs. Furthermore, the findings revealed that organizational policies and regulation support the adoption of PEPMIS. Moreover, the findings found that training and support provided to the employee for the aims of success in the implementation of PEPMIS. The study concluded that employees had different perceptions of OPRAS and PEPMIS, some support PEPMIS as more user-friendly system, transparent and provide real-time feedback compared with OPRAS. Also, organizational policies and regulations played a significant role in shifting to PEPMIS. Additionally, training and support had a strong influence on the successful implementation of PEPMIS. The study recommended that organizations should provide adequate training and support to employees to make them familiar with the system. Also, revision of organizational policies and regulations should be conducted to ensure clarity, inclusivity, and acceptance of policies and regulations, and some adjustments should be made.

all.title: Introduction: Performance Management in the Age of AI
PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL: CATALYST FOR ENHANCEMENT OF CREATIVE AND INNOVATIVE PERFORMANCE. A FOCUS ON IMO STATE CIVIL SERVICE (2010-2023)
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: Performance appraisal has the capacity of influencing the employee performance. It is the basis for the assessment and evaluation of the employees’ level of performance. With the objective of determining the effects of performance appraisal on creative and innovative performance of employees in Imo State Civil Service, the study employed survey research design. Mean score model based on a four-point likert scale was used in the analysis of data. The findings showed that performance appraisal has significantly improved employees training leading to high performance. Also, it has not adequately enhanced promotion and incentive of employees which has impacted negatively on their performance in Imo State Civil Service. The study recommended the use of bureaucratic rules in the conduct of performance appraisal with focus on training, regular promotion and financial incentives of workers for high performance in Imo State Civil Service

all.title: THE EFFECT OF CHANGES IN ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE AND WORK MECHANISMS ON THE PERFORMANCE OF SUB-DISTRICT (KELURAHAN) EMPLOYEES IN SOUTH NUNUKAN SUBDISTRICT, NUNUKAN REGENCY
all.abstract: This study examines the effect of changes in organizational structure and work mechanisms on the performance of sub-district (kelurahan) employees in South Nunukan Subdistrict, Nunukan Regency. The research employs a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design. A census method was used for sampling, involving all 64 civil servant (ASN) employees across four kelurahan in South Nunukan Subdistrict as respondents (total sampling). Data were collected through digital questionnaires (Google Forms) using a Likert scale (1–5) and analyzed using SPSS version 31, including validity tests, reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis. The results indicate that: (1) changes in organizational structure do not have a significant effect on employee performance (t-value = 0.644, Sig. = 0.522 > 0.05); (2) changes in work mechanisms have a positive and significant effect on employee performance (t-value = 2.141, Sig. = 0.036 < 0.05); and (3) simultaneously, changes in organizational structure and work mechanisms have a significant effect on employee performance (F-value = 7.207, Sig. = 0.002 < 0.05), with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.191, meaning that 19.1% of the variation in employee performance is explained by the two independent variables, while the remaining 80.9% is influenced by other factors not examined in this study. The findings suggest that bureaucratic streamlining through structural changes alone is insufficient to improve performance; rather, adjustments in work mechanisms—including assignment systems, task execution, accountability, performance management, and ICT utilization play a more decisive role.

all.title: EXPLORING PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT IN KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES: A SCOPUS-BASED BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
all.venue: Advanced International Journal of Business Entrepreneurship and SMEs
all.abstract: Recently, Performance Management (PM) and Knowledge Management (KM) have been explored as separate fields, with organizations relying on both to enhance employee capabilities, improve learning, and achieve better outcomes over time. Although these two constructs are closely related in practice, there are gaps in how their connection and integration are developed, structured, and related. This study analyses a possible method to address the gap through bibliometric mapping, focusing on PM and KM within the publication period from 2000 to October 2026. The final results, based on the keyword string and filter exclusion, recorded 877 publications. The publication trends were determined using Scopus Analyzer, while OpenRefine and VOSviewer were used to clean metadata. The final clean data were used to develop keyword co-occurrence mapping and a co-authorship network at the country level. The publication output has been steadily increasing, with the highest number of publications in 2026. The keywords used, such as KM, PM, and organizational learning, show the connection between the two fields. The results show clusters in sustainable development, intellectual capital, innovation and strategic Human Resource Management (HRM). These clusters show that PM and KM are related to many disciplines and broader research across countries and authors. The most publications were produced by the United States, China, and the United Kingdom. Meanwhile, international collaboration across countries shows uneven levels in co-authorship networks. This study urges future empirical analysis to provide researchers with a guide and argues for an integrated theoretical framework that PM practices were supported by KM, such as knowledge creation, application, and sharing, across countries and organizations.

all.title: Enabling vs. directive: How performance management affects innovative performance through thriving at work
all.abstract: Rapid changes in the business landscape push organizations to innovate. Scholars, practitioners and policymakers have emphasized the importance of innovative performance to remain competitive. This study investigates how directive and enabling performance management (PM) affect employee innovative performance. Drawing on the socially-embedded model of thriving, we propose thriving at work, the joint experience of vitality and learning, as mediating mechanism. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 461 employees and their supervisors, Structural Equation Modeling results indicate that: (1) enabling PM is positively related to innovative performance through both vitality and learning, whereas for directive PM only learning mediates the negative indirect relationship; (2) both vitality and learning are individually positively associated with innovative performance; and (3) learning only enhances innovative performance when vitality is high. This research explains how distinct PM approaches affect innovative performance and identifies vitality as a critical boundary condition for the learning-innovative performance relationship. These findings suggest that the joint effects of vitality and learning deserve greater attention in future research.

all.title: Performance Assessment Tools and Employee Motivation in a South African Public Legislature
all.venue: International Journal of Research on Multidisciplinary Studies
all.abstract: A prominent question in performance appraisal research is whether employee motivation is related to appraisal as an integrated HRM practice. Particularly in public legislative institutions, employees' experiences with appraisals through specialized assessment procedures have received less attention. Therefore, this study investigates how employees see the performance evaluation instruments integrated within the Limpopo Provincial Legislature's performance management system in South Africa. Out of 190 employees, 130 participated in a quantitative, cross-sectional survey. A structured questionnaire with eighteen Likert-scale statements was used to gather data. The analysis concentrated on mechanisms related to assessment, such as performance-linked incentives, procedural fairness, developmental support, recognition, and the use of assessment results for training and development. The results show a significant difference: while performance-linked incentives were highly supported as motivating, a significant percentage of workers expressed concerns about fairness and transparency, anxiety about assessments, dissatisfaction with recognition, a lack of developmental support, and weak connections between assessment results and training. By demonstrating that the motivational value of assessment depends not only on the existence of a formal system but also on the configuration and implementation of its constituent processes, the study adds a tool-level perspective to public-sector performance management.

all.title: The Role of Human Resources in Managing Employee Stress in the Hospitality Industry
all.abstract: Within the hospitality industry, employees are often required to have unsociable hours and face many challenges, including high standards expected of them, and both physical and psychological demands. Employees may experience stress within this sector and this can then lead to issues such as burnout, low motivation, absence and even employee resignation. Human Resource Management is integral in analysing why employees may become stressed and putting in place effective human resource management strategies in order to promote well-being. This paper investigates how Human Resources manage employee stress within the hospitality sector. The main factors which may result in employees becoming stressed include; workload, working hours, employee-employee relationships, work life balance, job instability, employee numbers and difficult customer relationships. Human resource activities which can be implemented to help manage stress include employee recruitment and resourcing, training, employee support services, health and well-being initiatives, variable working hours, positive management styles, complaint procedures, performance appraisal, reward and career progression. Sources of information include academic and report literature on topics such as, employee well-being, and employee stress and human resource management. Recent in-depth research has shown that both person, team and organizational factors can impact the well-being of those in hospitality. For example, a 2025 systematic literature review analysed 122 articles published in 19 hospitality journals. Within this, it was emphasised how significant the influence of organizational strategies can be on the well-being of hospitality employees. Likewise, research into the Indian hospitality industry also underlines the significance of stress and job satisfaction for employees within the hotels of Mumbai. Therefore, rather than managing employee stress on an individual basis, Human Resources should adopt a pro-active and holistic strategy. Strategies such as promoting good environments, optimising jobs, developing appropriate management and guaranteeing suitable numbers of employees, alongside offering access to mental health support, can all help to improve both employee well-being and business performance.

all.title: Performance Management Strategies And Management Innovation In Improving The Quality Of Public Services At The Gunungsitoli Idanoi District Office
all.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to analyze performance management strategies, management innovation, public service quality, and the supporting and inhibiting factors in enhancing public service delivery at the Gunungsitoli Idanoi District Office. Methods: This study employed a qualitative descriptive approach with purposive sampling to select local administrators, operational staff, and community members as key informants. Data were collected through field observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed using data reduction, data display, and conclusion verification techniques. Results: The findings indicated that performance management strategies functioned through task allocation, coordination, and supervision, although evaluations were conducted only on an incidental basis. Management innovations enhanced work processes and basic technology utilization, but these initiatives had not developed into an integrated digital service system. While procedural clarity and officer attitudes were rated favorably, service speed and completion time certainty required improvement. Supporting factors included active leadership and staff commitment, whereas inadequate infrastructure, limited human resources, and fragmented technology adoption served as primary barriers. Conclusions: The study concluded that improving public service quality required institutionalizing routine performance evaluations, establishing an integrated digital public service system, and reinforcing organizational infrastructure. Originality/value: This research provided empirical insights into sub-district public sector governance, presenting actionable evidence on how performance management and administrative innovation interacted to overcome operational constraints in local government offices.

all.title: Performance Information in the Public Sector: Three Essays on Feedback, Employee Evaluation, and Citizen Perceptions
all.abstract: Performance measurement has become an established practice in public organizations worldwide, generating a steady stream of performance information in diverse forms. This information is interpreted and used to inform judgment and decision-making by a wide range of stakeholders, including managers and other organizational actors, legislative and other oversight bodies, public employees, and service users and citizens. Through three empirical essays, this dissertation explores how performance information is generated, communicated, interpreted, and used across organizational, employee, and citizen contexts. The first essay examines how federally qualified health centers respond to performance feedback conveyed by a quality rating and recognition program. Using data from more than 1,400 federally qualified health centers across the U.S., it investigates whether receiving a relatively unfavorable quality rating is associated with subsequent performance improvement and whether organizational responses to feedback vary across performance dimensions. The findings indicate that the quality rating and recognition program primarily encourages continued improvement among high-performing organizations that have already received recognition. There is little evidence that concentrating attention on recognized performance dimensions undermines performance in other dimensions. The second essay compares the design of employee performance evaluation systems and their effects on employees in public and private workplaces in South Korea. Using organizational-level panel data, it analyzes three components of evaluation design: the ratio of quantitative to qualitative performance indicators, the dimensions of employee performance assessed, and the characteristics of evaluators. It then considers how these evaluation design features are associated with employee objections to evaluation results. The findings indicate that public workplaces rely more heavily on qualitative indicators than private workplaces. They also suggest that evaluating employees across a broader range of performance dimensions may increase, rather than reduce, objections to evaluation results. The third essay examines how citizens interpret comparative performance information about public schools and form evaluative judgments. Drawing on three survey experiments with U.S. adults, the study investigates how historical and social benchmarks function as reference points in citizens’ evaluations of school performance and their support for additional resources. The findings show that performance judgments are more responsive to historical benchmarks than to social benchmarks when each is presented independently. When multiple benchmarks are presented concurrently, however, social comparisons become more salient influences on citizens’ overall performance judgments. The three essays of this dissertation demonstrate that public performance management is not simply a technical process of measuring results. Rather, its utility depends on how performance is defined and measured, how performance information is communicated, and how organizational actors and citizens interpret and respond to that information. By examining these processes across organizational, employee, and citizen contexts, this dissertation advances understanding of the behavioral foundations of performance management and the conditions under which performance information shapes decisions and judgments in the public sector.

all.title: What Human Resource Development Practices are Necessary for Employee Engagement in Nepalese Banking Sector?
all.venue: Contemporary Research An Interdisciplinary Academic Journal
all.abstract: The organizations of the 21st century practice employee engagement in the key areas of concern— to drive forward initiatives matching employee motivation with the organizational strategic goals. To achieve this objective, this study aims to examine the structural and conditional dynamics of engagement with preliminary focus on both sufficient and necessary human resource development (HRD) practices that influence varying levels of employee engagement. The cross-sectional survey data were collected from 414 employees of eight commercial banks comprising two public limited, two joint venture, and 4 private commercial banks across the country. We used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (Smart-PLS) to analyze the data; to test the hypothesized relationships between variables, and to establish convergent and discriminant validity. The dual-method technique offers a comprehensive insight on how human resource development techniques work both as enabling and restricting variables for engagement. The findings on necessary condition analysis indicate that training and development is necessary at lower levels, career development and performance management at a moderate level; and perceived organizational support has emerged as necessary for high levels of engagement. This study examines employee engagement using dual-method approach combining PLS-SEM and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) as per the sequential requirement of NCA. Each of the human resource development practices become necessary at different engagement levels supported by sufficiency-only theories and is in line with Job Demands-Resource model.

all.title: EMPLOYEE MOTIVATION AND ORGANISATIONAL PERFORMANCE IN AKWA IBOM STATE: A STUDY OF THE AKWA IBOM STATE CIVIL SERVICE
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This study examined employee motivation and organisational performance in the Akwa Ibom State Civil Service, with particular attention to the relationship between remuneration and workers’ productivity, and between promotion opportunities and operational efficiency. The study was informed by the Three-Component Model of Organisational Commitment developed by Meyer and Allen (1991). A descriptive survey research design was adopted. The study population comprised 803 employees drawn from the Ministries of Agriculture, Lands and Education in Akwa Ibom State. A sample size of 260 respondents was determined using the Krejcie and Morgan sample size table, while a multistage sampling technique involving stratified, purposive and simple random sampling procedures was employed. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics and the chi-square test. The findings showed that remuneration package did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with workers’ productivity (χ² = 2.914, df = 18, p = 1.000). Similarly, promotion opportunities did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with operational efficiency (χ² = 8.605, df = 21, p = .992). The study therefore indicates that favourable perceptions of remuneration and promotion practices were not sufficient, on the basis of the tests conducted, to establish statistically significant associations with the respective organisational performance indicators. The study recommended amng others that the Akwa Ibom State Government should strengthen its remuneration administration through regular salary payments, appropriate financial benefits and improved reward systems. It also recommends transparent, timely and merit-based promotion procedures, supported by staff training and effective performance appraisal.

all.title: Career clinics as ethical infrastructures for sustainable organizational culture
all.abstract: Whether organizations' ethical and sustainability commitments carry weight in appraisal, promotion and succession depends on how career decisions are governed. Incorporating ethical criteria into such decisions raises a governance problem: candid reflection on dilemmas and mistakes may be inhibited if disclosures can affect careers, whereas career-consequential criteria require ethical conduct to be assessed. This conceptual article develops Career Clinics, a governance arrangement configuring three components: a recurring, ethics-focused developmental practice protected from individual career assessment; independently evidenced ethical conduct entering at least one promotion or succession rule, directly or through formally linked appraisal; and aggregated, de-identified developmental patterns informing governance of those criteria. Each component has established partial antecedents, including split developmental and evaluative appraisal, ethics-oriented performance appraisal and confidential, primarily developmental professional appraisal with anonymized thematic feedback. A structured, non-exhaustive literature search also identified organizational and professional arrangements combining partial features of two or three components. The configuration is therefore offered as a candidate contribution within the literature reviewed, not as a claim of priority. The theoretical contribution is twofold: the article extends ethical-infrastructure research toward governing career decision criteria, drawing on selective-coupling research, and specifies four defining thresholds, a two-channel architecture separating protected development from independent assessment, propositions specifying enabling conditions, mechanisms and moderators, and failure mechanisms and boundary conditions. Consistently applied criteria are proposed to help sustain ethical practices by aligning stated commitments with the signals sent by who advances. The framework has not been empirically validated; indicators and research designs for testing it are proposed.

all.title: Determinants of Effective Safety Communication and Employee Performance in Hotels in Akure, Ondo State, Nigeria
all.abstract: Effective safety communication is critical to workplace safety and employee performance, yet it remains systematically understudied in Nigeria's hospitality sector, where occupational hazards are prevalent and regulatory oversight is limited. This study examined the factors affecting effective safety communication in hotels in Akure, Ondo State. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, collecting primary data via structured questionnaires from 202 respondents drawn from 10 purposively selected hotels using stratified random sampling. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression analysis was applied to assess the effects of organizational factors, communication channels and technology, employee-related factors, management involvement and support, and training and awareness programs on three dimensions of employee performance. The task efficiency, service quality, and job satisfaction. Findings revealed that training and awareness programs β=0.722 (p<0.001), β=0.465 (p<0.001), β=0.321 (p<0.001) and employee-related factors β=0.328 (p<0.001), β=0.234 (p<0.01), β=0.234 (p<0.01) are the most significant direct determinants of effective safety communication and employee performance. Management involvement and support significantly influence service quality and job satisfaction β=−0.009 (p=0.903), β=0.209 (p<0.05), β=0.345 (p<0.001) but not task efficiency. Communication channels and technology = −0.032 (p=0.456), β=0.073 (p=0.148), β=0.074 (p=0.147), while perceived as useful, do not exert statistically significant direct effects on any performance dimension. The study concludes that safety communication in Akure hotels is moderately developed but not uniformly implemented, and that its effectiveness depends primarily on behavioral and cultural factors employee engagement, management commitment, and continuous training rather than on technological infrastructure alone. Recommendations include redesigning training programs for practical application, strengthening management commitment, institutionalizing two-way feedback mechanisms, and adopting inclusive, multi-channel communication strategies that transcend literacy and language barriers.

all.title: Present but not Supported: Inadequate Supervision for Lived Experience Workers in Australian Mental Health
all.abstract: Lived Experience Workers are increasingly employed in Australian mental health services. Unlike clinical staff, who can access discipline-specific supervision, Lived Experience Workers routinely lack structured support. There is currently limited evidence to understand Australian Lived Experience Workers' supervision experiences. This study seeks to understand Lived Experience workers supervision experiences in Australian mental health settings, examining supervision expectations and requirements, barriers, and consequences of inadequate support. Eighteen semi-structured interviews were conducted with Lived Experience Workers across four Australian states, using a qualitative narrative inquiry framework. Thematic analysis examined experiences across temporality, sociality, and place dimensions. Analysis identified nine themes. Participants articulated that effective supervision should be externally provided, discipline-specific, regularly scheduled, delivered by trained Lived Experience supervisors during protected work time. Current supervision was often undertaken by line managers, causing power imbalances, conflation with performance management, lack of discipline-specific expertise, and positioning as optional rather than essential. When organisations failed to provide supervision, Lived Experience workers self-organised alternatives through unpaid labour, inadvertently legitimising organisational withdrawal from responsibility. Effective supervisors were deeply grounded in Lived Experience values, committed to mutuality and non-hierarchy, and able to "sit in the mud" through non-judgemental presence that protected the distinct integrity of the role. Lived Experience workers possess clear knowledge of supervision requirements and access barriers; the challenge to the delivery of supervision is impacted by political will and resource allocation. Current supervision arrangements perpetuate marginalisation, enable clinical drift, and erode Lived Experience work's distinct epistemology. Discipline-specific supervision is essential to workforce wellbeing, practice integrity, and Lived Experience work's transformative potential. The absence of adequately resourced supervision for Lived Experience workers constitutes systemic inequity.

all.title: Challenges of Annual Performance Evaluation Report (APER) System to Employee Performance in Nigeria's Public Service System
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: This study investigated the challenges of annual performance evaluation report (APER) system to employee performance in Nigeria’s public service system. The specific objectives were to identify APER’s challenges, explore how it undermines suitable job placement, efficiency, proper promotion and retention, and staff competencies and behaviours. Anchored on Expectancy Theory, the study adopted the Ex Post Facto research design utilising qualitative method of data collection based on secondary sources and content analysis. Findings revealed a number of challenges of APER which include, lack of training and resources, subjectivity and lack of transparency, bureaucratic inefficiency, politicisation, unclear performance indicators, weak feedback mechanisms, lack of alignment between appraisals and career progression, its treatment as annual ritual replete with appraisal errors and reliability, validity and rating biases. Further revealed was that APER undermines suitable job placement given a high rate of subjective indices warranting placement of officers at unsuitable positions. More so, APER implementation undermines employees’ efficiency and poor service delivery preceded by poor scrutiny of staff performance and handling jobs with laxity and levity across agencies. Besides, APER undermines proper promotion and retention as there are no stipulated standards to qualify for good conduct, efficient performance and acceptable qualifications for promotion. Ultimately, manipulations of the APER system result in turnover and recycling of incompetent and poor quality public officers. The study recommends that the newly introduced Performance Management System to replace APER should be strictly implemented in accordance with set objectives to avoid the pitfalls of APER. Keywords: APER System, Employee Performance, Public Service, Efficiency, Competence.

all.title: Examination of Organizational Support and Environmental Competition on Transformational Leadership for Intrapreneurial Behaviour for Green Human Resource Management
all.venue: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
all.abstract: In the evolving landscape of sustainable organizational practices, Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) hasemerged as a strategic mechanism to foster both environmental stewardship and organizational effectiveness. By integrating environmentally oriented HR practices—including green recruitment and selection, green training and development, green performance management, and green reward systems—organizations can cultivate employees’ perceptions of strong organizational support. This study examines the influence of organizational support and environmental competition on transformational leadership and their combined effects on intrapreneurial behaviour, with a particular focus on the role of Green Human Resource Management (GHRM) practices. Grounded in leadership and organizational support theories, the study proposes an integrated conceptual framework in which GHRM enhances perceived organizational support, thereby fostering transformational leadership behaviours that stimulate employee intrapreneurship. A quantitative research design was employed using survey data collected from employees across diverse organizational contexts, and the hypothesized relationships were tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The measurement model was validated through Confirmatory Factor Analysis, demonstrating strong reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. The structural model exhibited excellent fit indices, confirming the robustness of the proposed architecture. The results indicate that GHRM practices have a strong positive effect on perceived organizational support (β = 0.61, p < 0.001), which significantly enhances transformational leadership behaviours (β = 0.58, p < 0.001). Environmental competition also positively influences transformational leadership (β = 0.46, p < 0.001), highlighting the role of external pressures in shaping leadership styles. Transformational leadership was found to be the strongest predictor of intrapreneurial behaviour (β = 0.63, p < 0.001), while organizational support also exerted a direct positive effect (β = 0.41, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis revealed significant indirect effects of organizational support (β = 0.37, p < 0.001) and environmental competition (β = 0.29, p < 0.001) on intrapreneurial behaviour through transformational leadership. The model explained 38% of the variance in organizational support, 52% in transformational leadership, and 61% in intrapreneurial behaviour, demonstrating substantial explanatory power. Overall, the findings underscore the critical role of integrating GHRM practices with transformational leadership to stimulate intrapreneurial behaviour and achieve sustainable competitive advantage.

all.title: Proposta de Gerenciamento de Desempenho em Plataformas Offshore de Petróleo e Gás
all.abstract: Work on offshore platforms presents unique challenges to human performance management, requiring special attention to the organizational climate and employee development. The literature lacks studies examining offshore workers' perceptions of performance management and its impacts on the organizational climate and their professional development. In this context, this study analyzed the perceptions of offshore platform workers regarding performance management, focusing on the organizational climate and employee development. The methodology consisted of semi-structured interviews conducted with six workers from an offshore platform, followed by thematic analysis. The results indicate deficiencies in communication and feedback, characterized by a lack of clarity and frequency, as well as the need for greater leadership presence and support for employees. Goals are often unclear and not negotiated, and performance appraisal is perceived as subjective and unfair. Despite the value placed on teamwork, the lack of continuity in work activities and the competitiveness generated by the performance management model hinder collaboration. Isolation, demanding work shifts, and pressure to achieve results negatively affect workers' mental health and well-being. The study proposes a performance management framework structured around the stages of planning, monitoring, and evaluation, with the aim of improving the organizational climate and employee development. It is concluded that performance management on offshore platforms can be enhanced through a more human-centered approach that considers the challenges of the offshore environment and invests in leadership development, communication, feedback, goal setting, and support for workers' mental health.

all.title: OPTIMALISASI PENILAIAN KINERJA BERBASIS KOMPETENSI SEBAGAI STRATEGI PENGEMBANGAN SUMBER DAYA MANUSIA
institutions: Universitas Islam Negeri Sultan Syarif Kasim Riau
all.abstract: Performance appraisal is one of the important functions of human resource management because it serves as a basis for organizations to evaluate work performance, provide feedback, develop competencies, and improve employee performance. This article aims to analyze the development of studies on performance appraisal from a human resource management perspective using a literature review method. The literature reviewed consists of ten studies that examine performance appraisal from various perspectives, including its influence on employee performance, job satisfaction, motivation, career development, appraisal fairness, human resource optimization, digitalization, and the use of decision support systems. The findings indicate that performance appraisal serves not only as an evaluation instrument but is also associated with employee development, motivation, job satisfaction, and organizational decision-making. The effectiveness of performance appraisal is influenced by the clarity of standards, measurement criteria, feedback, fairness in the appraisal process, career development, and the utilization of technology. The review also identifies several challenges, including resistance to digitalization, digital skill gaps, and the need for objective appraisal systems. Therefore, performance appraisal should be developed as a strategic system that is integrated with human resource development and organizational needs.

all.title: Effect of Human Capital Development on Personnel Management in Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Headquarters, Abuja
all.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
all.abstract: The general objective of this study is to assess the Effect of human capital development on personnel management in Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Headquarters, Abuja. The study is anchored on the Human Capital Theory as its theoretical framework while the survey design was adopted as its methodology. Thus, the population of this study is 1015. Taro Yamane (1967) was the technique used in drawing the sample size of 400 for the study. The study found that INEC provides adequate human capital development opportunities that are well-designed and effectively implemented. These programmes have a positive impact on employee job satisfaction and motivation, indicating that INEC's efforts to invest in its human capital are yielding positive results. It was further revealed by this study that employees with higher education levels are better equipped to understand and comply with performance management practices in INEC, ultimately contributing to improved efficiency and effectiveness of the organization's performance management systems. Thus, the study recommends that to maintain and improve upon the positive outcomes of its training and development programmes, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), headquarters in Abuja, should: develop specialized training programmes tailored to the specific needs of each department and employee role. Implement ongoing learning opportunities such as mentorship, workshops, and e-learning platforms. And there is need for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Headquarters, Abuja to prioritize educational development initiatives and implement policies that encourage the continuous educational advancement of its workforce by offering educational support programmes such as tuition reimbursement, scholarships, or study leave for employees seeking to further their education, particularly in areas related to performance management and organizational effectiveness.

all.title: Pengaruh Penilaian Kinerja, Kepuasan Kerja, dan Disiplin Kerja terhadap Produktivitas Kerja Karyawan MyRepublic Cabang Pati
all.venue: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
all.abstract: This study aims to investigate the influence of performance appraisal, job satisfaction, and work discipline on the work productivity of employees at the Pati branch of PT. Eka Mas Mora Republic Tbk (MyRepublic). A quantitative research method was employed. The study population consists of all 70 field marketing employees. Sampling was conducted using a probability sampling method, with the sample size determined by the Slovin formula, resulting in 59 MyRepublic employees as respondents. The t-test results show a t-calculated value (0.029) that is less than the t-table value (2.004), with a significance level of 0.977 (> 0.05); therefore, the hypothesis is rejected, indicating that performance appraisal has no significant partial effect on work productivity—a finding that confirms the first hypothesis. Furthermore, for job satisfaction, the t-calculated value (3.789) is greater than the t-table value (2.004), with a significance level of 0.001 (< 0.05); thus, the hypothesis is accepted, indicating a significant partial effect on work productivity, which confirms the second hypothesis. Similarly, for work discipline, the t-calculated value (8.208) is greater than the t-table value (2.004), with a significance level of 0.001 (< 0.05), demonstrating a significant partial effect on work productivity and confirming the third hypothesis. Furthermore, the fourth hypothesis—regarding the influence of the variables Performance Appraisal, Job Satisfaction, and Work Discipline on Work Productivity—is supported by the research findings. The calculated F-value of 257.261 exceeds the F-table value of 2.77, with a significance level of 0.001 (< 0.05), indicating a significant simultaneous effect. Additionally, the R² value is 0.933, or 93.3%, while the remaining 6.7% is influenced by other factors or variables.

all.title: Künstliche Intelligenz und das Unbewusste in der Organisation. Psychodynamische Perspektiven auf Transformation, Angst und Führung
Addressing the gender pay gap in Australia
all.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Pay disparities between men and women in Australia can be perpetuated by organizational structures. Addressing the pay gap requires efforts to identify and remove barriers to enable more women to be promoted into senior positions, ensure flexible work policies have the intended impact and increase transparency surrounding pay and remuneration. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

all.title: Tutta una questione di Gender Pay Gap?
Unequal Routes, Same Effort: Making Sense of India's Gender Pay Gap
all.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN MANAGEMENT
all.abstract: This review looks at the gender pay gap in India by drawing on studies of how wages are measured, how employment is structured, how sectors and regions differ, how social identity matters, and how equal-remuneration policy works. It keeps apart two ideas that are often merged: the earnings difference across the whole economy and unequal pay for comparable work. Existing studies report large disparities among salaried workers, and the size of the gap shifts with the point in the wage distribution, the type of employment, the location, and the sector. Official data give a snapshot of 2025 earnings, and PLFS 2023–24 evidence points to particularly wide differences among casual workers in rural services. Since the PLFS was redesigned in 2025, the newest figures are used as descriptive benchmarks and not as a directly comparable time series. The review also acknowledges the limits of the evidence it draws on: some survey years are dated, and some papers deal with education or caste-based earnings without estimating gender pay gaps directly. It closes by pointing to priorities for current, intersectional research. Keywords: gender pay gap; India; wage inequality; occupational segregation; labour market; PLFS

all.title: The gender pay gap during conflict: evidence from farm workers in Myanmar
all.abstract: Rising global conflict increasingly destabilizes food systems and labor markets that underpin livelihoods and food security. Conflict-driven shocks—such as male outmigration or shifts toward manual, gendered tasks—can fundamentally reshape the structural inequalities that determine how men and women are compensated. However, quantitative research on gendered agricultural labor markets remains rare, particularly in conflict settings. This paper addresses that gap by providing quantitative analysis of gender wage disparities among hired farm workers amidst conflict. We focus on Myanmar as a highly relevant case study: the country is facing devastating conflict following the military coup in early 2021. We use a unique nationwide primary dataset of 1504 farm workers matched with georeferenced data from the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data. Employing decomposition analysis, we find a 19% gender pay gap driven by structural inequalities rather than individual traits. While wages are lower in highly conflict-affected areas, the gender gap remains stagnant, likely due to offsetting market shocks. This persistent disparity represents a ‘hidden tax’ on female labor that, despite not widening, remains a structural barrier that undermines the efficiency and recovery of agri-food systems in crisis.

all.title: Unifying the Split Field: A Holistic Paradigm and Action-Oriented Framework for the Gender Pay Gap
all.abstract: Background: Despite extensive theoretical and empirical research, the gender wage gap remains a persistent global socioeconomic challenge, often examined through fragmented lenses. Purpose: This review seeks to synthesize seventy-eight academic studies to unify disparate perspectives and propose an action-oriented, holistic framework for future research and policy interventions. Methodology: A comprehensive literature review synthesizing core drivers of gender pay disparities, including human capital, occupational segregation, parenthood penalties, organizational dynamics, and institutional barriers. Key Findings: While individual factors explain part of the disparity, a substantial portion remains “unexplained” by objective qualifications, pointing directly to systemic discrimination, social norms, and stereotype threats. The existing literature predominantly relies on fragmented “molecular” analyses. Implications and Value: To overcome these limitations, we propose an overarching research paradigm that integrates structural, organizational, and individual variables. This action-oriented framework outlines concrete pathways, including standardized organizational interventions, flexible work policies, and targeted skill-building workshops, offering testable propositions for future empirical testing.

all.title: An Examination of Gender Pay Gap (GPG) Reports for Ireland’s Higher Education Sector 2022-2024
all.abstract: This examination primarily explores Gender Pay Gap Reports for the Irish higher education sector, which reveal significant gender pay inequality in favour of men over the first 3-year period of mandatory reporting (2022 through 2024). Given the only marginal annual improvements in pay parity by gender observed, it is projected that at current levels it may take between 9 and 25 years to achieve mean and median pay parity. This is the first time that standardised information on this issue has been available for most employers in Ireland. The process of deriving these figures is then critiqued as they may exclude large numbers of women, often working in low-paid jobs in universities. This suggests that actual pay differentials may be considerably higher than reported. The potential of invoking the Public Sector Duty to include these workers is explored. Proposed explanations for observed gender pay gaps are analysed, and those that lean towards victim-blaming are explored in greater depth. The issue of bullying and toxic cultures in university structures is also explored in-depth.

all.title: Procedural Provisions of the Pay Transparency Directive: A Procedural (R)evolution?
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
all.abstract: The EU Pay Transparency Directive has already generated considerable discussion. Some of its procedural provisions have also attracted criticism. This presentation examines a selection of these procedural provisions, analyses their impact on Belgian law, and assesses whether those concerns are well-founded.

all.title: Asset structural profitability and executive compensation stickiness: evidence from China
Pay Equity, Unionization, and Teacher Performance in Uganda’s Public Education Sector
all.abstract: This study examines how perceived pay equity affects staff performance in low-resource public-service environments. Using an integrated framework of Equity Theory, Herzberg’s Two-Factor Model, and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) Framework, the study evaluates job satisfaction as a mediating psychological bridge, and resource availability and unionization as critical operational and institutional moderators. We analyze survey data from 400 educators across primary, secondary, and tertiary institutions in Uganda using Covariance-Based Structural Equation Modeling (CB-SEM). The findings show that pay equity predicts staff performance directly (β = 0.245, p < 0.001) and indirectly through job satisfaction (β = 0.159, p = 0.001). Resource availability positively moderates the equity-satisfaction relationship (β = 0.235, p < 0.001), whereas unionization shows a weak, non-robust effect (β = 0.086, p = 0.039; 95% BC CI [-0.041, 0.204]). Compensation reforms must align with resource provisioning to optimize service delivery, in line with Equity Theory principles.

all.title: Audit Committee Structure and Executive Compensation of Agricultural Companies in Nigerian Exchange Group
all.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
all.abstract: This study examined the effect of audit committee structure on executive compensation of agricultural companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX). Specifically, the study examined the effect of audit committee size, audit committee independence, and audit committee meeting frequency on executive compensation. The study adopted an ex-post facto research design. The population consisted of five agricultural companies listed on the NGX, and the entire population was used as the sample through the census sampling technique. Secondary data were obtained from the annual reports and financial statements of the selected companies covering the period 2021 to 2025. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and ordinary least squares regression analysis. The regression results revealed that audit committee size had a positive and statistically significant effect on executive compensation. Audit committee independence had a negative and statistically significant effect on executive compensation. However, audit committee meeting frequency had a negative but statistically insignificant effect on executive compensation. The study concluded that audit committee size and independence were significant determinants of executive compensation, whereas meeting frequency had no significant influence. The study recommended maintaining an optimal audit committee size, strengthening committee independence, and improving the effectiveness of audit committee deliberations to promote transparent and accountable executive compensation practices.

all.title: DO CEO AND EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION INFLUENCE BANK PROFITABILITY? COMPARATIVE EVIDENCE FROM ISLAMIC AND CONVENTIONAL BANKS
all.abstract: This study examines the relationship between CEO compensation, executive compensation, and profitability in Pakistani conventional and Islamic banks. Using 156 bank-year observations from 32 banks during 2021–2025, the study employs pooled OLS, random effects, fixed effects, and two-step System GMM estimators. Profitability is measured through ROA, ROE, and NIM. The findings indicate that CEO compensation is positively associated with profitability in conventional banks but negatively associated with profitability in Islamic banks. Conversely, non-CEO executive compensation exhibits consistently negative associations with conventional-bank profitability and predominantly positive associations with Islamic-bank profitability. These findings highlight institutional differences in managerial remuneration and offer implications for bank governance and compensation policies.

all.title: The Core Driving Factors of Indonesian Employee Motivation: Research on Pay Equity, Cultural Fit, And Leadership Collaboration
all.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
institutions: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology
all.abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of three core factors—salary fairness, cultural adaptability, and leadership synergy (transformational leadership)—on the motivation of Indonesian employees. The study used a questionnaire survey method and collected 150 valid questionnaires. The empirical research results show that there is a significant positive correlation between salary fairness and the degree of employee motivation. When employees believe that salary distribution is fair, their work enthusiasm will be significantly improved, which shows that an open and fair salary system is essential to enhance employees' trust and sense of belonging. At the same time, cultural adaptability also has a significant positive impact on employee motivation. The higher the consistency between employees' values and organizational culture, the higher their level of investment in work, which emphasizes the importance of building an inclusive organizational culture in culturally diverse Indonesia. In addition, leadership synergy also has an important impact on employee motivation. Leaders' motivational behaviors, intellectual inspiration for employees, and personal care for employees can effectively stimulate employees' work enthusiasm and improve their job satisfaction.

all.title: Why is Reform Needed Now? Enhancing Executive Compensation Practices in Kuwaiti Public Companies: A Comparative Analytical Study
all.venue: European Journal of Comparative Law and Governance
all.abstract: Contemporary financial markets now address the challenges of excessive executive compensation by allowing shareholders to review and provide input into executive pay packages, with either binding or advisory voting policies. While Kuwait has developed a market aligned with modern markets on many factors, however, it still lacks a strong regulatory mechanism for executive compensation. Yet evidence of Kuwait’s ability to implement effective market changes and have investors retain faith in the market—with new regulations in the last decade and a half—suggests that Kuwait’s market may be ready for enhanced executive compensation regulations. A comparative analysis of foreign market regulations on executive compensation demonstrates that a new amendment to Kuwait’s corporate governance laws allowing shareholders in Kuwait to offer input on executive pay, would enhance the overall health of the market.

all.title: THE IMPACT OF PAY TRANSPARENCY ON EMPLOYEE VOICE BEHAVIOR: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF PSYCHOLOGICAL CONTRACT FULFILMENT AND THE MODERATING ROLE OF PERCEIVED DISTRIBUTIVE JUSTICE
all.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: Sidra,Salman Siraj,Dr. Muhammad Arshad Haroon,Dr. Mahnoor Afzal

all.title: Corporate Biodiversity Governance and Firm Environmental Performance: The Roles of Biodiversity Disclosure, CSR-Linked Executive Compensation, and Environmental Innovation
all.venue: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
all.abstract: Whether corporate environmental performance reflects what firms disclose, how executives are rewarded or the capabilities firms build remains an open empirical question. Drawing on stakeholder theory, this study examines the joint association of biodiversity disclosure (an information mechanism), CSR-linked executive compensation (an incentive mechanism) and environmental innovation (a capability mechanism) with the environmental pillar score of 664 firms from 20 countries and economies over 2015–2025. Pooled, random-effects and firm fixed-effects estimates show positive associations for all three variables. Within firms, biodiversity disclosure is associated with a 5.743-point higher score and CSR-linked compensation with a 2.781-point higher score, while a one-standard-deviation increase in environmental innovation corresponds to a 14.0-point higher score (0.60 standard deviations). Innovation is the most robust association, remaining stable when year effects are introduced, whereas the disclosure and compensation associations are sensitive to common time trends. All estimates are conditional associations. The findings imply that boards and investors should give weight to innovation capability and complement disclosure and pay-linkage practices with measurable targets and verification, while regulators should specify the content and quality of biodiversity disclosure. all.title: Religiosity and relative CEO compensation
institutions: The University of Texas at El Paso
all.abstract: This paper examines the association between local religiosity and executive compensation tournament structures. Firms headquartered in more religious communities have lower CEO compensation relative to non-CEO executives, which suggests a more equitable distribution among top executives. Additional analyses show that the documented association is stronger in long-term, incentive-based compensation and extends to minority religious groups. Overall, our paper suggests that social norms, particularly religiosity, are associated with corporate governance practices around pay equity.

all.title: Gender Parity Practices and Operational Performance in Kenya’s Alcoholic Beverage Industry
all.venue: American Journal of Business and Strategic Management
all.abstract: Aim: This study examined the influence of gender parity practices on the operational performance of the alcoholic beverage industry in Kenya. Methods: The study adopted a positivist paradigm and a correlational survey design. A sample of 393 respondents, drawn from a target population of 3,319 directors, managers, and employees across 50 registered alcoholic beverage firms, was selected using multi-stage sampling. Data were collected via structured questionnaires. A pilot study (N=40) confirmed the instrument’s reliability with a Cronbach’s Alpha of 0.89 for the gender parity construct. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression in SPSS v.30. Results: The findings revealed a statistically significant positive relationship between gender parity practices and operational performance, with the five constructs collectively explaining 28.4% of the variance (R² = 0.284, F = 99.68, p < 0.001). Social and economic equity (β = 0.129, p < 0.001) emerged as the strongest predictor, followed by gender-sensitive leadership (β = 0.118, p < 0.001), gender-balanced employment (β = 0.106, p < 0.01), equitable workplace participation (β = 0.092, p < 0.05), and sexual harassment policies (β = 0.079, p < 0.05). Descriptive statistics showed moderate overall implementation (Mean = 3.45), but highlighted a critical gap between high scores for workforce diversity (M=4.10) and low scores for unbiased salary increments (M=2.95). Conclusion: The study concludes that gender parity serves as a vital strategic driver of operational performance within Kenya’s alcoholic beverage industry, extending well beyond basic regulatory compliance. Recommendations: The study recommends that firms implement mandatory annual pay equity audits, link executive compensation to gender balance targets, and establish safe, anonymous harassment reporting channels. Future research should consider longitudinal designs to track the long-term impact of these interventions.

all.title: ESG-based pay, corporate sustainability performance and moderating impact of institutions: insights from top global companies
all.abstract: Purpose The study aims to investigate the association between ESG-based pay and corporate sustainability performance (CSP) and how institutions moderate the relationship. The authors focus on formal (legal system and country institutional quality) and informal (i.e. cultural environment) institutions. Design/methodology/approach Using a panel research design, the authors analyse a sample of the world’s 500 largest companies. Given the panel structure of the data, the authors use firm and year fixed-effects ordinary least squares (OLS) regressions to control for unobserved, time-invariant firm characteristics and common year-specific effects. We further conduct interaction analyses to examine the moderating effects of the variables of interest. To assess the robustness of our findings and address potential differences in observable characteristics between treatment and comparison groups, the authors conduct additional robustness tests using propensity score matching (PSM) and entropy balancing. Findings Results show that ESG-based pay is positively associated with CSP. However, the legal system moderates this relationship, with the positive effect being weaker in common law countries, where firms generally exhibit higher CSP levels. Institutional quality also moderates the relationship, as stronger institutional environments reduce reliance on ESG-linked executive compensation to drive sustainability outcomes. Furthermore, cultural context shapes the effectiveness of ESG-based pay, with some cultural dimensions substituting for and others reinforcing, executive incentive mechanisms. The findings remain robust to alternative sample specifications and tests addressing endogeneity and selection bias. Practical implications The findings offer important practical implications for policymakers and corporate decision-makers. ESG-based executive compensation can be an effective governance mechanism for enhancing CSP. However, its effectiveness depends on the broader institutional and cultural context. Originality/value The authors contribute to knowledge by addressing a gap in the literature on the role of institutions in ESG-based pay and sustainability performance. By exposing the role of formal and informal institutions in shaping the effectiveness of executive compensation packages to achieve sustainability targets, the authors draw attention of stakeholders to the need to consider institutional environments when designing executive compensation packages within the context of CSP.

all.title: Employee Motivation and Performance of Bank of Kigali Rwanda
all.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education
all.abstract: The study aimed to examine how employee motivation influences the performance of Bank of Kigali Rwanda.To achieve this purpose, attention was given to four specific dimensions of motivation: employee job autonomy, employee compensation, employee growth prospects, and employee recognition and welfare, with each dimension assessed in relation to organizational performance.The study was guided by Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs Theory, and McGregor's Theory X and Theory Y.A descriptive and correlational research design was applied to 129 employees at Bank of Kigali Headquarters, and all 129 respondents participated, yielding a 100% response rate.Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and multiple regression.Employee job autonomy had a significant positive effect on performance (B = 0.185, β = 0.216, p = 0.016), employee growth prospects produced the strongest significant effect (B = 0.444, β = 0.407, p = 0.000), and employee recognition and welfare was also significant (B = 0.548, β = 0.299, p = 0.001).Employee compensation was positive but marginal at the 5% level (B = 0.192, β = 0.171, p = 0.051).The model explained 31.9% of the variation in Bank of Kigali performance (R² = 0.319).The study concluded that autonomy, growth opportunities, and recognition and welfare were important motivational drivers of performance and recommended strengthening delegated decision-making, competitive compensation practices, structured career development, and formal recognition and employee welfare programs.

all.title: ESG disclosure, capital intensity, and corporate financial distress: the role of sustainability governance and executive incentives
all.abstract: This study examines the joint effects of ESG disclosure and capital intensity on corporate financial distress and investigates whether sustainability governance verification (SGV) and ESG-linked executive compensation moderate these relationships. Using panel data from 568 firms across 40 countries over 2015–2024, obtained from the Bloomberg–DataStream database, the study employs firm fixed effects, year fixed effects, and firm-clustered standard errors as the primary estimation approach. Corporate financial distress is measured using the Altman Z-score, with higher values indicating stronger financial health and lower financial distress. Robustness is assessed using two-step system GMM, an alternative financial distress measure, disaggregated ESG dimensions, and subsample analyses based on industry and governance characteristics. The results show that capital intensity is negatively associated with the Altman Z-score, whereas ESG disclosure has no significant direct association with financial distress. However, the ESG × capital intensity interaction is positive and statistically significant, indicating that higher ESG disclosure attenuates the negative association between capital intensity and the Altman Z-score. Subsample analyses provide preliminary evidence that this moderating relationship is more evident among firms with sustainability governance verification and those incorporating climate-related or broader ESG objectives into executive compensation arrangements. The system GMM results confirm the positive and significant interaction, although the direct effect of capital intensity becomes statistically insignificant.
